7iYjk3ELmx.evidence: A universal approximation theorem for continuous equivariant operators and numerical experiments on PDE systems with different symmetry groups, including Allen-Cahn on the sphere, non-rotating spherical shallow water and thermoelasticity on an annulus.
7iYjk3ELmx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is a clean, general extension of equivariance to the whole DeepONet factorization, with compatibility conditions and an equivariance proof, tested on several symmetry settings.
7iYjk3ELmx.main_concern: The comparisons may be unfair, since baselines look under-trained and the vanilla DeepONet sees sparse sensors while the equivariant model sees the full field, and no ablation isolates the equivariance constraint.

BcWPSJhheQ.one_liner: Blueprint for wallpaper-group-equivariant message passing on small graphs defined relative to a periodic substrate, splitting point-group and lattice-translation symmetry.
BcWPSJhheQ.problem: Equivariant GNNs target continuous Euclidean groups such as E(3), but graphs defined relative to a periodic structure have wallpaper-group symmetry, and representing the whole periodic system as a large graph is costly.
BcWPSJhheQ.method: The model represents only the small graph of interest and incorporates the surrounding periodic structure's symmetry by separating point-group equivariance from lattice-relative translational symmetry; reviewers cite Wyckoff-anchor encodings with anchor displacements and member labels.
BcWPSJhheQ.key_idea: Split wallpaper-group symmetry into point-group equivariance and lattice-relative translation, encoding the substrate through symmetry-aware anchor features instead of explicit periodic graph nodes.
BcWPSJhheQ.evidence: Experiments covering all 17 wallpaper groups and a molecular adsorption problem on a periodic graphene substrate, plus a theorem on equivariance (Theorem 1, per reviewers).
BcWPSJhheQ.claimed_gains: High accuracy at a fraction of the cost of full-system message passing; no numbers are stated.
BcWPSJhheQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the formulation is well motivated and technically strong, with convincing experiments covering all 17 wallpaper groups and a graphene application.
BcWPSJhheQ.main_concern: The presentation is hard to follow, with dense definitions in Section 3, no overview figure, and key visualizations deferred to the appendix.

5YWfCcvclm.one_liner: Diffusion watermark whose pattern derives from a content code of the predicted clean image mid-denoising, binding watermark to content.
5YWfCcvclm.problem: Diffusion watermarking work focuses on distortion and removal attacks, but forgery attacks can transfer valid watermark evidence to content the system did not generate.
5YWfCcvclm.method: At a late denoising step, TrajBind extracts a compact content code from the model's predicted clean image and combines it with a secret key to set the watermark pattern embedded during the remaining steps; verification needs only the received image. It adds a general forgery formulation and a bound on detection-level forgery success in terms of content-code collision.
5YWfCcvclm.key_idea: Derive the watermark pattern from a keyed code of the predicted clean image at a late denoising step, so the watermark depends on content.
5YWfCcvclm.evidence: Five existing forgery attacks against 12 baseline watermarking methods, with robustness to benign transformations and removal attacks, collision statistics, component ablations, and a theoretical bound on detection-level forgery success.
5YWfCcvclm.claimed_gains: Lower worst-case forgery success than each of the 12 baseline watermarking methods across five existing forgery attacks, while keeping robust detection and message recovery under benign transformations and removal attacks; no forgery rates are stated.
5YWfCcvclm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deriving a content-specific pattern within the same generation trajectory, without a separate model or extra generation, is a useful design with lower worst-case forgery success than the baselines.
5YWfCcvclm.main_concern: The security evidence is incomplete, with no adaptive attacker targeting code collisions or forging via similar-layout donors or content edits, and fidelity and runtime costs are not fully reported.

2zNMbonNRe.one_liner: Trains a 4B SQL autocomplete model with context-grounded SFT targets, silence labels, and gate-first RL rewards before an LLM-judge reward.
2zNMbonNRe.problem: Completions recorded in editing logs often depend on information absent at the cursor, creating a supervision mismatch for SQL autocomplete and a need for calibrated silence.
2zNMbonNRe.method: Each SFT target is trimmed to its longest inferable prefix, with empty targets kept as silence labels; RL then applies deterministic abstention and grounding gates before a graded LLM-judge reward. A selective evaluation framework reconstructed from real editing sessions jointly measures suggestion quality and firing-abstention behavior.
2zNMbonNRe.key_idea: Trim SFT targets to the longest prefix inferable at the cursor and apply deterministic abstention and grounding gates before the LLM-judge reward in RL.
2zNMbonNRe.evidence: Controlled comparisons of grounded versus raw targets, an RL comparison against a judge-only reward, an offline selective evaluation built from real editing sessions, and matched seven-day deployment windows against a prior 30B system.
2zNMbonNRe.claimed_gains: Context grounding raises precision by nearly 13 percentage points; gated RL raises pass@1 on predictable triggers from 35.8% to 43.4%; the TL;DR states a 4B model beats a 30B MoE in precision, acceptance and latency.
2zNMbonNRe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the distinction between inferable completions and eventual user edits is important and well operationalized, with clear writing and live-deployment gains in quality and latency.
2zNMbonNRe.main_concern: The training-reference pipeline and offline evaluator share one model, risking correlated bias, and the 4B-versus-30B deployment comparison is confounded by differing training data.

5VLf3zfFJe.one_liner: Online loop: pretrained generative models flag policy failures, imagine corrected rollout continuations, and the policy is fine-tuned on them.
5VLf3zfFJe.problem: Reward-based RL can require costly exploration to discover better behaviors in open-world environments with sparse rewards.
5VLf3zfFJe.method: Given a policy rollout, ReVision identifies failures and uses pretrained generative models to generate counterfactual continuations that correct them; the policy is fine-tuned on the corrected rollouts and redeployed to collect new experience, repeating online. Reviewers describe a VLM judging rollouts, a corrector interacting with a world model, and a scorer filtering trajectories.
5VLf3zfFJe.key_idea: Repeatedly apply pretrained generative priors to the current learner's own failures, generating counterfactual corrections to fine-tune on, rather than distilling fixed teacher demonstrations.
5VLf3zfFJe.evidence: Minecraft ObtainDiamond with behavior-cloned and vision-language-action policies, controlled comparisons against teacher distillation and correcting a frozen learner, PPO and Dreamer baselines (per reviewers), and RLBench manipulation tasks.
5VLf3zfFJe.claimed_gains: Returns comparable to PPO using 5 times fewer online environment steps (6M versus 30M) on Minecraft ObtainDiamond, plus improvements on RLBench manipulation policies.
5VLf3zfFJe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-loop design is well constructed and practical, with fair comparisons, error bars and ablations, and that targeting the learner's own failures is a sound route to sample-efficient improvement.
5VLf3zfFJe.main_concern: Gains may come from the strong off-the-shelf VLM and world model assumed rather than the algorithm, with no DAgger-style baseline, no real-robot test and no full cost accounting.

bcLdVcBKJG.one_liner: Separates what an LLM user simulator must accomplish from how it pursues goals to keep simulated interactions task-faithful and human-plausible.
bcLdVcBKJG.problem: Task success from LLM user simulators is informative only if the simulated interaction is valid, but simulators can drift from the assigned task or behave in ways extreme relative to real users.
bcLdVcBKJG.method: The paper audits Task Fidelity (TF) and Human Plausibility (HP) across 30 user LLMs, finds persona prompting raises HP at the expense of TF, and proposes a method that separates what the simulator needs to accomplish from how it pursues those goals (called TPS, with a goal tracker, per reviewers).
bcLdVcBKJG.key_idea: Separate a goal tracker, which fixes what the simulator must accomplish, from the generator that decides how to phrase each turn.
bcLdVcBKJG.evidence: An audit of 30 user LLMs plus agent evaluation with multiple agent models and baselines, ablations, agent-ranking consistency and agreement with external evaluations.
bcLdVcBKJG.claimed_gains: 34.1% of successful interactions contain HP violations and 45.9% of failures contain TF violations; the method turns average TF loss into a gain (-6.4 to +0.6 pp) and improves HP by +6.1 pp across 30 user LLMs.
bcLdVcBKJG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating task fidelity from human plausibility is a well-posed, intuitive idea, supported by extensive evaluation across 30 user LLMs and effects on agent rankings.
bcLdVcBKJG.main_concern: HP rests on a few statistical indicators such as response length and repetition, and the claim that the method is more human-like than persona-plus-task prompting is under-supported, since a goal tracker or persona alone gets most of the gain.

skI2EL3PZ1.one_liner: Camera-controlled long-video generation from one image using warp-and-inpaint generation plus a second denoiser conditioned on subsampled long-range history.
skI2EL3PZ1.problem: Autoregressive camera-controlled video generation drifts as frames condition on generated outputs, and explicit 6-DOF pose conditioning or self-forcing costs compute or yields inconsistent scene scale.
skI2EL3PZ1.method: Two models, WanAR and FixAR, built on online reconstruction and hierarchical denoising: generation is reformulated as warping and inpainting for camera-scale consistency, frames are first generated from the immediate past, then refined by a second denoiser conditioned on a temporally subsampled long-range history.
skI2EL3PZ1.key_idea: Generate frames from the immediate past, then refine them with a denoiser conditioned on a temporally subsampled long-range history, giving each frame access to full context cheaply.
skI2EL3PZ1.evidence: Experiments on RealEstate10k and DL3DV, with eight baselines per reviewers (the abstract is truncated).
skI2EL3PZ1.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is truncated before the results)
skI2EL3PZ1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework is practical and well motivated, combining warping and inpainting with hierarchical temporal refinement, and gives competitive results on RealEstate10K and DL3DV.
skI2EL3PZ1.main_concern: Camera-pose adherence is not measured directly and the role of ground-truth geometry at inference is unclear, which makes the single-image claim and baseline fairness hard to assess.

6u5kT1Kl0o.one_liner: Proves deep ReLU networks need width exactly k to universally approximate maps from [0,1]^d to R^k when k >= 2d+2.
6u5kT1Kl0o.problem: The exact minimum width for universal approximation by deep ReLU networks is known only in a few cases, leaving a one-neuron gap between bounds.
6u5kT1Kl0o.method: The proof builds on a diffeomorphism approach that splits minimum width into a geometric quantity w(d,k) and extra width for approximating diffeomorphisms. One extra neuron suffices for continuous nonaffine activations with a nonzero derivative somewhere, and for ReLU it is removed when k >= 2d+2 by approximating only on the lower-dimensional image of [0,1]^d.
6u5kT1Kl0o.key_idea: Approximate only on the lower-dimensional image of the input cube, where ReLU's extra neuron for full-dimensional diffeomorphisms is unnecessary.
6u5kT1Kl0o.evidence: Theoretical proofs only: matching bounds for k >= 2d+2, a general upper bound w(d,k)+1, and a construction at k=2d+1 where the geometric argument fails; no experiments.
6u5kT1Kl0o.claimed_gains: Exact minimum width k whenever k >= 2d+2, improving the previous upper bound by one, and the same for GELU, SiLU, Softplus and other ReLU-approximating activations; for k <= 2d+1 the width is w(d,k) or w(d,k)+1.
6u5kT1Kl0o.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a rigorous, exact result on a fundamental expressivity question that closes an infinite family of minimum-width cases.
6u5kT1Kl0o.main_concern: The result is a pure expressivity statement for the unusual regime k >= 2d+2, leans on external factorization theorems, and has limited practical implication, with some related work uncited.

Fj2fkh1Ys8.one_liner: Model-based RL objective replacing pixel reconstruction with an adversarial term enforcing reward and next-latent sufficiency, yielding bisimulation-based latents.
Fj2fkh1Ys8.problem: Reconstruction-based model-based RL objectives waste representational capacity on task-irrelevant distractors.
Fj2fkh1Ys8.method: VIBES replaces pixel reconstruction with an adversarial term requiring latent states to suffice for predicting rewards and the next latent state, combined with a fixed-capacity latent bottleneck. It drops into Dreamer's model-learning component and is shown to induce bisimulation relations on histories whenever exact sufficiency is attainable.
Fj2fkh1Ys8.key_idea: Train the encoder adversarially so latents are sufficient to predict rewards and next latents, with a fixed-capacity bottleneck discarding the rest.
Fj2fkh1Ys8.evidence: Distracting Control Suite, Realistic ManiSkill and a 100-link swimmer robot, against Dreamer variants, DreamerV3, HRSSM and RePo, with latent-space analyses (UMAP and nearest-neighbor probes).
Fj2fkh1Ys8.claimed_gains: Claims top results on the Distracting Control Suite (best per-task mean on four of six tasks, per reviewers), plus Realistic ManiSkill and a 100-link swimmer; the abstract gives no scores.
Fj2fkh1Ys8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that removing pixel reconstruction is well motivated for distractor-heavy control and that Distracting Control Suite results are strong, supported by ablations and representation analyses.
Fj2fkh1Ys8.main_concern: The main theorem's conclusion requires joint realizability of reward and dynamics sufficiency, which is not established, and bisimulation conditions alone do not guarantee that distractors are discarded.

EUrRozfeCg.one_liner: GPU neural evaluators predict Lean verdicts and compiler feedback to build hybrid GRPO rewards that cut theorem-prover training time.
EUrRozfeCg.problem: Training theorem-proving language models needs many slow Lean verifier calls, which leave GPUs waiting and withhold rewards from potentially correct proofs when checks time out.
EUrRozfeCg.method: Neural evaluators are trained on 4.84M labelled programs: validity classifiers and a feedback model that predicts goal states and error messages, in a two-stage cascade where a classifier screens candidates and the feedback model scores its positives. Speculative decoding speeds feedback generation, and predicted verdicts are combined with Lean verdicts in a hybrid GRPO reward.
EUrRozfeCg.key_idea: Screen proof candidates with a classifier, score positives with a feedback model, and mix these predicted verdicts with Lean verdicts as the RL reward.
EUrRozfeCg.evidence: A 68,932-program benchmark of public-prover outputs, throughput measurements on one H100 against a 64-worker Lean baseline, and one-epoch GRPO training with hybrid versus Lean-only rewards evaluated on miniF2F.
EUrRozfeCg.claimed_gains: 87.8% accuracy predicting Lean acceptance; 3.5 candidates per second on one H100, 4.2x a 64-worker Lean baseline; GRPO steps about 31% shorter, with miniF2F pass@1 of 62.2% versus 62.4% and pass@32 of 72.4% versus 71.3%.
EUrRozfeCg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a concrete bottleneck in RL for formal theorem proving and credit its end-to-end evaluation of the hybrid reward in actual prover training, plus a useful 4.84M-program corpus.
EUrRozfeCg.main_concern: Methodological novelty is limited and components are not isolated, since GRPO uses only binary validity predictions with no classifier-only hybrid compared, and training results come from one checkpoint per reward condition.

icRw5ZcUxW.one_liner: Studies how short-horizon training rewards diverge from long-horizon outcomes using delayed code corrections from merged pull requests.
icRw5ZcUxW.problem: Post-training rewards are computed over short horizons, but the consequences of a code change can appear days or months later, so rewards may not reflect long-horizon objectives.
icRw5ZcUxW.method: The authors use code corrections as delayed feedback, compare the signals available at short and long horizons, and analyze how critic models trained on long-horizon outcomes may distill some delayed feedback into short-horizon rewards.
icRw5ZcUxW.key_idea: Link later corrections to earlier merged changes to build long-horizon labels, then compare critics trained on short- versus long-window outcomes.
icRw5ZcUxW.evidence: A dataset of 257,788 merged pull requests across 11 open-source repositories with a one-year follow-up window and a chronological split with a 365-day gap (per reviewers), plus critics trained on different horizons.
icRw5ZcUxW.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports only that short- and long-horizon signals differ substantially.
icRw5ZcUxW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the dataset gives a concrete, traceable way to study delayed feedback, with a transparent protocol (one-year maturation, chronological split with a 365-day gap) across 11 repositories.
icRw5ZcUxW.main_concern: Predicting corrections is not shown to give a better reward for code generation, since task and repository differences can drive prediction, and no policy ranking or real code-quality validation is provided.

L8JD2F8NiG.one_liner: Shows LLM correction loops fix exposed failing checks far more often than hidden ones, causing false completion under partial verification.
L8JD2F8NiG.problem: Correction loops stop when their checks pass, but checks rarely cover every way an output can be wrong, so accepted outputs may keep defects the checks missed.
L8JD2F8NiG.method: A correction loop runs on three task domains (music-as-code audio, SVG repair, API workflows) with eight models; each task has eight deterministic checks, all scored every round but only some exposed to the model, and the loop stops when the exposed checks pass, so hidden defects can be counted.
L8JD2F8NiG.key_idea: Score all eight checks every round but expose only some to the model, so repaired and remaining hidden defects can be counted.
L8JD2F8NiG.evidence: Three task domains with eight proprietary and open-weight models, eight deterministic checks per task, fixed-horizon and matched-continuation controls, and reasoning and self-chosen-check experiments.
L8JD2F8NiG.claimed_gains: not stated (the paper reports findings rather than gains: exposed defects are repaired far more often than hidden ones, and extra rounds recover little)
L8JD2F8NiG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled design (shared initial drafts, all checks scored, fixed-horizon controls) gives credible evidence that repair concentrates on reported failures.
L8JD2F8NiG.main_concern: Conceptual novelty is limited because the main results largely quantify expected effects of incomplete verification, and the stopping analysis mixes stopping rules with revision budgets.

1ifRzv1QQE.one_liner: Theory and experiments showing when multi-layer linear attention transformers beat one layer for in-context regression via function-vector routing.
1ifRzv1QQE.problem: It is unclear when stacking many attention-feedforward blocks gives a computational advantage over a single transformer block for in-context learning.
1ifRzv1QQE.method: A theory of distributed inference in generalized linear attention transformers under communication and depth constraints shows layers can use internal function vectors to infer a latent context variable at increasingly finer scales. For in-context linear regression it predicts that one layer suffices for Gaussian priors while multi-layer transformers win for non-Gaussian, tree-like priors, tested with trained models and causal key-patching.
1ifRzv1QQE.key_idea: Internal function vectors in intermediate layers route information adaptively, letting depth infer a latent variable coarse-to-fine when its prior is tree-like.
1ifRzv1QQE.evidence: Theory for in-context linear regression with linear attention, trained linear attention transformers reproducing quantitative predictions, and causal key-patching experiments.
1ifRzv1QQE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is well written, motivated and sound, with experiments that support the theory and an interesting interpretation of the roles of MLPs and attention in adaptive inference.
1ifRzv1QQE.main_concern: The theory and experiments are limited to in-context linear regression with linear attention and a purpose-built routing architecture, with no evidence for softmax transformers or more general settings.

entdQSKDfx.one_liner: Two-headed estimator fitting separate expert and proxy utilities, coupled by a penalty on their difference, to learn from biased preferences.
entdQSKDfx.problem: In specialized domains expert comparisons are scarce while general-population comparisons are plentiful but systematically biased, and pooling the two learns a utility between the populations.
entdQSKDfx.method: THE fits one utility per population with the sign loss from a small gold sample and a large proxy sample, coupling them through a penalty on their difference to estimate the direction of the experts' utility center; re-weighting the pooled samples is its infinite-penalty limit.
entdQSKDfx.key_idea: Fit separate utilities for gold and proxy comparisons and penalize their difference, so finite coupling can beat any scalar re-weighting of pooled data.
entdQSKDfx.evidence: Theorems on estimation error under proxy bias (sign loss, smoothed loss, sparse bias), synthetic experiments with cross-fitted tuning, and real preference data using the Bradley-Terry logistic loss (per reviewers).
entdQSKDfx.claimed_gains: not stated; the theory says proxy comparisons speed up estimation while their bias is below the statistical error of pooling, and a variant of THE has smaller asymptotic error than every re-weighting under stated conditions.
entdQSKDfx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that using abundant biased proxy preferences with scarce gold data is a practical problem and that the theoretical analysis is detailed and clearly formulated.
entdQSKDfx.main_concern: There is a gap between the theory (sign loss, assumed distributions) and practice (Bradley-Terry logistic loss), and practical tuning causes substantial negative transfer under large proxy bias.

AQg5hFhI6b.one_liner: Adds self-attribution, measuring how well a prompt explains its own trajectory versus rivals, to GEPA's parent and child selection.
AQg5hFhI6b.problem: Prompt optimizers select candidates by task accuracy alone, which cannot tell which instruction accounts for a correct response, so equally accurate prompts may differ in solution strategy or merely reword each other.
AQg5hFhI6b.method: Self-attribution measures how much better a candidate's own instruction explains its trajectory than the best competing instruction does, with a proof that it gives a computable lower bound on the information accuracy discards. SAGE adds it to GEPA's choice of parents and of which mutated children are kept, with a proposal recipe aimed at different solution strategies.
AQg5hFhI6b.key_idea: Score each prompt by how much better it explains its own trajectories than the best competing prompt, and use that score in selection alongside accuracy.
AQg5hFhI6b.evidence: Four open-weight models, six benchmarks and four baselines in the main experiments (per reviewers), including Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-30B-A3B and GPT-OSS-120B.
AQg5hFhI6b.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is truncated before the results)
AQg5hFhI6b.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the limitation of accuracy-only selection is real and self-attribution is a clear, simple complementary signal, evaluated at large scale across models and benchmarks.
AQg5hFhI6b.main_concern: Gains are modest and shrink for larger models (about 2.3 on Qwen3-4B and 1.0 on GPT-OSS-120B), the theory is not tied to practical gains, and the change touches only two steps of an existing optimizer.

hQhAZ6H4Vc.one_liner: Tree-based speculative diffusion sampling that ranks draft candidates and samples a rank with TV-optimized weights, keeping exact target law.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.problem: D-GRS tests K conditionally independent draft candidates sequentially in generation order, ignoring an informative ranking available without extra target-model evaluations.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.method: RASS orders draft candidates along the proposal-target mean displacement and samples a rank with weights optimized to minimize total variation between the selected-proposal and target laws. The selected candidate is then maximally coupled with the target, with residual correction keeping sampling exact for any rank weights.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.key_idea: Rank-aware list coupling: order exchangeable draft candidates by proposal-target mean displacement and select a rank with TV-minimizing weights, with residual correction keeping sampling exact.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.evidence: A Gaussian-mixture target, pixel-space CIFAR-10, FFHQ and ImageNet with PixelDiT, and latent text-to-image with Stable Diffusion 3.5 and FLUX.2 on COCO 2014 prompts.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.claimed_gains: Not stated in the visible abstract; a review reports best SD3.5 target-call speedups of 1.152 for RASS versus 1.142 for D-GRS.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the verification rule is mathematically principled, exact for any feasible rank weights, and reduces target-model calls relative to existing speculative baselines.
hQhAZ6H4Vc.main_concern: Target-call savings are not shown to become wall-clock speedups, since timings exclude model execution and uncached rank-weight optimization and cache-hit rates are unreported.

63kjdVZa7H.one_liner: GNN scores transformer computation-graph edges from clean and counterfactual activations, giving circuits in one forward pass.
63kjdVZa7H.problem: Existing circuit discovery methods approximate interventions to first order (attribution patching) or optimize new masks per task (Edge Pruning), so nothing reusable is learned about finding circuits.
63kjdVZa7H.method: A graph neural network runs on the transformer's computation graph, takes clean and counterfactual activations, and assigns a score to each edge; keeping the top-scoring edges gives a circuit at any target sparsity without attribution-derived features or test-time optimization. A scorer is also trained jointly across tasks.
63kjdVZa7H.key_idea: Learn an edge scorer by message passing over the transformer computation graph, conditioned on clean and counterfactual activations, then threshold scores to any sparsity.
63kjdVZa7H.evidence: Per-task and multi-task GNN scorers evaluated on the MIB Benchmark against EAP and EAP-IG, with reviews noting models including GPT-2, Qwen, Gemma and Llama.
63kjdVZa7H.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims per-task scorers outperform EAP and EAP-IG on integrated circuit performance (CPR) on the MIB Benchmark.
63kjdVZa7H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see strong per-task results and a practical way to train circuit scorers without ground-truth circuits, with promising but weaker multi-task results.
63kjdVZa7H.main_concern: Comparisons do not isolate the GNN's contribution (no edge-wise MLP, no scorer without message passing, no directly optimized masks), and multi-task and out-of-distribution results are incomplete and modest.

2Itft5dETc.one_liner: Optimistic FTRL with adaptive learning rates gives scale-free fast convergence to Nash and correlated equilibria without knowing utility scale.
2Itft5dETc.problem: Almost all fast convergence guarantees in learning in games require prior knowledge of the utility scale.
2Itft5dETc.method: Learning dynamics based on optimistic follow-the-regularized-leader with adaptive learning rates. Two-player zero-sum games use a new stopping-time analysis; multiplayer general-sum games combine a hybrid regularizer with clipped utilities based on past observations.
2Itft5dETc.key_idea: Adaptive learning rates exploit negative terms in optimistic FTRL regret bounds, via a stopping-time analysis (zero-sum) and a hybrid regularizer with clipped utilities (general-sum).
2Itft5dETc.evidence: Theoretical regret and convergence-rate analyses for two-player zero-sum and multiplayer general-sum games; no experiments are mentioned in the visible text.
2Itft5dETc.claimed_gains: Zero-sum: external regret of order A_diff giving an A_diff/T rate to Nash; general-sum: swap regret O(U_max sqrt(log T)) giving a U_max sqrt(log T)/T rate to correlated equilibrium, up to log factors.
2Itft5dETc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the scale-free problem meaningful, the zero-sum convergence result interesting, and the definitions, lemmas and theorems clearly written.
2Itft5dETc.main_concern: The dynamics are coupled, with learning rates depending on both players' payoff variation or shared statistics across players, and the communication-free alternative loses scale-freeness.

hxvEda1S5F.one_liner: SCALE fits local-reference residual experts on frozen time-series features to apply minority-directed corrections to a class-balanced anchor.
hxvEda1S5F.problem: With frozen encoders, scarce minority labels may not identify generalizing feature directions, leaving a gap between training and test minority recall under class-balanced readouts.
hxvEda1S5F.method: SCALE builds compact residual coordinates from shared local references and fits complementary experts on observed and modeled support. The experts propose minority-directed corrections to a class-balanced anchor, with training cross-validation selecting the correction rule, using no extra labels or encoder updates.
hxvEda1S5F.key_idea: Correct a class-balanced anchor readout with minority-directed expert outputs computed in residual coordinates relative to shared local references, choosing the rule by cross-validation.
hxvEda1S5F.evidence: 690 univariate encoder-task pairs plus multivariate evaluation, compared with cRT and other readouts; reviews cite 138 tasks from 58 datasets, five representations, a shared 100-trial TPE budget and Holm-corrected statistics.
hxvEda1S5F.claimed_gains: Highest aggregate balanced accuracy, Macro-F1 and Min-F1 across 690 univariate encoder-task pairs; improves on cRT by 2.06 balanced-accuracy and 3.43 Min-F1 percentage points, with positive aggregate multivariate gains over cRT.
hxvEda1S5F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the large, controlled evaluation (same frozen features, splits and tuning budget, dataset-level statistics) and consistent gains over cRT on a practical problem.
hxvEda1S5F.main_concern: Gains are not attributed to local references versus simpler alternatives (global LDA projection, standalone RBF-SVM), and imbalance ratio is confounded with minority count.

hIjDO9q4uH.one_liner: Prunes singular values of the fine-tuning weight delta below the Gavish-Donoho threshold to repair forgetting without data or training.
hIjDO9q4uH.problem: Fine-tuning degrades capabilities the task data never threatened, low-rank methods forfeit incidental gains, and recovery usually needs original training data that practitioners rarely have.
hIjDO9q4uH.method: DG-Hard takes the SVD of each weight-delta matrix between the base and fine-tuned checkpoints, keeps singular values above the closed-form Gavish-Donoho hard threshold (task-aligned spikes), and reverts the Marchenko-Pastur-like bulk. The paper also introduces a partition-conditional metric tracking healing, preservation, non-damage and target-task retention.
hIjDO9q4uH.key_idea: A fine-tuning update splits into task-aligned singular-value spikes and a Marchenko-Pastur noise bulk; keeping spikes above the closed-form hard threshold and reverting the bulk repairs forgetting.
hIjDO9q4uH.evidence: Reviews cite 14 model-task combinations (two language models, seven fine-tuning tasks), comparisons with spectral truncation variants, V-SoftMask and FAPM, and synthetic experiments in Appendix M.
hIjDO9q4uH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a simple, data-free, hyperparameter-free method that needs only two checkpoints and gives a good recovery-preservation tradeoff.
hIjDO9q4uH.main_concern: Novelty is limited (truncated SVD of task vectors and the Gavish-Donoho threshold are reused), results are not best on every metric, and model and fine-tuning conditions are narrow.

M1ag2tCmQo.one_liner: All-atom flow map for crystal structure prediction and generation with few-step sampling, plus Reinforce Adjoint Matching post-training.
M1ag2tCmQo.problem: State-of-the-art flow and diffusion models for materials are bottlenecked by the inference cost of proposing candidate materials.
M1ag2tCmQo.method: OMatG-flash is an all-atom flow map for crystal structure prediction (CSP) and de novo generation (DNG) that samples with far fewer steps; reviews note it reuses Crystalite's backbone. Reinforce Adjoint Matching (RAM) is applied to the flow map for post-training fine-tuning on CSP.
M1ag2tCmQo.key_idea: Replace multi-step flow/diffusion sampling with a flow map that generates crystals in few steps, then fine-tune it with Reinforce Adjoint Matching on the flow map's velocity.
M1ag2tCmQo.evidence: CSP and DNG benchmarks (reviews cite MP-20 and MP-20-ps) against Crystalite and MCFlow, with MACE relaxations used to compute RAM rewards.
M1ag2tCmQo.claimed_gains: An order of magnitude fewer inference steps and less wall-clock time than existing flow and diffusion models at benchmark performance on par with the state of the art; RAM further improves CSP (no numbers stated).
M1ag2tCmQo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives a competitive quality-speed trade-off with far fewer model calls, under a Pareto-optimality claim that is honestly scoped.
M1ag2tCmQo.main_concern: Geometric accuracy lags baselines (RMSE 0.1172 versus 0.0592 for MCFlow on MP-20), the RAM post-training is not ablated, and novelty beyond combining existing parts is limited.

9xIhJWqfbr.one_liner: Context compaction for coding agents that only truncates or drops content, never rewrites or re-compacts, without LLM summarization.
9xIhJWqfbr.problem: Long-horizon agents need millions of tokens of context, forcing compaction within limited windows, where rewriting causes context drift and edits can invalidate caches.
9xIhJWqfbr.method: CliffCompaction truncates or drops content verbatim and never re-compacts an existing compaction. It is implemented as a scaffold-agnostic API proxy usable with Claude Code, Codex and other harnesses, with per-rollout savings reinvested in test-time scaling.
9xIhJWqfbr.key_idea: Preserve context fidelity by only truncating or dropping content, never rewriting it, and never compacting an existing compaction, which prevents context drift.
9xIhJWqfbr.evidence: Terminal-Bench (2.0 and 2.1) across scaffolds and model families, and KernelBench sessions over a million tokens, against sliding-window, summarization and microcompaction baselines.
9xIhJWqfbr.claimed_gains: Up to 50% cost reduction on Terminal-Bench at equal or better performance; over 10 points gained via test-time scaling for under the cost of two full-context runs; KernelBench CUDA speedups of 2.23x at 200 steps and 3.58x at 400.
9xIhJWqfbr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers see a simple, training-free, deployable method that works through an API proxy across scaffolds and models and stays near full-context performance.
9xIhJWqfbr.main_concern: Core design choices (verbatim retention, dropping prior compactions, truncation rules) are not ablated, and headline gains lack statistical support, e.g. a selector trained and evaluated on the same 89 Terminal-Bench 2.0 tasks.

9yHbh2vv4q.one_liner: Derives optimality constraints on dictionary-learning features from identifiability results to explain SAE splitting, absorption and other oddities.
9yHbh2vv4q.problem: It is unclear whether odd sparse autoencoder behavior reflects the network's representations or distortion imposed by the SAE objective.
9yHbh2vv4q.method: Uses dictionary-learning identifiability results to derive constraints that optimal features must satisfy, such as an optimal feature never turning on only while another is active. The constraints explain hierarchical splitting and absorption, residual features, dense antipodal features and infinite feature splitting, and serve as diagnostics on real SAEs.
9yHbh2vv4q.key_idea: Optimal dictionary-learning solutions must satisfy identifiability-derived feature and residual constraints, so SAE oddities follow from the objective itself rather than network structure.
9yHbh2vv4q.evidence: Theoretical derivations with empirical examples; real SAEs pass the constraint diagnostics on their training dataset but increasingly fail on more distant test datasets.
9yHbh2vv4q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it gives a clean, unifying theoretical framework that explains several SAE oddities from first principles and is clearly written.
9yHbh2vv4q.main_concern: Results are derived for vanilla (L1) dictionary learning assuming optimal codes and no optimization gap, so they may not carry to TopK or JumpReLU SAEs with trained encoders, and some insights overlap prior work.

KVS1GOjkcu.one_liner: Information-flow control for browser agents: gates click, type and navigate actions on labels propagated from element-level HTML annotations.
KVS1GOjkcu.problem: LLM browser agents are exposed to prompt injection and data exfiltration, and restoring the Same-Origin Policy is neither sufficient nor necessary to protect users.
KVS1GOjkcu.method: SPIDES propagates confidentiality and integrity labels from element-level HTML annotations, masks untrusted and confidential content from the agent's context, and blocks unauthorized flows by gating primitive browser actions. The authors build MicroNet, 28 interlinked websites with element-level ground-truth labels and paired benign and adversarial tasks.
KVS1GOjkcu.key_idea: Enforce information-flow policies outside the LLM by gating primitive browser actions on confidentiality and integrity labels propagated from element-level HTML annotations.
KVS1GOjkcu.evidence: Evaluation on the authors' MicroNet benchmark against baseline defenses under a common threat model, including UCM and SOPGuard per the reviews.
KVS1GOjkcu.claimed_gains: 0% attack success rate by design while retaining high task completion rate and autonomy; no other figures visible in the abstract.
KVS1GOjkcu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the information-flow approach principled, independent of the underlying model, more flexible than same-origin restrictions, and low in utility cost.
KVS1GOjkcu.main_concern: The guarantee depends on accurate element-level labels from website operators, which is untested since all MicroNet labels are ground truth, and evaluation uses only the authors' own benchmark.

o1zN398IHm.one_liner: Learnable E(3)-equivariant generalization of the Fast Multipole Method adding multiscale long-range interactions to short-range EGNNs at O(N) cost.
o1zN398IHm.problem: Finite cutoffs truncate long-range information in equivariant GNN potentials, and existing long-range extensions use fixed kernels, restrict communication to scalars or degree-preserving channels, or scale super-linearly.
o1zN398IHm.method: NEMORA treats equivariant message passing as a learnable multipole expansion and generalizes the FMM's analytical expansion and translation operators to learned equivariant operators. These transport the backbone's hidden tensor features through an adaptive spatial hierarchy, coupling angular degrees while keeping analytical radial factors.
o1zN398IHm.key_idea: Equivariant message passing as a learnable multipole expansion: learned equivariant expansion and translation operators move tensor features through an adaptive hierarchy, keeping FMM's analytical radial factors.
o1zN398IHm.evidence: Benchmarks including MD22, held-out cumulene lengths, comparisons across four baseline backbones, and a scaling plot supporting O(N) time; the abstract is truncated before further results.
o1zN398IHm.claimed_gains: No accuracy numbers stated in the visible abstract; it claims O(N) computational cost for long-range interactions.
o1zN398IHm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the equivariant-features-plus-FMM-hierarchy design is promising, improves over local models across datasets and backbones, and scales linearly.
o1zN398IHm.main_concern: Evidence does not isolate the learned FMM design from simply adding directional nonlocal information (no fixed-FMM ablation or Ewald-based baselines), and accuracy at large scale is untested.

ZjTEBV3mT2.one_liner: Coordinates separately trained protein generators at inference by conditioning each on the others' sequence populations, iteratively refining multi-context designs.
ZjTEBV3mT2.problem: Multi-scenario protein tasks, such as a binder for two unrelated targets or a ligand-triggered fold switch, cannot be trained directly because structural data for one protein across contexts is scarce.
ZjTEBV3mT2.method: Control-Proteina (Ctrl-P) lets each separately trained model express its preferences as a population of sequences and condition its own generation on the preferences of the others. Iterative refinement converges on designs that succeed in every context; reviews note it also uses folding-model seeding.
ZjTEBV3mT2.key_idea: Each context-specific generator conditions on populations of sequences preferred by the other generators, and iterating this exchange converges on sequences that work in every context.
ZjTEBV3mT2.evidence: A multi-target protein-protein interaction benchmark spanning similar and dissimilar binding interfaces, and allosteric motif-switch design tasks, judged by AlphaFold-family predictions per the reviews.
ZjTEBV3mT2.claimed_gains: Solves 18 of 20 target pairs, including 8 of the 10 dissimilar pairs where the strongest baseline solves 2; solves 8 of 12 allosteric switch tasks versus a stronger-baseline figure that is truncated.
ZjTEBV3mT2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it coordinates models without multi-scenario training data and clearly beats baselines on dissimilar-interface multi-target tasks.
ZjTEBV3mT2.main_concern: Success is measured only by in-silico AlphaFold-family predictions and confidence scores without wet-lab validation, and ablations isolating preference alignment are limited.

1YLDlrCVvr.one_liner: Multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching, pretrained on ~5M OMol25/OMat24 structures for unified atomistic generation and prediction.
1YLDlrCVvr.problem: Existing atomistic generative models are specialized to chemistry or biology, or do not use both organic molecule and inorganic material data for general-purpose pretraining.
1YLDlrCVvr.method: Zatom-2 pretrains a multiscale Transformer with conditional flow matching on approximately five million structures from OMol25 and OMat24. It supports force conditioning and tasks including generation, structure prediction and energy and force prediction, and transfers to protein generation.
1YLDlrCVvr.key_idea: Jointly pretrain generation, structure prediction and energy/force prediction on molecule and material data so physics-based objectives transfer to low-data protein generation.
1YLDlrCVvr.evidence: Molecule and material generation benchmarks, controllable generation across low- and high-force regimes, and protein backbone designability in a length-extrapolation setting with and without pretraining.
1YLDlrCVvr.claimed_gains: Better molecular distribution fidelity than Zatom-1; protein backbone designability in length extrapolation rises from 67.8% without pretraining to 74.8%.
1YLDlrCVvr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it tackles an important unified atomistic modeling problem with a broad, coherent implementation and shows pretraining benefits for generation and protein designability.
1YLDlrCVvr.main_concern: Improvements are not isolated to individual pretraining components, since adding the MLIP task also changes the task mixture and loss weights, and methodological novelty is limited.

ziWJ6tZUwg.one_liner: Hazard-guided sampler for graph discrete flow matching that plans edits and adapts sampling time from CTMC hazard and jump decomposition.
ziWJ6tZUwg.problem: Graph discrete flow matching models still need sampling budgets comparable to diffusion, and existing graph samplers rely on task-specific heuristics that expand the hyperparameter space.
ziWJ6tZUwg.method: H-Glow decomposes CTMC generators into hazards and conditional jump distributions, uses them to plan graph edits and adjust sampling time to graph activity, and can be applied to pretrained graph DFM models. A new DFM model based on conditional generator matching predicts hazards and jumps directly, with an objective that decomposes exactly into hazard matching and hazard-weighted jump prediction.
ziWJ6tZUwg.key_idea: Predict the hazard, then the conditional jump, from the CTMC generator decomposition, and use them to plan graph edits and adapt sampling time to graph activity.
ziWJ6tZUwg.evidence: Experiments on molecular and synthetic graph generation (abstract truncated); reviews mention QM9 for the new training loss, integration with DeFoG, and realized NFE counts.
ziWJ6tZUwg.claimed_gains: No numbers stated; the abstract claims substantially better generation quality with fewer steps on pretrained graph DFM models.
ziWJ6tZUwg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the hazard-then-jump idea technically solid, with well-developed mathematics, addressing generation quality under small sampling budgets and integrating with existing frameworks.
ziWJ6tZUwg.main_concern: Acceleration evidence is thin, with realized NFEs but no matched-hardware wall-clock measurements or uncertainty estimates, and the gap relative to prior hazard-based work such as SimGFM is unclear.

ci5rXZp0QI.one_liner: Studies causal linear sequence mixers, especially DeltaNet, for tabular in-context learning and stabilizes length generalisation with a decay schedule.
ci5rXZp0QI.problem: Softmax attention limits tabular foundation models on large datasets, and existing linear-time alternatives are mostly causal and underexplored for tabular in-context learning.
ci5rXZp0QI.method: They revisit causal training setups, compare linear sequence mixers, and probe generalisation beyond the pretraining context length, then modulate DeltaNet's write rates with a time-dependent decay schedule and read out from the final state to reintroduce non-causality.
ci5rXZp0QI.key_idea: DeltaNet's learned write rates overfit the pretraining context length, so a time-dependent decay schedule stabilises its drifting recurrent state at longer contexts.
ci5rXZp0QI.evidence: Controlled comparisons under a TabPFNv1-style setup per reviews, a hidden-state oracle, DeltaNet versus non-causal linear attention, and length-generalisation tests beyond the pretraining context length.
ci5rXZp0QI.claimed_gains: DeltaNet outperforms non-causal linear attention but degrades beyond 2-4x the pretraining context length; no performance numbers for the final method are given in the available abstract.
ci5rXZp0QI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper offers a broad sweep of experimental and ablation insights on linear attention for tabular foundation models, with clear framing and explicitly stated shortcomings.
ci5rXZp0QI.main_concern: The controlled setup (fixed prior, parameter count, and hyperparameters of a weak TabPFNv1-style recipe) makes it unclear whether the insights transfer to real model development.

Zj3deXGzeO.one_liner: Uses real geometry to bound VC and split-VC dimension of multi-layer softmax transformers over real values, with lower-bound constructions.
Zj3deXGzeO.problem: Prior results on transformer abilities and limits restrict the model definition in various ways, so the expressivity of softmax multi-layer transformers operating on real values is poorly characterized.
Zj3deXGzeO.method: Applies results from real geometry to bound the VC dimension of softmax-attention multi-layer transformers (O(n^4) with fixed positional encodings, O(n^6) with learned ones) and their split VC dimension (O(n^6)), and constructs transformers witnessing Omega(n) lower bounds for the learned-encoding VC and split-VC cases.
Zj3deXGzeO.key_idea: Real-geometry bounds on softmax transformer computations over the reals give polynomial VC bounds without finite-precision or unproven complexity-theoretic assumptions.
Zj3deXGzeO.evidence: Pure theory: VC and split-VC upper bounds, lower-bound constructions, and consequences for symmetric functions and bit-access limits.
Zj3deXGzeO.claimed_gains: VC dimension bounds of O(n^4) with fixed positional encodings and O(n^6) with learned ones, split VC dimension O(n^6), and Omega(n) lower bounds for the second and third cases.
Zj3deXGzeO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the VC bounds without finite-precision assumptions and the use of real geometry interesting, and value the bit-access result showing infinite precision does not give unlimited access to the bits of a real number.
Zj3deXGzeO.main_concern: Novelty over classical Pfaffian VC bounds and prior split-VC and limitation results is unclear, the symmetric-function inexpressibility is nonconstructive, the bounds have large gaps (Omega(n) versus O(n^4) and O(n^6)), and the paper is hard to follow.

DTySOElXfw.one_liner: Studies adversarial preference-based episodic MDPs with Borda losses, giving matching regret bounds via online linear optimization over occupancy measures.
DTySOElXfw.problem: Dueling bandit theory does not cover settings where the compared pair also affects the next state, as when a shown pair changes a user's next context.
DTySOElXfw.method: They formulate a state-wise preference-based MDP where the learner picks an arm pair at each visited state, sees only a noisy comparison, and incurs Borda-score loss under adversarially changing preferences. They give an occupancy-measure algorithm and a policy optimization algorithm with closed-form updates.
DTySOElXfw.key_idea: Run online linear optimization over occupancy measures with Borda-score losses, which matches a lower bound showing the cost of action-dependent transitions.
DTySOElXfw.evidence: Regret upper and lower bounds for known transitions, a policy optimization regret bound, and synthetic experiments built on the lower-bound setting.
DTySOElXfw.claimed_gains: Minimax regret under known transitions is Theta~(min{HT, (H^3 S K)^{1/3} T^{2/3}}), and the policy optimization algorithm has regret O~((H^4 S K^3)^{1/3} T^{2/3}) up to lower-order terms.
DTySOElXfw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the move from dueling bandits to sequential decision-making is well motivated and the theory is comprehensive, with matching upper and lower bounds and results for known and unknown transitions.
DTySOElXfw.main_concern: Technical novelty looks like a combination of standard adversarial-MDP methods and Borda estimation, and the practical relevance of the model and its experimental validation are limited.

hiKt0Otgde.one_liner: Behavioral probes show top open ASR models reproduce benchmark reference transcripts even when audio is contradictory, masked, or ambiguous.
hiKt0Otgde.problem: Public ASR benchmarks can be optimized for in ways that do not generalize to real-world data, and the extent of this is not quantified.
hiKt0Otgde.method: Three families of behavioral probes (reference disagreement, masked-number recovery, orthographic agreement) measure how often models reproduce reference spans when the audio underdetermines the transcript. The behavior is then manipulated causally with low-rank linear steering or appended audio.
hiKt0Otgde.key_idea: Use cases where audio underdetermines the reference, so reproducing reference spans exposes benchmark-conditioned behavior, then toggle that behavior by steering or appending audio.
hiKt0Otgde.evidence: Probes on the highest-scoring open-source ASR models, context experiments (truncation, appended audio, steering) with clip-level bootstrap intervals, and a fine-tuning experiment on public training sets.
hiKt0Otgde.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the probes are a systematic, reusable way to measure benchmark-conditioned behavior and that the intervention experiments give stronger evidence than cross-model correlation.
hiKt0Otgde.main_concern: What counts as a reference error is ambiguous (annotation style and editing conventions in VoxPopuli), and probes such as orthographic agreement and audio lift may measure formatting or useful context rather than benchmark optimization.

pSoaOGXiXQ.one_liner: Geometric framework clarifying when parameter symmetries yield gradient-flow conservation laws, with an inheritance principle for multilayer networks.
pSoaOGXiXQ.problem: The precise relationship between parameter-space symmetries and conservation laws under gradient flow is unclear, since prior Noether-inspired work did not settle when symmetries give conservation laws.
pSoaOGXiXQ.method: It develops a geometric framework giving conditions under which partial symmetries correspond to conservation laws, introduces compositional identifiability, and uses it for an inheritance principle characterizing partial symmetries and conservation laws in multilayer networks. It is applied to multihead and grouped-query attention, polynomial networks, and square deep linear networks.
pSoaOGXiXQ.key_idea: The gap between symmetries and conservation laws is the Lie-algebra rank minus the symmetry rank, zero iff involutive; compositional identifiability gives layerwise inheritance.
pSoaOGXiXQ.evidence: Theorems and propositions with applications to multihead and grouped-query attention, polynomial neural networks, and square deep linear networks; the work is theoretical.
pSoaOGXiXQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clarifies the link between symmetries and conservation laws under gradient flow, and that the inheritance principle and the clean gap characterization are valuable theoretical contributions.
pSoaOGXiXQ.main_concern: Key definitions need geometric motivation and the multilayer claim is overstated, with restricted applicability of the inheritance theorem and limited novelty because the gap characterization follows from existing ideas.

nQbIaZEuXP.one_liner: Proves linear lower and upper bounds on frames for continuous equivariant weighted frame averaging, with an explicit Wronskian construction.
nQbIaZEuXP.problem: Canonicalization is discontinuous, and the frame averaging that restores continuity costs more as the number of frames grows (n^(d-1) in Dym et al.'s construction).
nQbIaZEuXP.method: They prove with Dold's generalization of Borsuk-Ulam and characteristic classes of Grassmannians that linearly many frames are necessary for continuous SO(d)/O(d)-equivariant weighted frames, and give a Wronskian-based construction with d(n-d)+1 frames. The construction allows training with one frame per input and continuous prediction by weighted averaging without retraining.
nQbIaZEuXP.key_idea: Wronskian-based weighted frames attain the linear upper bound of d(n-d)+1 frames; train with one frame per input, predict by weighted averaging.
nQbIaZEuXP.evidence: Topological lower-bound proofs and an explicit construction, plus a synthetic 24-particle force-prediction experiment and a moving-boundary experiment mentioned in reviews.
nQbIaZEuXP.claimed_gains: Uses 61 instead of 1,012 frames for 24 particles in three dimensions and reports 48.2% lower error on held-out configurations in a synthetic 24-particle force-learning experiment.
nQbIaZEuXP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of how many frames continuous equivariant frame averaging needs is natural and important, and that the theoretical analysis looks solid.
nQbIaZEuXP.main_concern: The presentation is too dense and assumes specialist background, and the synthetic experiments are weak compared with the theory.

bFQtHEiLVo.one_liner: Trains LLM user simulators on latent-state labels as posterior-regularized marginal likelihood, optimized with self-normalized importance sampling EM.
bFQtHEiLVo.problem: Treating user latent state as a latent variable in LLM user simulation is intractable and unidentifiable from observational data, so it has been handled heuristically and generalizes poorly to novel agents.
bFQtHEiLVo.method: RUSTLeD formalizes fine-tuning on latent-state labels as posterior-regularized maximization of the marginal likelihood of observed conversations, interpolating between teacher distillation and autoencoding. The SNIS-EM algorithm optimizes it with self-normalized importance sampling over LLM-proposed latent states.
bFQtHEiLVo.key_idea: A regularization weight alpha interpolates between label distillation (alpha=0) and marginal-likelihood autoencoding, optimized by self-normalized importance sampling EM over LLM-proposed latent states.
bFQtHEiLVo.evidence: Held-out human conversation likelihood and reproduction of human behavior against natural baselines; reviews note a single shopping domain with Gemini 2.5 labeler, simulator, and judge.
bFQtHEiLVo.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says simulators generalize better to unseen agents than natural baselines, without numbers)
bFQtHEiLVo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framework gives a principled unification of label distillation and marginal-likelihood training for latent-state simulators, with an explicit trade-off between following the labeler and fitting observed behavior.
bFQtHEiLVo.main_concern: Gains from SNIS-EM reweighting over the alpha=0 smoothing baseline are small and confounded with proposal count, and evaluation covers one shopping domain and one model family with an unvalidated LLM judge.

o21n20wHpB.one_liner: Benchmark for target-conditioned trigger attribution in videos, with an event-graph reasoning baseline, EventGraph-Trigger.
o21n20wHpB.problem: Video models capture temporal co-occurrence but struggle to separate events that merely precede a target from events that meaningfully explain it.
o21n20wHpB.method: Given an ordered sequence of localized events and a target event anywhere in the timeline, models must identify earlier events that give plausible explanatory support. The benchmark provides auto-verified trigger labels, evaluates heuristic, sequential, graph-based, multimodal, causal and LLM baselines, and adds EventGraph-Trigger, a multimodal event-graph reasoning framework.
o21n20wHpB.key_idea: Frame explanation as target-conditioned trigger attribution over localized events, with auto-verified labels and a multimodal event-graph reasoner.
o21n20wHpB.evidence: A broad baseline comparison (heuristic, sequential, graph-based, multimodal, causal, LLM), independent human annotation of 300 samples agreeing with auto labels in 77.7% of cases, and modality ablations.
o21n20wHpB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the target-conditioned task is meaningful and that the annotation pipeline and human validation make the dataset credible.
o21n20wHpB.main_concern: Labels and baselines rely on older models (GPT-4 Turbo, GPT-4o) with caption-only verification, and novelty over prior work such as CARVE and CERN is questioned.

1SOwFByqYJ.one_liner: Shows velocity-prediction DiTs retain noise outside the output layer's span, forcing width to track token dimension; clean prediction avoids this.
1SOwFByqYJ.problem: Diffusion transformers can fail to fit even a single image when width is smaller than the token dimension, and the implications for sampling and for the choice of prediction target are unclear.
1SOwFByqYJ.method: Proves that for direct velocity prediction deterministic updates preserve the component of the initial noise outside the span of the output weights and bias, gives a general linear-skip criterion separating regression penalty from retained noise, and tests the predictions with interventions on head rank, backbone features and readout loss.
1SOwFByqYJ.key_idea: The output layer's rank fixes which noise components deterministic sampling can remove, so predicting the clean token, which is not full rank, avoids the width requirement.
1SOwFByqYJ.evidence: Theory plus interventions at fixed backbone width on single-image fitting and full data distributions, with a data-spectrum bound on the optimal rank-induced excess.
1SOwFByqYJ.claimed_gains: At fixed backbone width, reducing head rank from 768 to 256 raises mean FID after fine-tuning by 74.3 for direct prediction and 84.2 for EDM, versus 2.6 for clean prediction.
1SOwFByqYJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper gives a precise, quantitatively validated explanation of the width bottleneck that links output-layer rank to a sampling invariant.
1SOwFByqYJ.main_concern: The contribution overlaps substantially with prior work (RAE's covariance-tail bound, JiT, AsymFlow) and is not clearly distinguished from it.

A70YVKYiBn.one_liner: Two-layer gather-and-match transformer circuits, proven exact for deterministic and near-Bayes-optimal for stochastic cellular automata, found in trained models.
A70YVKYiBn.problem: Induction-head theory assumes the relevant context is a contiguous block, but serializing multidimensional data scatters spatial neighbors across distant token positions.
A70YVKYiBn.method: In spatial induction heads, the first layer gathers the relevant spatial neighborhood through two explicit realizations and the second layer matches that configuration against earlier occurrences, implementing Bayesian counting. Trained two-layer transformers are then tested on unseen rules.
A70YVKYiBn.key_idea: The first attention layer reconstructs each cell's spatial neighborhood from flattened positions, and the second counts matching earlier neighborhoods to approximate the Bayesian posterior.
A70YVKYiBn.evidence: Constructive proofs (positional dimension depends only on neighborhood and spatial dimension, plus an end-to-end bound) and experiments on trained two-layer transformers in one- and two-dimensional cellular automata, with attention analysis, ablations, and probes.
A70YVKYiBn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending induction-head theory to spatial dependencies scattered by serialization is a clear, constructive framing supported by mechanistic evidence in trained models.
A70YVKYiBn.main_concern: The empirical settings are small, mild synthetic cellular-automata problems (for example a 6 x 6 grid), so evidence for realistic or scalable spatial routing is limited.

uggzfUoAgS.one_liner: Memory-efficient adaptive zeroth-order optimizer that tracks one scalar to adapt the global step size, matching ZO-Adam robustness.
uggzfUoAgS.problem: Adaptive ZO methods such as ZO-Adam are claimed to help LLM fine-tuning but add optimizer-state memory, and it is unclear whether their adaptivity helps beyond well-tuned ZO-SGD.
uggzfUoAgS.method: The paper shows ZO-Adam gives no performance or convergence advantage over tuned ZO-SGD, explains why coordinate-wise adaptivity is weak in large-scale ZO, and proposes MEAZO, which tracks a single scalar to adapt the global step size. Convergence is guaranteed under standard smoothness assumptions.
uggzfUoAgS.key_idea: Replaces per-coordinate second-moment state with one scalar that adapts the global step size, because a shared isotropic term dominates per-coordinate second moments when q is much smaller than d.
uggzfUoAgS.evidence: Synthetic quadratic problems and fine-tuning of multiple LLM families (e.g., Llama-3.2 1B) on diverse tasks, with step-size sweeps, multiple seeds, and comparisons to ZO-SGD, ZO-Adam, and FZOO.
uggzfUoAgS.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract says MEAZO performs comparably to competing methods and matches ZO-Adam's step-size robustness without extra memory or latency overhead, with no numbers.
uggzfUoAgS.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clear theoretical account (Proposition 3.1) of why coordinate-wise adaptivity fails in ZO and the extensive step-size sweeps across models and tasks.
uggzfUoAgS.main_concern: Missing comparisons with other memory-efficient or step-size-robust ZO methods (ZO-SignSGD, LOZO, Sparse-MeZO, normalized ZO-SGD, clipping), alongside limited novelty and a robustness gain smaller than claimed.

zU6jaaKkqZ.one_liner: Search agent trained with SFT then GRPO to find evidence via shell commands over a text corpus, with execution speedups.
zU6jaaKkqZ.problem: Most LLM search agents depend on retrievers over a pre-built index, and stabilizing RL for agents that search large corpora directly with shell commands is hard and slow.
zU6jaaKkqZ.method: GrepSeek is a direct corpus interaction agent first initialized on verified, causally grounded trajectories from an answer-aware Tutor and an answer-blind Planner, then refined with GRPO. Two semantics-preserving optimizations, Pruned Adaptive Command Execution and Sharded-Parallel Corpus Search, speed up shell search.
zU6jaaKkqZ.key_idea: Treats the corpus as the environment: the agent composes executable shell commands (e.g., rg, head) to find, filter, and compose evidence, trained on grounded trajectories then GRPO.
zU6jaaKkqZ.evidence: Eight open-domain QA benchmarks against dense-retrieval baselines, latency tests on a 14 GB corpus of 21 million documents, and ablations of cold-start SFT and GRPO.
zU6jaaKkqZ.claimed_gains: Up to 77x lower shell-search latency (PACE) on a 14 GB, 21-million-document corpus and up to 7.6x speedup (SPCS); the abstract reports the strongest overall performance on eight QA benchmarks, with the accuracy figure cut off.
zU6jaaKkqZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the execution optimizations are practical and the Tutor-Planner cold-start data plus GRPO pipeline is carefully built and supported by ablations.
zU6jaaKkqZ.main_concern: Attribution of gains is unclear: no BM25 baseline, limited differentiation from prior direct corpus interaction work, and the strongest retrieval baseline is not trained with the same two-stage pipeline.

iNMAzvzAYd.one_liner: Adapts pretrained graph foundation models for link prediction with cached full-neighborhood signatures, query-side structural operators, and score fusion.
iNMAzvzAYd.problem: Retrieval-compatible graph foundation models lose structural evidence through neighborhood sampling, restrict its use with standard similarity readouts, and suffer negative transfer from shared structural mechanisms across relationships.
iNMAzvzAYd.method: SURF augments a pretrained graph-transformer backbone (HGT by default) with precomputed full-neighborhood node signatures, lightweight relation-conditioned structural operators, and score fusion. Relation-dependent computation is confined to the query side, so reusable candidate representations and indexed retrieval are preserved.
iNMAzvzAYd.key_idea: Confine relation-dependent structural computation to the query side over precomputed neighborhood signatures, so candidate vectors stay reusable for indexed retrieval without updating the backbone.
iNMAzvzAYd.evidence: 16 academic datasets (the abstract is cut off) across multiple backbones, plus large-scale production experiments that reviewers describe as over a billion scored pairs.
iNMAzvzAYd.claimed_gains: SURF delivers 73.4-183.6% relative MRR gains on production data.
iNMAzvzAYd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the gap in structural link prediction for graph foundation models is well defined and that the lightweight, index-preserving design gives substantial gains across datasets and backbones.
iNMAzvzAYd.main_concern: Ablations do not isolate whether gains come from the structural adaptation or from calibration and learned fusion of known heuristics, and comparisons with structural predictors such as NCN/NCNC or MPLP are missing.

aSWuUvGT84.one_liner: Injects knowledge by self-distilling on token mixtures of a fact-aware expert conditional and a naive conditional of the base model.
aSWuUvGT84.problem: SFT knowledge injection degrades pretrained capabilities because human- or externally-written targets diverge from the model's own distribution, forcing the optimizer to imitate low-probability sequences.
aSWuUvGT84.method: MixSD is teacher-free: it builds supervision dynamically by mixing tokens from two conditionals of the base model, an expert conditional that sees the injected fact in context and a naive conditional reflecting the original prior. The resulting sequences keep the factual signal while staying closer to the base model's distribution.
aSWuUvGT84.key_idea: Bernoulli token-level mixing of the expert (fact-in-context) and naive conditionals of the same model produces distribution-aligned supervision sequences.
aSWuUvGT84.evidence: Two constructed synthetic corpora (KGFact and KGFunc), open-domain factual QA, and knowledge editing, across multiple model scales, with ablations and Fisher-alignment analysis.
aSWuUvGT84.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says MixSD consistently achieves a substantially improved memorization-retention trade-off over SFT and other baselines, without figures).
aSWuUvGT84.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the controlled synthetic setup and analyses make the forgetting claim testable, and that MixSD gives a better memorization-retention trade-off than SFT and OPSD.
aSWuUvGT84.main_concern: Novelty over context distillation and self-distillation work is limited, MixSD still falls below the base model on held-out capability, and gains are not isolated from changes in target length and style.

rpovJ3Apnt.one_liner: Computes minimum complete specification languages via Bellman backups over Specification Equivalence Sets, with a VQVAE-style deep RL extension.
rpovJ3Apnt.problem: As AI systems solve any task we can specify, the bottleneck becomes specifying tasks efficiently, and the minimum specification language that determines optimal behavior for any task in a domain is unknown.
rpovJ3Apnt.method: They formalize the Specification Language Design Problem and define the Specification Equivalence Set, the minimum information needed to determine an optimal policy, which has recursive substructure allowing exact computation by Bellman backup. A deep RL extension trains an agent controllable through a latent specification language with a VQVAE-inspired method.
rpovJ3Apnt.key_idea: Group tasks that share optimal policies into Specification Equivalence Sets that obey a Bellman recursion, then learn a discrete latent code for those sets with a VQVAE-style agent.
rpovJ3Apnt.evidence: An exact algorithm on specification problems (maze experiments per reviews) and a deep RL algorithm that matches the exact one at small scales and scales to larger domains; reviewers note proofs of Theorem 1 and Proposition 2.
rpovJ3Apnt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question of the minimum information needed to specify an optimal policy is interesting and relevant, and that separating completeness from minimality gives a useful framework.
rpovJ3Apnt.main_concern: The contribution is unclear and the theory-practice link is weak: the exact algorithm assumes optimal policies and a shared transition kernel, and the deep objective does not enforce completeness or minimality and suffers codebook collapse.

pwseyFaKAp.one_liner: Training-free Euler timestep schedule for flow matching derived from offline finite-difference estimates of velocity-field sharpness along calibration trajectories.
pwseyFaKAp.problem: Fast flow-matching sampling has a small fixed evaluation budget, and uniform timestep grids do not spend steps where the learned velocity field changes fastest.
pwseyFaKAp.method: SharpEuler profiles a pretrained model offline by finite-difference estimates of where the velocity field changes most rapidly along calibration trajectories. The sharpness profile is smoothed and turned by a quantile transform into a timestep grid for any budget, and sampling stays ordinary Euler with the same number of evaluations.
pwseyFaKAp.key_idea: Allocate Euler steps in proportion to trajectory acceleration (sharpness) measured offline, converted into a timestep density by a quantile transform.
pwseyFaKAp.evidence: Three principles (Euler error from trajectory acceleration, variational power-law timestep densities, a finite-sample stability guarantee), plus synthetic studies, FLUX with 1,000 held-out prompts, and qualitative video per reviews.
pwseyFaKAp.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says sample quality improves at fixed budgets, with less inter-mode leakage and more mode coverage, without numbers)
pwseyFaKAp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is simple to deploy with no retraining or extra evaluations, has a clear rationale linking acceleration to Euler error, and improves FLUX agreement with a high-step reference at matched budgets.
pwseyFaKAp.main_concern: Comparisons with alternative calibrated schedules such as OSS are limited mostly to synthetic data, and calibration-set construction and sensitivity on large models are underspecified.

t2tpUCDzws.one_liner: Learns causal abstractions of linear SCMs, including some cyclic ones, by graph partitioning followed by differentiable learning of aggregation weights.
t2tpUCDzws.problem: A valid causal abstraction must preserve interventional semantics in a more compact model, but unsupervised methods for finding abstractions of linear SCMs are limited and cyclic models are not covered.
t2tpUCDzws.method: Two stages: partition variables with algorithms, one of which guarantees sufficient graphical conditions for exact abstraction, then learn linear aggregation weights with a differentiable constrained objective, with algebraic characterizations extended to a subclass of cyclic SCMs. Reduces p variables to a target k < p.
t2tpUCDzws.key_idea: Pick clusters satisfying sufficient graphical conditions (All-In, One-Child, acyclic cluster graph) and then fit aggregation weights by constrained differentiable optimization with a tunable error tolerance.
t2tpUCDzws.evidence: Sufficient-condition theorems and experiments on synthetic graphs and empirical economic input-output networks, compared against an existing unsupervised baseline.
t2tpUCDzws.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the abstract says the methods recover non-trivial abstractions and outperform the existing unsupervised baseline.
t2tpUCDzws.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory a novel, sound extension of linear causal abstraction to a class of cyclic graphs, with a constructive pipeline and a controllable trade-off between exactness and informativeness.
t2tpUCDzws.main_concern: The One-Child condition forces large merged clusters on branching graphs, empirical validation rests on one real economic example, and AOC Closure's validity guarantee is not fully supported.

wcpwuWOfkY.one_liner: Probe has a strong model write yes/no questions per item so a small judge ranks systems on fewer items.
wcpwuWOfkY.problem: Selecting benchmark items improves ranking agreement only for systems used in selection and hurts new systems, so it is unclear when a small test can match a reference ranking better than the full benchmark.
wcpwuWOfkY.method: In Probe, a strong model writes yes/no questions once per item and a small judge answers them on 21% to 30% of the full benchmark, keeping the number of judge calls the same. A rule fitted on the systems used in the selection predicts the gain.
wcpwuWOfkY.key_idea: Change the question the judge answers by replacing each item with strong-model-written yes/no questions, instead of only choosing which items to keep.
wcpwuWOfkY.evidence: Experiments over 49 task-judge pairs with weak and strong judges and reference rankings from correct answers or strong-model ratings, evaluated on new systems not used in selection.
wcpwuWOfkY.claimed_gains: With a weak judge Probe beats the full benchmark on new systems by +0.41 (+0.32 after correcting for pair choice, +0.23 under a stricter per-split weak-judge definition); the first question alone gains +0.48 without human labels, and a fitted rule predicts the gain at r = 0.95 and the winner in 42 of 49 task-judge pairs.
wcpwuWOfkY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is meaningful that a compressed benchmark can match human rankings better than the full one, and that the experiments are fairly comprehensive.
wcpwuWOfkY.main_concern: The Headroom Law is presented as more general than shown: headroom is defined from the same baseline correlation that bounds the gain, and evaluation cells share tasks and judges so they are not independent.

xSyhsAIPkU.one_liner: Trust-Anchored Gating elects an anchor reward channel and conditions auxiliary reward credit on it to prevent multi-reward hacking.
xSyhsAIPkU.problem: Symmetric aggregation of several reward signals in LLM post-training can raise the aggregate reward while the primary criterion degrades, as the policy adopts behavior that satisfies an auxiliary channel without satisfying the primary one.
xSyhsAIPkU.method: The paper analyzes a one-step multi-reward MDP with two channels and three actions, proving that GRPO dynamics select the auxiliary action under a reward-frequency gap. TAG elects an anchor channel from the drift each channel induces when optimized alone, then conditions auxiliary credit on that anchor structurally.
xSyhsAIPkU.key_idea: Pick the anchor channel by the drift each channel induces when optimized alone, then give auxiliary credit only conditioned on the elected anchor channel.
xSyhsAIPkU.evidence: Theory on a two-channel, three-action one-step MDP under GRPO, plus experiments across several settings whose auxiliary probes include answer templates, negative answers and constant-printing programs per reviews.
xSyhsAIPkU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is relevant, the explanation of why symmetric aggregation fails under GRPO is clear, and the method mitigates the failure modes across several settings.
xSyhsAIPkU.main_concern: The theory rests on a highly simplified one-step MDP, and anchor election is under-validated on few two-channel settings and possibly confounded by response length.

LsfWORAbdA.one_liner: ProoFit audits overfitting with zero-knowledge proofs of weight-only tests, avoiding proofs of the training trajectory.
LsfWORAbdA.problem: Auditing whether a model is overfitted cannot be done directly without revealing proprietary weights, and zero-knowledge proofs of entire training trajectories are prohibitively expensive.
LsfWORAbdA.method: ProoFit uses tests that depend only on trained model weights, leveraging theoretical connections between generalization and model complexity. Per reviews it follows model commitment, certificate generation and audit verification, and proves computations on audit examples relative to a reference model.
LsfWORAbdA.key_idea: Prove in zero knowledge a weight-based complexity test comparing the candidate model against a reference model, rather than proving the training process.
