LsfWORAbdA.evidence: Experiments on CNNs such as ResNet-18 on CIFAR-10 and SimpleCNN on FMNIST, compared with baseline cryptographic approaches that prove training.
LsfWORAbdA.claimed_gains: 10^3 to 10^7 times improvement in runtime over baseline cryptographic approaches.
LsfWORAbdA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that confidential overfitting audits address a practical, well-motivated problem and that the efficiency gains over proving full training are significant.
LsfWORAbdA.main_concern: Audit reliability is unclear: the test is relative to an under-described reference model, and true negative rates are only 60% and 62.5% in some settings.

MFFYUUwGjs.one_liner: One ~21M JEPA trained with Brownian-bridge state noise and flow-matching action noise serves planning, behaviour cloning, and inverse dynamics.
MFFYUUwGjs.problem: Published pixel-based JEPA world models each commit at training time to one inference paradigm, so a checkpoint trained to plan cannot serve as a policy without retraining.
MFFYUUwGjs.method: Qantara pairs a Brownian-bridge interpolant between consecutive clean latents on the state axis with noise-to-data flow matching on the action axis. One checkpoint serves latent planning, behaviour-cloning action sampling, and a video-inverse composition that predicts the next latent without action conditioning and then recovers the bridging action.
MFFYUUwGjs.key_idea: Train by sampling (action-noise, state-noise) levels along the edges of the noise square, one edge per inference path, so each path is trained where it is queried.
MFFYUUwGjs.evidence: Evaluated on the LeWM control suite (Push-T, Cube, Two-Room, Reacher, Cube-Double per reviewers) against in-pipeline retrained baselines such as LeWM and DINO-WM, with 750 episodes per cell over 3 training seeds and a sampler ablation.
MFFYUUwGjs.claimed_gains: Edge-based sampling gives Push-T planning success of 90.1 versus 53.3 for uniform sampling at matched compute; other results are cut off in the abstract.
MFFYUUwGjs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the evaluation is careful (retrained baselines, 750 episodes over 3 seeds), the sampling ablation is well controlled, and planning results on Cube and other tasks are strong.
MFFYUUwGjs.main_concern: Gains over LeWM are not compute-matched because each sample is replicated across five modes, and matched specialist baselines (separate policy plus world model, heads on frozen LeWM latents) are missing.

pUSAvpWvyZ.one_liner: Intent-centric composed video retrieval: explicit intent localizes modifications and implicit intent suppresses irrelevant details of the reference video.
pUSAvpWvyZ.problem: Existing composed video retrieval methods refine each modality separately and underexplore how video-text interaction determines retrieval intent, causing imprecise modification and indiscriminate preservation.
pUSAvpWvyZ.method: IC-CoVR builds structured video representations for video-text interaction and intent reasoning, uses explicit intent to locate and guide targeted modification, and uses implicit intent to selectively preserve unmodified content by suppressing irrelevant details.
pUSAvpWvyZ.key_idea: Split retrieval intent into explicit intent (what to modify) and implicit intent (what to preserve), both resolved from joint video-text interaction rather than per-modality refinement.
pUSAvpWvyZ.evidence: Experiments on FineCVR-1M and EgoCVR with ablations on main components, granularity alignment, training objectives, and backbones.
pUSAvpWvyZ.claimed_gains: Reports top performance on FineCVR-1M and EgoCVR; the abstract gives no numbers.
pUSAvpWvyZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deciding what to modify and what to preserve is a well-motivated problem, results on FineCVR-1M are strong, and the ablations are extensive.
pUSAvpWvyZ.main_concern: The explicit and implicit intent modules mostly combine existing attention and fusion techniques without direct supervision, so it is unclear the model learns meaningful intents, and recent baselines are missing.

1ebOQtaUvN.one_liner: Jointly tuning batch size and recipe for repeated-data pretraining shows small batches and fewer GPUs can win under deadlines.
1ebOQtaUvN.problem: Prior infinite-compute pretraining results with finite unique data fixed or studied in isolation choices such as batch size and training recipe, and did not treat GPUs and wall-clock time as separate resources.
1ebOQtaUvN.method: An empirical study that revisits infinite-compute pretraining (Kim et al. 2025), jointly optimizes batch size with epoch counts, tunes recipe choices (repacking documents each epoch, weight tying, positive embedding weight decay), then relaxes the infinite-compute assumption by separating GPUs from time.
1ebOQtaUvN.key_idea: Optimizing batch size jointly with epoch count reveals a U-shaped loss-versus-batch-size curve favoring small batches, likely through implicit regularization from gradient noise.
1ebOQtaUvN.evidence: Empirical sweeps over batch size, epochs, and recipe choices on finite data pools, with a reviewer noting B=64 stays optimal across three data pools.
1ebOQtaUvN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is a practical, well-documented empirical guide for data-limited pretraining, with experiments over a wide range of batch sizes and all configurations reported.
1ebOQtaUvN.main_concern: Novelty and generality are unclear: small-batch generalization is a known effect, the small-batch advantage may not be specific to repeated data, and the pattern may depend on model size, learning-rate schedule, and dataset.

gYYg17iMGl.one_liner: Latent variance-scaled consistency training with frozen, prototype-based test-time adaptation for semi-supervised domain generalization.
gYYg17iMGl.problem: With few labeled examples per class, semi-supervised domain generalization struggles to learn reliable class structure, and domain shift can misalign that structure with target data.
gYYg17iMGl.method: During training, pseudo-labels from weakly augmented examples supervise two views: an image-space augmentation and a variance-scaled stochastic perturbation of the learned latent representation. At test time the encoder and classifier stay frozen; target representations are aligned with source class structure and target-aware prototypes are estimated from confident target samples, excluding samples with little evidence of domain shift.
gYYg17iMGl.key_idea: Perturb latents by a learned posterior variance for consistency training; at test time only align features and re-estimate class prototypes, with no parameter updates.
gYYg17iMGl.evidence: PACS, OfficeHome, Digits-DG, and miniDomainNet with 5 and 10 labels per class, compared with the strongest SSDG baseline and parameter-free TTA methods, plus an ablation removing the variational latent component.
gYYg17iMGl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the uncertainty-aware latent perturbation and the frozen, parameter-free test-time adaptation are interesting, and it outperforms the evaluated parameter-free TTA methods.
gYYg17iMGl.main_concern: Test-time adaptation uses the whole unlabeled test set, so comparison with SSDG baselines that get no target information may be unfair, and the individual design components of the latent perturbation are not ablated separately.

1937ieHnYA.one_liner: Per-sample sparse coding replaces linear SAE encoding to learn dictionaries with more consistent features across seeds.
1937ieHnYA.problem: Sparse autoencoder dictionaries vary across training runs, limiting reproducibility of model-interpretability analyses.
1937ieHnYA.method: ConSDL optimizes sparse coefficients per sample instead of using a single linear encoder pass. The method also combines coefficient refitting with regularization of co-active similar atoms.
1937ieHnYA.key_idea: Optimize each sample's sparse code under the current dictionary rather than estimating coefficients with one linear encoder pass.
1937ieHnYA.evidence: Experiments test recovery across 16 synthetic settings and cross-seed consistency across four vision and language settings against six SAE baselines.
1937ieHnYA.claimed_gains: Dictionary and coefficient consistency improve by 17.6% and 35.9% over the average of six SAE baselines, and by 1.9% and 13.3% over the strongest respective baselines.
1937ieHnYA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reproducible interpretability and the combination of synthetic recovery tests with vision and language evaluations.
1937ieHnYA.main_concern: Multiple reviewers request stronger comparisons with existing iterative sparse-coding and SAE methods to establish the added benefit.

yCVrq2IlGU.one_liner: Instance-specific teacher annealing blends LLM pseudo-labels with student predictions for low-resource text classification.
yCVrq2IlGU.problem: Unreliable pseudo-labels cause confirmation bias in semi-supervised learning, while persistent teacher guidance can constrain an improving student.
yCVrq2IlGU.method: AccentMatch generates initial pseudo-labels with an LLM and fuses them with student predictions. It adjusts the teacher weight for each unlabeled example according to the student's learning status, shifting toward self-training as learning stabilizes.
yCVrq2IlGU.key_idea: Weight each LLM pseudo-label against the student's prediction according to the student's learning status on that example.
yCVrq2IlGU.evidence: Experiments compare SSL and few-shot LLM baselines across six text classification benchmarks, with controls for fixed weighting, agreement filtering, linear scheduling, and teacher removal.
yCVrq2IlGU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical adaptive supervision scheme and comparisons across multiple datasets.
yCVrq2IlGU.main_concern: The experimental protocol does not explain how multilabel RCV1 and GoEmotions examples fit the single-label formulation.

j2s7UJYUU9.one_liner: Scale-tuned initialization and replay updates stabilize sparse RL, while shared parameters co-train adjacent N:M patterns.
j2s7UJYUU9.problem: Magnitude-based N:M sparse training loses performance at high sparsity in continuous-control reinforcement learning.
j2s7UJYUU9.method: The study separates actor saturation collapse from critic shocks after mask updates and addresses them with scale-tuned initialization and additional replay updates. Time-multiplexed training co-trains adjacent discrete sparsity patterns through shared parameters.
j2s7UJYUU9.key_idea: Tune initialization to prevent actor saturation, add updates after mask changes, and co-train adjacent sparsity patterns using shared parameters.
j2s7UJYUU9.evidence: Continuous-control TD3 experiments examine static and dynamic sparsity, replicate runs across seeds, and measure actual training time.
j2s7UJYUU9.claimed_gains: With increased width and a higher replay ratio, stabilized 1:8 agents achieve higher mean returns than same-width dense agents in 13 of 18 environment-buffer configurations.
j2s7UJYUU9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the diagnosis of sparse-training failures and the empirical evaluation, including measured execution time.
j2s7UJYUU9.main_concern: The efficiency comparisons do not sufficiently isolate sparsity's advantage from changes in width, replay ratio, optimizer, and implementation.

RFmvmW0JiH.one_liner: A physiology-based hidden-state simulator evaluates fitness coaches through year-long workout recommendations and wearable observations.
RFmvmW0JiH.problem: Short conversations and LLM user role-play fail to preserve trainee profiles over the long horizons required for fitness coaching.
RFmvmW0JiH.method: FitSim models coaching as a partially observable Markov decision process, projecting wearable observations from evolving physiology and adherence traits. It samples daily workout outcomes and measures coaching gain, overtraining, and injuries from simulator state.
RFmvmW0JiH.key_idea: Generate wearable observations and workout outcomes from a persistent hidden persona state with fitness-fatigue dynamics, adherence traits, and injury tracking.
RFmvmW0JiH.evidence: Year-long closed-loop evaluations compare LLM coaches with rule-based coaches and fully or partially informed oracle strategies.
RFmvmW0JiH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reproducible long-horizon evaluation without persona drift or LLM-based judging.
RFmvmW0JiH.main_concern: Reference coaches access the simulator's intent calendar while LLM coaches must infer training patterns, confounding performance comparisons.

v8bflLFYm7.one_liner: Clipped, noisy aggregate task vectors encode private image-text demonstrations for reusable multimodal in-context learning.
v8bflLFYm7.problem: Existing private in-context learning methods incur privacy costs that limit many-shot multimodal use.
v8bflLFYm7.method: DP-MTV partitions demonstrations, clips per-layer representations, and adds noise to their aggregate steering vector. It pays privacy cost during construction and reuses the released vector for inference, with a fully private head-selection variant.
v8bflLFYm7.key_idea: Privatize an aggregate steering vector from clipped demonstration representations once, then reuse that vector across inference queries.
v8bflLFYm7.evidence: Experiments span eight benchmarks and three VLM architectures, including Qwen-VL on Flowers-102 and membership-inference evaluation.
v8bflLFYm7.claimed_gains: DP-MTV matches or exceeds non-private performance on most tasks at epsilon=2, while the fully-private variant at epsilon=5 reaches 96% on Flowers-102 with Qwen-VL versus 77% for non-private MTV.
v8bflLFYm7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value reusable private task vectors and promising results across multimodal benchmarks.
v8bflLFYm7.main_concern: The sensitivity proof may omit a factor when a changed record alters a whole clipped chunk, undermining the stated privacy accounting.

Im9YwgTYhq.one_liner: Independent missingness-based group selection followed by Mondrian calibration targets coverage gaps across hospitals.
Im9YwgTYhq.problem: Marginal conformal coverage can conceal undercoverage within missingness-defined patient groups under cross-hospital distribution shift.
Im9YwgTYhq.method: The procedure selects a measurement on an independent sample, partitions patients by whether it was recorded, and calibrates each group separately. A hospital-level decomposition analyzes how pooling changes coverage through reweighting and error cancellation.
Im9YwgTYhq.key_idea: Select a measurement independently, split patients by its recording status, and apply Mondrian conformal calibration within each group.
Im9YwgTYhq.evidence: Evaluations use three predictors across eICU hospitals and MIMIC-IV care units, with site-bootstrap intervals and constructed population distributions.
Im9YwgTYhq.claimed_gains: The average worst-group coverage gap on selected groups decreases in all six settings with a median reduction of 1.9 percentage points, and paired site-bootstrap intervals exclude zero in five.
Im9YwgTYhq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clinical problem and the analysis showing how pooled evaluation can obscure hospital-level coverage behavior.
Im9YwgTYhq.main_concern: The calibration procedure adds little beyond existing missingness-conditional methods, and the selector lacks theoretical support tied to the analyzed error mechanism.

3skyGzgBET.one_liner: Latent-factor synthetic instruments and group-sparse neural IV regression identify nonlinear multi-treatment causal effects under confounding.
3skyGzgBET.problem: Estimating nonlinear causal effects of multiple treatments on an outcome under unobserved confounding is challenging when external instrumental variables are unavailable.
3skyGzgBET.method: Assuming a latent-factor treatment model and functional treatment sparsity, the authors derive synthetic instruments (SIVs) directly from the joint treatment distribution to identify nonlinear effects via a plurality rule. Sparse Neural SIV then jointly selects active treatments and estimates the structural response by matching outcomes to predictions averaged conditionally on the synthetic instruments.
3skyGzgBET.key_idea: Derive synthetic instruments from multiple treatments under a latent-factor model and fit treatment-sparse neural IV regression via plurality-rule identification.
3skyGzgBET.evidence: Estimation-error and exact-treatment-recovery theorems are paired with Gaussian and two-component mixture interaction simulations and a mouse-genomics application.
3skyGzgBET.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending synthetic instrumental variables from linear models to nonparametric nonlinear settings with sparse neural networks is timely, clearly written, and mathematically sound under its assumptions.
3skyGzgBET.main_concern: All three reviewers criticize the heavy, restrictive identification and estimation assumptions—such as additive separability, sparsity bounds, and plurality voting vulnerable to ties and misspecification—which are largely deferred to the appendix.

uUWcdKTFuv.one_liner: RASI preserves target-specific sampling geometry while applying distributionally robust optimization to uncertain proxy-label residual risks.
uUWcdKTFuv.problem: Underestimating proxy-label error can assign too few queries to important regions and inflate inferential variance.
uUWcdKTFuv.method: RASI decomposes the sampling policy into target-specific loading and uncertain residual risk. It preserves the loading while deriving minimax sampling policies over an ambiguity set of residual risks.
uUWcdKTFuv.key_idea: Robustify only residual-risk estimates while retaining the estimand-specific loading in the sampling policy.
uUWcdKTFuv.evidence: The paper derives minimax policies and reviewers report theory and experiments covering linear and nonlinear statistical targets.
uUWcdKTFuv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers support separating target geometry from unreliable residual-risk estimates when designing active sampling policies.
uUWcdKTFuv.main_concern: The assumption that target geometry is reliable needs stronger justification for nonlinear targets whose loadings depend on estimated outcome quantities.

MHbZ4D86Gz.one_liner: Measured action relations recover compatible state coordinates and executable tool laws from scalar terminal feedback.
MHbZ4D86Gz.problem: Tool systems with hidden states and no intermediate observations lack explicit structure for executing and revising computations.
MHbZ4D86Gz.method: Under projective and identifiability assumptions, the method recovers action-aligned coordinates and dynamics using noisy Lie-bracket measurements and a spectrally separated anchor. Reset constructions and retained output records enable conditional recovery of maps, local laws, and parent sets.
MHbZ4D86Gz.key_idea: Use measured action relations to align hidden-state decoding with tool dynamics, then recover dependencies through reset experiments and retained outputs.
MHbZ4D86Gz.evidence: Constructive recovery theorems give perturbation bounds and polynomial complexity, while synthetic motion and compilation experiments examine acquisition and reuse.
MHbZ4D86Gz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the concrete recovery construction and explicit error control for learning hidden structure from terminal feedback.
MHbZ4D86Gz.main_concern: The complete acquisition-to-execution pipeline lacks convincing validation under noise without supplied structural information.

qqnjmClzTz.one_liner: Urchin parameterizes key-value Gaussian mixtures with fixed components to retain nonlinear attention retrieval in a fixed-size state.
qqnjmClzTz.problem: Finite-state attention alternatives struggle with long-context recall despite competitive language modeling performance.
qqnjmClzTz.method: The framework interprets softmax attention as a Gaussian mixture over key-value pairs and replaces one component per pair with a fixed component count. This view unifies dual-state state-space models and supports new memory-update and retrieval rules.
qqnjmClzTz.key_idea: Compress the key-value density into a fixed-component Gaussian mixture while retaining softmax nonlinear retrieval.
qqnjmClzTz.evidence: Reviewers describe matched-budget dual-state model comparisons and long-context retrieval tests including NIAH-1 from RULER.
qqnjmClzTz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mixture-model interpretation and the demonstrated long-context recall gains.
qqnjmClzTz.main_concern: Missing architectural ablations leave unclear which changes cause the recall gains and how broadly those gains extend beyond simple retrieval tasks.

QKwS3S4jVv.one_liner: Exact shallow-to-deep prediction bounds characterize when limited candidate evaluations can identify Best-of-K accuracy.
QKwS3S4jVv.problem: Evaluating fewer candidates than deployment uses can leave Best-of-K performance unidentified even with abundant shallow data.
QKwS3S4jVv.method: The paper constructs systems with identical shallow ordered-label distributions and computes their maximal deeper accuracy gap. It analyzes how bounded response slopes and shared score distributions change extrapolation limits.
QKwS3S4jVv.key_idea: Match the entire shallow ordered-label law while maximizing the gap in deeper Best-of-K accuracy.
QKwS3S4jVv.evidence: Finite-budget gap theorems and assumption-specific simulations accompany evaluations on natural reward-model scores.
QKwS3S4jVv.claimed_gains: At K = 16, the maximal gap is 60 percentage points for B = 4 and under 5 for B = 8.
QKwS3S4jVv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the rigorous finite-budget characterization of shallow-to-deep uncertainty.
QKwS3S4jVv.main_concern: The practical takeaways and applicability of the recovery theory remain insufficiently established by the experiments.

WLOYkzCJ4O.one_liner: Linear probes predict future audit rewards from target-model activations to rank conversation branches during beam-search red teaming.
WLOYkzCJ4O.problem: Automated conversational audits need to choose branches likely to elicit target behaviors rather than relying only on auditor-generated continuations.
WLOYkzCJ4O.method: The paper formulates auditing as a Markov decision process and applies beam search over conversation histories. Value Probes learn linear activation readouts of discounted future judge rewards and guide branch selection.
WLOYkzCJ4O.key_idea: Rank conversation branches with linear activation probes trained to predict discounted future behavioral rewards.
WLOYkzCJ4O.evidence: Experiments cover 18 target behaviors and 3 model scales, with search ablations and probe fitting from smaller-model off-policy data.
WLOYkzCJ4O.claimed_gains: Across 18 target behaviors and 3 model scales, peak audit scores rise by roughly 50% over token-matched standard auditing.
WLOYkzCJ4O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge improved auditing performance and value controls separating search structure from branch ranking.
WLOYkzCJ4O.main_concern: Missing current-reward-only and simpler ranking controls leave the specific benefit of future-value probes unresolved.

ATCOL2wCW1.one_liner: CfactSP uses state-identifying anchor sequences and tensor geometry to learn noisy deterministic POMDPs from one reset-free trajectory.
ATCOL2wCW1.problem: Partial observability prevents directly collecting alternative action-sequence outcomes from a common hidden state without resets.
ATCOL2wCW1.method: The paper studies identifiability through joint distributions of observation sequences under different actions. For deterministic finite-state machines with bounded noise, CfactSP combines anchor sequences, tensor decomposition, and nonnegative matrix factorization to identify dynamics from a single trajectory.
ATCOL2wCW1.key_idea: Use anchor histories that determine hidden states to recover shared-state action-outcome information from a reset-free sequence.
ATCOL2wCW1.evidence: Identifiability and bounded-corruption guarantees address overlapping windows and imperfect anchors, alongside experiments on example systems.
ATCOL2wCW1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value a concrete approach to identifying partially observable systems without resets.
ATCOL2wCW1.main_concern: The counterfactual definitions and identifiability claims need clearer assumptions and more precise statements.

N2GKkZzVtf.one_liner: IDDM interpolates state retention, prior resampling, and target-directed transitions to permit corrections in discrete diffusion.
N2GKkZzVtf.problem: Masked diffusion locks in early errors, while uniform diffusion can depend too strongly on intermediate latent states.
N2GKkZzVtf.method: IDDM partially resets probability mass to a prior through a controllable resampling mechanism. Its transition rule interpolates staying, resampling, and target-directed changes while preserving marginals and separating training from inference.
N2GKkZzVtf.key_idea: Interpolate between retaining the current state, resampling the prior, and moving toward the target state.
N2GKkZzVtf.evidence: Marginal-consistency derivations accompany molecular graph and text generation experiments, including GuacaMol and OWT results discussed by reviewers.
N2GKkZzVtf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the resampling construction simple and report competitive results on graph and text generation.
N2GKkZzVtf.main_concern: The experiments do not sufficiently explain when resampling actually corrects errors or improves sample quality.

hwghymA1aM.one_liner: FloodMark uses expert-authored visual questions to test flood reasoning and distinguish supported answers from insufficient evidence.
hwghymA1aM.problem: Existing flood-scene evaluation does not adequately test fine-grained physical judgments and recognition of insufficient visual evidence.
hwghymA1aM.method: FloodMark annotates real flood and post-flood images with tasks spanning evidence quality, scene context, flood-state perception, physical reasoning, and operational reasoning. Its answer design distinguishes supported absence from inability to determine a condition.
hwghymA1aM.key_idea: Evaluate flood judgments with explicit insufficient-evidence answers across expert-authored physical and operational tasks.
hwghymA1aM.evidence: The benchmark evaluates 13 MLLMs on 1,400 images and over 16,000 human-annotated image-question pairs across 15 tasks.
hwghymA1aM.claimed_gains: Gemini 3.8 Flash reaches 73.2% accuracy, while models give specific answers in 70.0% of cases with insufficient evidence on average.
hwghymA1aM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the practical flood-assessment tasks and explicit distinction between supported absence and insufficient evidence.
hwghymA1aM.main_concern: Physical and operational labels need stronger independent validation, particularly for visually ambiguous depth, flow, and passability judgments.

0MbGPkl3uv.one_liner: Variance Path Diffusion allocates noise by region using Gamma variance paths and a Beta-thinning time-varying-rate construction.
0MbGPkl3uv.problem: Conditional generation needs spatially and temporally different noise levels that existing methods specify separately for each task.
0MbGPkl3uv.method: VPD models cumulative noise with a Gamma process centered in expectation on a nominal schedule and uses Beta thinning to construct time-varying rates with preserved marginals. A sampling-time allocation parameter controls unconditional generation, editing, and inpainting using one trained model.
0MbGPkl3uv.key_idea: Allocate regional noise through Gamma variance paths whose time-varying rates use Beta thinning to preserve marginal distributions.
0MbGPkl3uv.evidence: Gamma–Beta derivations accompany inpainting experiments on FFHQ, LSUN Bedroom, and ImageNet and motion in-betweening on HumanML3D.
0MbGPkl3uv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize useful probabilistic constructions and strong practical results for inpainting and motion in-betweening.
0MbGPkl3uv.main_concern: The theoretical claims overstate how necessary the stochastic construction and regional scheduling choices are for the practical method.

8cIJp7skPT.one_liner: Aperture stores additive Fourier moments of merged-token positions to preserve rotary states across repeated compression.
8cIJp7skPT.problem: Assigning merged tokens a single center loses phase cancellation caused by their distributed source positions.
8cIJp7skPT.method: Aperture stores pooling mass and weighted complex phase sums at each rotary frequency. Adding these states across merges recovers mean rotary multipliers without retaining source coordinates.
8cIJp7skPT.key_idea: Represent positional support with pooling mass and additive Fourier moments at the model's rotary frequencies.
8cIJp7skPT.evidence: Minimum-dimension theory accompanies five trained EPIC-Kitchens readers with 15,360 merge-order-consistent predictions and Qwen2.5-VL-7B tests on StreamingBench.
8cIJp7skPT.claimed_gains: On 2,498 StreamingBench questions, Aperture averages 71.39% accuracy versus PPE's 71.84%, with 1,024 slots storing 1.01 MiB versus 17.91 MiB of coordinates at the longest prefix.
8cIJp7skPT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the relevance of preserving positional information consistently when tokens merge.
8cIJp7skPT.main_concern: The algebraic guarantees have not translated into clear, consistent practical performance gains over simpler positional baselines.

JucyLXk0OU.one_liner: GRIT estimates unstable feature directions from invariant-pair differences and projects them out before predictor training.
JucyLXk0OU.problem: Finite, noisy invariant pairs can miss spurious variation or cause consistency penalties to discard predictive information.
JucyLXk0OU.method: GRIT estimates an unstable subspace from the covariance of pair differences in fixed pretrained features and removes the selected directions. Predictor fitting then uses the projected features with ERM or other robustness objectives.
JucyLXk0OU.key_idea: Estimate a low-rank nuisance subspace from pair-difference covariance and enforce invariance by projecting it out.
JucyLXk0OU.evidence: Target-risk bounds relate pair count, noise, coverage, and rank, with experiments across eight objectives on ColoredMNIST-INV and Waterbirds-INV.
JucyLXk0OU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the finite-noise statistical analysis and report promising OOD improvements from the projection.
JucyLXk0OU.main_concern: The guarantees rely on restrictive subspace and pair-noise assumptions whose applicability to real feature geometry remains insufficiently validated.

D0ec1PBylX.one_liner: NML matches forget-example likelihood distributions to a nonmember reference while distilling retained behavior.
D0ec1PBylX.problem: Unlearning can remove knowledge yet leave likelihood signatures that distinguish forgotten records from never-seen data.
D0ec1PBylX.method: NML caches the original model's negative log-likelihoods on nonmembers and matches the forget-example NLL distribution to that reference using energy distance. Retain-set distillation preserves utility without requiring a retrained model.
D0ec1PBylX.key_idea: Match the full forget-example NLL distribution to original-model nonmember NLLs rather than continually lowering forget likelihoods.
D0ec1PBylX.evidence: TOFU and MUSE-News evaluations use multiple likelihood-based membership attacks and question-only identification attacks.
D0ec1PBylX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find distribution matching intuitive and empirically effective at reducing identifiable unlearning signatures.
D0ec1PBylX.main_concern: The method depends on reference nonmembers having a suitable distribution for the forget set, which current validation does not establish broadly.

d1RejSWved.one_liner: KKT-informed optimality and reward-improving counterfactuals learn constraints from safe expert demonstrations using learned dynamics.
d1RejSWved.problem: Constraint learning often requires known dynamics or unsafe exploration that safe demonstrations alone do not provide.
d1RejSWved.method: CF-KKT fits local differentiable dynamics and applies KKT-inspired optimality conditions to demonstrations. It generates nearby reward-improving counterfactual behaviors as synthetic infeasible examples.
d1RejSWved.key_idea: Use locally learned dynamics to construct reward-improving counterfactuals and combine their inferred infeasibility with KKT conditions on expert demonstrations.
d1RejSWved.evidence: Maze and MuJoCo experiments evaluate constraint recovery, policy returns, and violations, while a lemma supplies a sufficient infeasibility condition under true dynamics.
d1RejSWved.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value learning safety constraints from safe demonstrations without additional risky exploration.
d1RejSWved.main_concern: The inferred infeasibility of counterfactuals relies on locally optimal demonstrations and active constraints, assumptions reviewers question in practice.

NxnQTL2qn7.one_liner: Full-game Slay the Spire evaluation probes LLM planning through horizon-dependent decisions, knowledge ablations, and cross-run memory.
NxnQTL2qn7.problem: Short episodic benchmarks poorly separate long-horizon strategic reasoning from prior knowledge and luck.
NxnQTL2qn7.method: SpireBench evaluates complete Slay the Spire runs and isolated decision puzzles. Consistent game-term renaming and cross-run memory analyses test prior knowledge and experience reuse.
NxnQTL2qn7.key_idea: Combine full-game strategic trajectories with payoff-horizon puzzles, consistent terminology renaming, and cross-run memory analyses.
NxnQTL2qn7.evidence: Experiments evaluate 20 LLMs at the highest game difficulty against heuristic and human references and analyze decision horizons and memory use.
NxnQTL2qn7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value analyses of overly cautious play and the factors underlying long-horizon performance.
NxnQTL2qn7.main_concern: Game-specific framing and terminology make the benchmark's broader relevance and accessibility unclear.

Bpd8XglXGR.one_liner: On-policy residual-state training and commitment masks adapt neural route constructors to periodic dynamic vehicle routing.
Bpd8XglXGR.problem: Static routing training misses deployment states shaped by arriving requests, prior route choices, and irreversible dispatch commitments.
Bpd8XglXGR.method: NPR represents execution histories as residual routing problems and trains on its own protocol-constrained rollouts. Commitment-Consistent Decoding intersects commitment and feasibility masks to preserve fixed route prefixes.
Bpd8XglXGR.key_idea: Train on residual states from the solver's own periodic rollouts while masking any decoding choice that violates committed route prefixes.
Bpd8XglXGR.evidence: Experiments use POMO and ReLD on 100-1,000-customer problems, 122 public DVRP instances, and transfer across demand distributions and dynamism.
Bpd8XglXGR.claimed_gains: At 1,000 customers with clustered Poisson arrivals, ReLD's gap to ALNS drops from 40.77% to 3.92%; NPR's mean gap on 122 public DVRP instances is 1.78%.
Bpd8XglXGR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the reusable residual-state interface, commitment-preserving decoding, and controlled improvements over static training.
Bpd8XglXGR.main_concern: A fixed hand-designed execution protocol leaves sensitivity to dispatch and replanning choices unexplored.

KZSwfCEkqN.one_liner: A fixed large-to-small model handoff lets a cheaper decoder continue a high-capability reasoning prefix without verification.
KZSwfCEkqN.problem: Long generations from large language models impose substantial latency, monetary cost, and energy use.
KZSwfCEkqN.method: Primed decoding asks a larger model to generate an initial prefix and a smaller model to continue at a scheduled handoff. It requires no verifier, router, retraining, or shared serving stack.
KZSwfCEkqN.key_idea: Generate the beginning of a response with a stronger model, then condition a smaller model on that prefix for unverified continuation.
KZSwfCEkqN.evidence: Evaluation covers five model pairs from two families and six reasoning, mathematics, and code benchmarks, with H200 throughput, cost, and energy measurements.
KZSwfCEkqN.claimed_gains: A 1024-token Qwen3.5-122B-A10B prefix followed by Qwen3.5-4B recovers 92% of the larger model's performance, reduces long-generation latency by 1.6–1.8×, cuts cost by 60%, and cuts energy by 68%.
KZSwfCEkqN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the handoff is simple to deploy and offers savings in favorable model and task settings.
KZSwfCEkqN.main_concern: Limited comparisons with stronger multi-model methods under matched costs leave the practical advantage insufficiently established.

JHUnaQnSCq.one_liner: Complementary token corrections and signed reconstruction weights approximate dense teacher feedback under sparse supervision.
JHUnaQnSCq.problem: Selecting fewer supervised tokens can distort on-policy distillation updates by discarding reinforcing or canceling correction contributions.
JHUnaQnSCq.method: CoRD represents teacher corrections in output-head gradient space, selects complementary directions, and assigns signed weights to reconstruct their dense mean. Theory bounds approximation error within that representation.
JHUnaQnSCq.key_idea: Select complementary correction directions and reconstruct the full mean correction with signed weights over selected tokens.
JHUnaQnSCq.evidence: Experiments cover three student models and six mathematical reasoning benchmarks, including MATH-500 and AIME 2024/2025, under matched GPU-hour caps with multiple seeds and ablations.
JHUnaQnSCq.claimed_gains: At a 25% supervised-token budget, CoRD improves macro mean@16 by 1.2–1.3 percentage points and pass@8 by 1.0–2.3 points over the strongest compared baselines.
JHUnaQnSCq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value combining direction selection with mean-contribution reconstruction and supporting it with theory and experiments.
JHUnaQnSCq.main_concern: The connection between output-head proxy reconstruction and actual LoRA updates remains insufficiently established.

ALe1JxnpCa.one_liner: Confidence-aware importance-ratio caps correct training–inference engine mismatch through bounded log-odds displacement.
ALe1JxnpCa.problem: Separate rollout and training engines assign different token probabilities, distorting RLVR policy updates.
ALe1JxnpCa.method: Calibrated Importance Sampling models engine mismatch as additive log-odds displacement and truncates large positive displacements at a constant threshold. Mapping back yields a ratio cap that tightens with token confidence.
ALe1JxnpCa.key_idea: Cap positive log-odds displacement rather than raw importance ratios, producing confidence-dependent truncation.
ALe1JxnpCa.evidence: Theory bounds the corrected second-moment term, and experiments compare three MoE models on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks with ablations and sensitivity analyses.
ALe1JxnpCa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clear mismatch characterization, simple confidence-aware correction, and supporting empirical ablations.
ALe1JxnpCa.main_concern: The numerical diagnostics do not directly establish reduced training-gradient error under correctly matched sampling conditions.

QZ2L5vOWsu.one_liner: Directional flow Jacobians and recursive trajectory bounds estimate action-distribution shifts from local visual perturbations.
QZ2L5vOWsu.problem: It remains unclear which small visual perturbations change a flow-matching VLA policy's executed action distribution.
QZ2L5vOWsu.method: The paper derives a local probabilistic bound using perturbation magnitude and direction together with conditioning Jacobians. Shared-noise coupling and recursive remainder control connect perturbed observations to generated action shifts.
QZ2L5vOWsu.key_idea: Propagate directional conditioning perturbations through the action flow using Jacobian linearization and recursively bounded remainders.
QZ2L5vOWsu.evidence: LIBERO experiments compare predicted sensitivity with observed action-distribution shifts under several classes of visual perturbations.
QZ2L5vOWsu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the coherent direction-sensitive framework connecting visual changes to action-distribution geometry.
QZ2L5vOWsu.main_concern: Finite-search numerical approximations may underestimate curvature and fail to enclose perturbed trajectories, but containment and search-budget sensitivity are unverified.

HXWNgUXeAl.one_liner: Cross-form probes and module-restricted updates diagnose unlearning transfer, with synthetic augmentation expanding forgotten query coverage.
HXWNgUXeAl.problem: Knowledge that appears removed in one query form can remain recoverable through other forms, languages, or attacks.
HXWNgUXeAl.method: The study evaluates unlearning across query formats, languages, and parameter modules, examining which updates transfer. AugUnlearning combines synthetic data augmentation with localized training to improve coverage beyond single-form unlearning.
HXWNgUXeAl.key_idea: Train and evaluate across augmented query forms while localizing updates to modules whose forgetting transfers across forms.
HXWNgUXeAl.evidence: Experiments span fourteen objectives, two model families, eight query forms, four prompt attacks, and up to eighteen languages, using a small RWKU biographical subset.
HXWNgUXeAl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing within-form paraphrase transfer from cross-form forgetting and the systematic module and language analyses.
HXWNgUXeAl.main_concern: Broad generalization and mechanism claims exceed the limited factual dataset and available controls.

46Fo90wuC2.one_liner: Paired support residuals adapt EEG queries while leave-one-out pseudo-queries suppress candidate hubness.
46Fo90wuC2.problem: Inter-subject variation limits EEG-to-image retrieval, and adapting pretrained models to unseen subjects with few examples remains underexplored.
46Fo90wuC2.method: PairCal applies support-guided EEG–image residual corrections to queries and constructs leave-one-out pseudo-unseen queries to estimate candidate-specific bias. Both components use paired support examples without updating pretrained encoders.
46Fo90wuC2.key_idea: Correct queries using paired EEG–image residuals and normalize candidate attraction using leave-one-out support-derived queries.
46Fo90wuC2.evidence: Evaluation spans held-out subjects, encoder architectures, training schemes, support sizes, repeated checkpoints and support draws, and candidate-permutation controls.
46Fo90wuC2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the clearly defined inductive adaptation setting and consistent retrieval gains without encoder updates.
46Fo90wuC2.main_concern: Targeted comparisons with existing residual adaptation and candidate-normalization methods are insufficient to establish the components' distinct contributions.

GsYrFXFdlr.one_liner: Proof-difficulty estimates normalized by statement length rank conjectures and train a theorem-generating model.
GsYrFXFdlr.problem: Increasing theorem-generation capability does not establish whether generated mathematics is interesting or useful.
GsYrFXFdlr.method: The paper defines intrinsic interestingness through proof length relative to statement length and trains a 27B proof-difficulty predictor as a practical scoring component. It optimizes a conjecturer against the metric and iteratively expands a formal library with selected theorems.
GsYrFXFdlr.key_idea: Estimate proof difficulty relative to theorem description length and use the resulting score to select and train conjectures.
GsYrFXFdlr.evidence: Experiments compare proof-difficulty prediction with general-purpose models, study interestingness and downstream utility on Mathlib, and evaluate an iterative theorem-discovery loop.
GsYrFXFdlr.claimed_gains: Optimizing the metric reduces substantial or full overlap with Mathlib from 91.9% to 30.6%.
GsYrFXFdlr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find computable proof-difficulty-based conjecture scoring a useful direction for studying mathematical discovery.
GsYrFXFdlr.main_concern: The proposed proxy lacks independent validation that higher scores represent genuinely more interesting or useful mathematics.

ubG3iePD3q.one_liner: Concurrent SSD reads and blockwise decompression–projection pipelines increase realized bandwidth for memory-constrained MoE inference.
ubG3iePD3q.problem: SSD-backed MoE inference on unified-memory devices bottlenecks on the OS-mediated storage path rather than expert computation.
ubG3iePD3q.method: XStream issues concurrent routed-expert reads and jointly tunes codec chunk size and I/O-worker count. It pipelines lossless decompression through Gate, Up, and Down projections without waiting for whole-expert materialization.
ubG3iePD3q.key_idea: Expose concurrent expert reads and consume arriving weight blocks immediately through decompression and dependent expert projections.
ubG3iePD3q.evidence: System experiments cover multiple models and two hardware platforms, with NVIDIA GB10 comparisons and component ablations for compression, reads, and pipelining.
ubG3iePD3q.claimed_gains: On NVIDIA GB10, XStream achieves 2.07–4.65× ZipMoE throughput, 1.26–1.52× ANS Serial throughput, 3.57–4.05× adapted MoE-Infinity throughput, and 1.57–1.86× the decode rate of tested Colibrì configurations.
ubG3iePD3q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the practical storage-path bottleneck and useful system implementation and evaluation evidence.
ubG3iePD3q.main_concern: The contribution beyond combining established concurrent I/O, decompression, and blockwise execution techniques remains unclear.

eyoOGAYjGE.one_liner: Structured trace-summary embeddings locate agents among reference systems to predict benchmark scores from few executions.
eyoOGAYjGE.problem: Binary correctness alone discards agent-trajectory information that could improve low-budget benchmark estimation.
eyoOGAYjGE.method: The method embeds LLM-generated structured trace summaries and constructs low-dimensional reference-system representations. It predicts a new system's score from this geometry and combines that estimate with an item-response model.
eyoOGAYjGE.key_idea: Embed rubric-structured execution summaries and use reference-system geometry to augment item-response-based score estimation.
eyoOGAYjGE.evidence: SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0 experiments compare limited-task estimation against sample averages and IRT-only methods, including leave-one-family-out evaluation.
eyoOGAYjGE.claimed_gains: With one random executed task, mean absolute error falls from 0.13 to 0.08 on SWE-bench Verified (Wilcoxon p < 10^{-4}) and from 0.14 to 0.12 on Terminal-Bench 2.0 (Wilcoxon p < 10^{-3}).
eyoOGAYjGE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that structured trace representations improve benchmark-score prediction under very small execution budgets.
eyoOGAYjGE.main_concern: Missing matched controls and stronger trace-based estimators leave the value of behavioral trace geometry beyond outcome cues insufficiently isolated.

JL7KZXx8eT.one_liner: Pose-conditioned multi-view diffusion generates consistent directional views and assembles them into HDR illumination panoramas.
JL7KZXx8eT.problem: Sparse captures omit light sources, while existing generative lighting methods do not fully use camera poses to estimate illumination at arbitrary query locations.
JL7KZXx8eT.method: A multi-view diffusion model jointly generates views covering all directions from sparse posed LDR frames, enforcing agreement with each other and the observations. These views form an HDR panorama, with the learned prior filling unobserved regions.
JL7KZXx8eT.key_idea: Condition jointly generated panoramic views on posed observations and a query location, using a learned prior for unseen directions.
JL7KZXx8eT.evidence: Evaluation includes single-image lighting estimation on Poly Haven and both Laval benchmarks, additional-frame studies, and moving-camera captures at varying distances.
JL7KZXx8eT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value estimating query-location lighting from sparse posed observations and report useful single-image reconstruction results.
JL7KZXx8eT.main_concern: Missing matched multi-frame baselines, especially LuxDiT's video mode, leave the claimed multi-view advantage insufficiently established.

C2FeOFeSia.one_liner: Minimum-surprisal best-of-N sampling selects reasoning outputs using the base model's own length-normalized probabilities.
C2FeOFeSia.problem: Complex inference-time sampling methods incur substantial compute costs when improving reasoning without training.
C2FeOFeSia.method: Generate multiple candidate solutions and select the sequence with the lowest surprisal rate, using length-normalized negative log-likelihood without an external verifier.
C2FeOFeSia.key_idea: Rank sampled reasoning sequences by length-normalized negative log-likelihood and return the least surprising sequence.
C2FeOFeSia.evidence: Reviews describe comparisons across three models and two benchmarks, while the abstract reports reasoning comparisons with MCMC and reinforcement learning.
C2FeOFeSia.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the method offers a simple, effective inference-time alternative to more complex sampling.
C2FeOFeSia.main_concern: Reviewers question the theoretical guarantees and their connection to the practical sampling algorithm.

2hHLXzCNaY.one_liner: AssetArena connects industrial evidence, tools, and operational actions in executable MCP workflows with replayable evaluations.
2hHLXzCNaY.problem: Industrial agent benchmarks usually test isolated capabilities rather than complete stateful asset-operation workflows.
2hHLXzCNaY.method: AssetArena combines heterogeneous evidence and operational tools in an MCP environment where agents acquire information interactively. An evidence-first construction process establishes independent reference outcomes and records executions for replay.
2hHLXzCNaY.key_idea: Require interactive evidence acquisition and operational actions within isolated, replayable workflows scored against independently established reference outcomes.
2hHLXzCNaY.evidence: The benchmark evaluates eight language-model configurations on 231 human-authored, machine-verified scenarios using 85 tools across six MCP servers.
2hHLXzCNaY.claimed_gains: Models achieve 16.5--29.9% Pass@1 across the benchmark.
2hHLXzCNaY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the expert-built industrial workflows and executable environment for evaluating realistic agent behavior.
2hHLXzCNaY.main_concern: Reviewers question evaluation reliability because of overlapping evidence bundles, insufficient reference validation, and inconsistent reported counts.

Pu6WmLmVI6.one_liner: An intraclass correlation metric isolates prompt-formulation dependence by subtracting decoding noise from correctness variation.
Pu6WmLmVI6.problem: Existing prompt-sensitivity metrics conflate formulation effects with specificity and stochastic decoding.
Pu6WmLmVI6.method: The study varies formulation and specificity, analyzes ten metrics with principal component analysis, and introduces rho_F. This intraclass correlation measures correctness variation across formulations after subtracting within-prompt decoding noise.
Pu6WmLmVI6.key_idea: Decompose correctness variation across prompt formulations and repeated answers to subtract decoding noise from formulation dependence.
Pu6WmLmVI6.evidence: The abstract reports AmbigQA and AMBROSIA experiments on seven open-weight models with 7 to 72 billion parameters and held-out AmbigQA checks.
Pu6WmLmVI6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the relevant problem and detailed statistical analysis of prompt-sensitivity metrics.
Pu6WmLmVI6.main_concern: Reviewers consider the methodological contribution incremental relative to established intraclass correlation and correctness-based variance decomposition.

S0XkbS65HP.one_liner: MOSE selects features across multiple history windows while retaining causal-graph-derived state variables for deep reinforcement learning.
S0XkbS65HP.problem: Raw observations lack guaranteed Markovian states, and minimal causal states alone may train poorly in neural reinforcement learning.
S0XkbS65HP.method: A graph-based procedure constructs a proposed minimal Markovian state, while MOSE feeds multiple history orders to a shared Q-function through an attention selector. Causal MOSE forces the selector to retain every minimal-state variable while allowing redundant inputs.
S0XkbS65HP.key_idea: Select value-relevant features across history orders while forcing retention of the causal graph's minimal-state variables.
S0XkbS65HP.evidence: The paper presents state-construction theory and empirical comparisons of minimal states, window states, and MOSE, including synthetic settings discussed in reviews.
S0XkbS65HP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question of sufficient states and useful redundancy worthwhile for neural reinforcement learning.
S0XkbS65HP.main_concern: Reviewers agree that an extra gradient update in Causal MOSE confounds attribution of gains to state selection.

DgTx3hQKsk.one_liner: Neural Evidence Transport transfers frequency-normalized brain-decoder probabilities through an audio-derived bridge between speech token vocabularies.
DgTx3hQKsk.problem: A brain decoder trained for one speech vocabulary cannot directly supply evidence to another without refitting.
DgTx3hQKsk.method: NET divides source-token probabilities by reference frequencies and averages the resulting ratios through a soft bridge estimated from audio. Context-dependent fusion weights update target priors after selection on development participants.
DgTx3hQKsk.key_idea: Transport source probability-to-frequency ratios through an audio-derived token bridge before updating target priors.
DgTx3hQKsk.evidence: The study proves neutral-evidence preservation and a chi-square contrast identity, then tests MEG with 11 held-out LibriBrain100 participants and EEG with 14 held-out participants.
DgTx3hQKsk.claimed_gains: Transport retains 97% of Ridge's improvement over the prior for HuBERT and achieves 60.6% attended-speaker accuracy over 12 seconds (95% confidence interval: 56.4--65.6%).
DgTx3hQKsk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematically specified frequency correction and careful evaluation of decoder reuse.
DgTx3hQKsk.main_concern: Reviewers agree that testing only two compatible 256-state HuBERT and Wav2Vec2 vocabularies leaves broader tokenizer generality unestablished.

UHAm6gUKSD.one_liner: Minimal-edit distillation corrects teacher-disfavored tokens in failed student rollouts while reinforcing successful multimodal reasoning trajectories.
UHAm6gUKSD.problem: Small vision-language models can misread diagrams, causing subsequent mathematical reasoning to proceed from incorrect premises.
UHAm6gUKSD.method: A teacher uses training-only figure descriptions and verified solutions to score incorrect student rollouts under a minimal-edit objective. Only teacher-disfavored tokens receive corrective loss, while correct rollouts receive task-reward reinforcement learning.
UHAm6gUKSD.key_idea: A token-level sign mask restricts corrective distillation to teacher-disfavored parts of the student's own incorrect rollout.
UHAm6gUKSD.evidence: Experiments use small Qwen-family VLMs on mathematics and perception benchmarks, with token-mask ablations and a frozen same-size teacher setting.
UHAm6gUKSD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the corrective mechanism simple and computationally economical because the teacher scores student rollouts without generating solutions.
UHAm6gUKSD.main_concern: Evaluation on small, older models from one family leaves transfer to stronger starting models uncertain.

qbrzKui3oE.one_liner: Controlled comparisons and bootstrap tests examine whether nonlinear recurrence and state tracking improve time-series forecasting over linear recurrence.
qbrzKui3oE.problem: Reported gains from expressive recurrent architectures do not establish whether recurrence expressivity itself improves forecasting.
qbrzKui3oE.method: The study compares recurrent families with different transition complexity and state-tracking capabilities using controlled synthetic and real-world forecasting tasks. Bootstrap hypothesis tests and multi-seed evaluations assess whether increased expressivity produces reliable accuracy gains.
qbrzKui3oE.key_idea: Comparing recurrence families under controlled forecasting protocols separates transition expressivity from observed predictive accuracy.
qbrzKui3oE.evidence: Experiments cover 12 recurrent models on synthetic tasks, LTSF, and GIFT-Eval, including comparisons within model families and equal-shot hyperparameter search.
qbrzKui3oE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the well-motivated question and broad, carefully structured comparisons across recurrent architectures and forecasting datasets.
qbrzKui3oE.main_concern: The study does not sufficiently explain which architectural biases or dataset properties actually determine forecasting performance.

rOWAmFiBjE.one_liner: Trains flow-matching return-distribution critics by enforcing Bellman consistency across all intermediate noise levels.
rOWAmFiBjE.problem: Bootstrapped value learning in offline reinforcement learning with limited data and sparse rewards extracts weak supervision signals and often suffers from return-distribution collapse.
rOWAmFiBjE.method: Value Forcing models return distributions via flow matching and applies a Flow Bellman operator that enforces Bellman consistency between marginal distributions at every intermediate noise level rather than only at clean endpoints. The authors instantiate an actor-critic variant (VF) and an expectile-weighted implicit value-learning variant (IVF).
rOWAmFiBjE.key_idea: Enforces distributional Bellman consistency across all intermediate flow-matching noise levels to supervise return-distribution estimation from limited transitions.
rOWAmFiBjE.evidence: Supported by contraction proofs for the Flow Bellman operator and empirical evaluation of VF and IVF across 26 long-horizon offline RL tasks and policy-evaluation diagnostics.
rOWAmFiBjE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the intermediate-noise Flow Bellman operator and its contraction analysis well-motivated, backed by broad offline RL experiments and ablations.
rOWAmFiBjE.main_concern: Experiments lack ablations isolating intermediate-noise supervision from shared-noise boundary coupling (PCBF) as well as classical distributional RL baselines like C51 and IQN, while distribution-accuracy diagnostics are localized.

TToNLahVXD.one_liner: Benchmarks LLM agents on auditing agent-harness source code using 170 verified historical vulnerability re-injection tasks.
TToNLahVXD.problem: LLM agent harnesses execute model outputs as authenticated actions, creating code-level security vulnerabilities that model alignment cannot fix and crash or unit testing often misses.
TToNLahVXD.method: HarnessSecGym compiles 313 historical vulnerabilities from 14 open-source agent harnesses into 170 source-code review tasks (including unmodified clean controls) verified via defect re-injection and differential security tests across three repository scopes.
TToNLahVXD.key_idea: Re-injects verified historical vulnerabilities with differential security tests into full agent-harness repositories across three localization scopes to evaluate code-review agents.
TToNLahVXD.evidence: Evaluates six agent configurations pairing four frontier LLMs with five harnesses (including Claude Code, OpenCode, and Pi) across 170 review tasks from 14 open-source harness repositories.
TToNLahVXD.claimed_gains: Evaluated frontier agent configurations miss 19% to 33% of planted harness vulnerabilities even when the task explicitly names the defective file.
TToNLahVXD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that auditing security boundaries in agent-harness code is a timely, underexplored problem and commend grounding tasks in real historical fixes verified by differential tests and controls.
TToNLahVXD.main_concern: Grading relies on a single LLM judge validated on only 20 reports that overlaps in model and harness with evaluated systems and shows unexplained harness-dependent false-alarm rates on clean controls.

KAnuHtIqqk.one_liner: Steers inference-time flow-matching sampling under hard terminal constraints via receding-horizon primal-dual control and terminal flow-map prediction.
KAnuHtIqqk.problem: Inference-time steering of pretrained flow-matching models lacks a tractable way to simultaneously maximize rewards, satisfy hard terminal constraints, and minimize deviation from pretrained dynamics.
KAnuHtIqqk.method: ConicFlow formulates constrained sampling as a discretized optimal control problem solved over short sliding windows via a receding-horizon primal-dual algorithm with persistent dual multipliers. A terminal-estimate variant (RH-T) evaluates rewards and constraints at flow-map-predicted terminal states to avoid local horizon-truncation errors.
KAnuHtIqqk.key_idea: Solves short-window primal-dual optimal control subproblems during flow-matching inference while evaluating objectives and hard constraints on flow-map-predicted terminal samples.
KAnuHtIqqk.evidence: Supported by finite-horizon suboptimality bounds (including sharper bounds under convex-affine structure) and experiments in low-dimensional settings and high-dimensional image generation with FLUX.1-dev.
KAnuHtIqqk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ConicFlow offers a clean, unified optimal-control formulation of reward maximization and hard terminal feasibility, strengthened by terminal flow-map estimation.
KAnuHtIqqk.main_concern: Theoretical guarantees rely on idealized affine dynamics and convex-concave assumptions violated by neural flow models and perceptual rewards, while image evaluations cover very few prompt-seed instances.

wcQVK7UR0H.one_liner: Co-designs a 2.5-bit two-level-scale quantization format with a W2A16 grouped GEMM kernel for MoE serving.
wcQVK7UR0H.problem: Mixture-of-Experts LLM serving is bottlenecked by expert weight memory and bandwidth, yet existing two-bit compression formats lack efficient grouped GEMM kernels while kernel-friendly formats stop at four bits.
wcQVK7UR0H.method: ULMoE introduces a 2.5-bits-per-weight quantization format using two-level integer group scales whose metadata for 64 weights packs into a single aligned 32-bit word. It pairs this uniform layout with a custom W2A16 grouped GEMM kernel integrated into SGLang.
wcQVK7UR0H.key_idea: Packs two-level integer scale metadata for 64 weights at 2.5 bits per weight into one aligned 32-bit word for W2A16 grouped GEMM execution.
wcQVK7UR0H.evidence: Evaluated across seven Mixture-of-Experts models from three families (including Qwen3.5-122B in SGLang on RTX PRO 6000 and L40S GPUs) on accuracy, reasoning, kernel latency, and serving throughput.
wcQVK7UR0H.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the practical algorithm-system co-design, the roofline analysis of sparse grouped GEMMs, and systematic accuracy and end-to-end serving evaluations across multiple MoE families.
wcQVK7UR0H.main_concern: Comparisons omit GPTQ-Int4 accuracy tables alongside codebook/rotation baselines, do not separate byte-reduction gains from kernel efficiency, and test synthetic workloads on non-HBM GPUs.

OTOqU3N8nf.one_liner: Augments MeanFlow trajectory generation with step-size-aware affine control barrier constraints for arbitrary-step safe robotic planning.
OTOqU3N8nf.problem: Flow-matching robotic planners rely on slow multi-step sampling and lack formal mechanisms to enforce unseen hard safety constraints at test time.
OTOqU3N8nf.method: ASAP combines MeanFlow few- or one-step trajectory generation with a virtual control input constrained by a step-size-aware affine control barrier function solved via quadratic programming at test time without retraining.
OTOqU3N8nf.key_idea: Applies an affine control barrier constraint scaled by the sampling step size to steer MeanFlow trajectory generation into safe sets.
OTOqU3N8nf.evidence: Evaluated without retraining under unseen test-time constraints on navigation, locomotion, manipulation, and dexterous manipulation benchmarks (Maze2d, Hopper, KUKA, Adroit) and a real-world robot obstacle handover task.
OTOqU3N8nf.claimed_gains: Plans at least 20x faster than safety-guaranteed baselines on navigation, locomotion, and manipulation, 2x faster on dexterous manipulation, and in 0.04 s per plan (over 200x faster) on real-world robot handover.
OTOqU3N8nf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ASAP delivers substantial planning speedups while reliably enforcing unseen test-time safety constraints across simulated benchmarks and real-robot hardware.
OTOqU3N8nf.main_concern: Reviewers show that formal safety for arbitrary step counts reduces to projecting only the final generated sample onto the safe set, leaving intermediate-step barrier corrections theoretically redundant and unablated.

ibzsoUqJYP.one_liner: Establishes uniform-in-time Neural Tangent Kernel stability for wide classification networks via parameter regularization or full-support targets.
ibzsoUqJYP.problem: Unregularized cross-entropy training with one-hot labels on separable data drives logits to infinity, causing wide neural networks to leave the constant Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) regime.
ibzsoUqJYP.method: Treating softmax within the function-space cross-entropy loss, the authors prove uniform-in-time NTK stability and linearization closeness under gradient flow when either parameter-space regularization is applied or target class probabilities are strictly positive. They use this linearization to characterize converged solutions implicitly via the NTK and compare initialization-induced ensemble variance against Bayesian Laplace approximations.
ibzsoUqJYP.key_idea: Preserves constant-NTK linearization uniformly over infinite training time in cross-entropy gradient flow via parameter-space regularization or strictly positive target class probabilities.
ibzsoUqJYP.evidence: Supported by infinite-horizon gradient-flow linearization proofs and illustrative visual comparisons.
ibzsoUqJYP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly establishes uniform-in-time NTK linearization guarantees for cross-entropy classification, filling an infinite-horizon gap left by finite-time analyses.
ibzsoUqJYP.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing quantitative experiments, unaddressed potentially exponential width requirements, and mathematical errors in the Bayesian covariance scale conversion and unregularized softmax logit gauge.

KIVY3wrEwO.one_liner: Combines random-allocation batch sampling, GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo privacy accounting, and amplification-aware matrix optimization for DP-BandMF.
KIVY3wrEwO.problem: Differentially private banded matrix factorization (DP-BandMF) relies on suboptimal Poisson-inspired batching, slow Monte Carlo privacy accounting, and noise correlation matrices tuned independently of sampling amplification.
KIVY3wrEwO.method: The authors design random-allocation-inspired batch selection schemes compatible with b-banded correlated noise, derive GPU-parallelizable recurrences to accelerate O(1/delta) Monte Carlo privacy accounting, and jointly optimize the Toeplitz correlation matrix and bandwidth with the sampling scheme.
KIVY3wrEwO.key_idea: Pairs random-allocation batch schedules with GPU-accelerated Monte Carlo privacy-loss sampling and joint optimization of banded noise correlation matrices under sampling amplification.
KIVY3wrEwO.evidence: Evaluated via theoretical privacy proofs and certified Monte Carlo prefix-sum RMSE comparisons against Poisson and Balls-in-Bins batching baselines.
KIVY3wrEwO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean privacy analysis connecting random-allocation participation control with banded correlated-noise accounting and certified Monte Carlo calibration.
KIVY3wrEwO.main_concern: Evaluations report only analytical prefix-sum RMSE without any neural-network training experiments and apply joint correlation-matrix optimization only to the proposed samplers rather than baseline batchers.

kGt4miGhQH.one_liner: Evaluates multimodal LLMs on closed-loop active perception, locomotion, and manipulation across 29 OmniGibson spatial subcategories.
kGt4miGhQH.problem: Existing spatial intelligence benchmarks evaluate passive reasoning over pre-collected oracle views rather than an embodied agent's ability to actively acquire observations that resolve occlusion, containment, and physical dynamics.
kGt4miGhQH.method: ESI-Bench constructs an interactive benchmark in OmniGibson spanning 10 categories and 29 subcategories grounded in Spelke's core knowledge systems, requiring agents to sequence perception, locomotion, and manipulation actions to gather evidence before answering.
kGt4miGhQH.key_idea: Places multimodal models inside an interactive OmniGibson perception-action loop where occluded spatial and physical properties must be uncovered through sequenced actions.
kGt4miGhQH.evidence: Evaluates MLLMs in OmniGibson across 10 task categories and 29 subcategories comparing single-view, passive multi-view, reference-trajectory, and active-exploration conditions.
kGt4miGhQH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the broad, cognitively grounded task taxonomy and controlled comparisons between passive multi-view and active embodied exploration.
kGt4miGhQH.main_concern: Reviewers flag a discrepancy where 3D grounding results discussed as empirical findings are labeled hypothetical in a table caption, alongside final-answer accuracy not separating chance guesses from evidence-backed exploration.

yybcQGbRlW.one_liner: Transfers norm-preserved dominant singular directions of isolated LLM reinforcement-learning weight updates into vision-language model language modules.
yybcQGbRlW.problem: Endpoint-based model merging from reasoning LLMs to vision-language models mixes pre-existing parameter differences with RL post-training changes, while full RL weight updates contain non-transferable directions.
yybcQGbRlW.method: Selective-RL subtracts the pre-RL LLM checkpoint to isolate the RL-stage weight delta, extracts its dominant matrix-wise singular directions via SVD while rescaling to preserve update magnitude, and adds them to a recipient VLM's language backbone without gradient training.
yybcQGbRlW.key_idea: Isolates the RL-stage parameter update and transfers its magnitude-preserved dominant matrix-wise directions into the language modules of a recipient VLM.
yybcQGbRlW.evidence: Evaluated across three model families (including Qwen3-VL) and five visual-reasoning benchmarks (including MathVision) with matched controls for random directions, trailing directions, rank, and norm scaling.
yybcQGbRlW.claimed_gains: Outperforms full-update interpolation in 12 of 15 benchmark-family comparisons, including an 8.55 percentage-point gain on MathVision for the Qwen recipient.
yybcQGbRlW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating RL-stage updates from pre-existing backbone differences is clean and well-supported by controlled rank, direction, and scaling ablations.
yybcQGbRlW.main_concern: The method combines established SVD filtering and norm-rescaling merging techniques incrementally, and its practical benefit over directly RL-training the VLM is unclear when donor LLMs are trained from scratch for transfer.

IIo9hOJ96u.one_liner: Lifts generalized coordinates into linearly transforming features to parameterize symmetry-invariant neural Lagrangians with Noether conservation guarantees.
IIo9hOJ96u.problem: Standard Lagrangian Neural Networks operating in generalized coordinates do not enforce spatial symmetries, leading to drift in physically conserved momenta during rollout.
IIo9hOJ96u.method: Equivariant Lagrangian Neural Networks (EqLNNs) map nonlinear generalized coordinates and velocities into lifted features with linear transformation laws and pass them through an equivariant architecture to predict a symmetry-invariant scalar Lagrangian. Dynamics derived via the Euler-Lagrange equations then satisfy the corresponding Noether conservation laws when the learned Lagrangian is regular.
IIo9hOJ96u.key_idea: Lifts nonlinear generalized coordinates and velocities to features with linear transformation laws so an equivariant network outputs a symmetry-invariant scalar Lagrangian.
IIo9hOJ96u.evidence: Evaluated across five dynamical systems spanning translations, articulated and rigid-body systems, and external fields against matched lifted LNNs and earlier Lagrangian baselines.
IIo9hOJ96u.claimed_gains: Improves over a lifted LNN on four of five systems, achieving 2.4 to 52.5 times lower median trajectory MAE on free-body systems and bounding enforced-symmetry momentum drift to at most 5.7e-4.
IIo9hOJ96u.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the mathematically principled integration of generalized coordinates, equivariant feature lifting, and Noether conservation guarantees, validated against matched lifted-LNN controls.
IIo9hOJ96u.main_concern: Experiments omit recent symmetry-preserving Lagrangian baselines (such as Müller 2023), rely on small noiseless systems without many-body scaling, and under-analyze failure cases like CoupledPendulum.

O5wP85WFVL.one_liner: Studies covert accomplice discovery among LLM agents over monitored public channels using mutual-identification games and strategic vagueness.
O5wP85WFVL.problem: Prior multi-agent LLM collusion studies assume scheming agents already know their accomplices, overlooking how hidden collaborators initially identify one another over publicly monitored communication channels.
O5wP85WFVL.method: The authors design a public-channel mutual-identification game in which two scheming agents must recognize each other while completing an ordinary task alongside benign agents and an external monitor, complemented by a controlled coordination experiment varying message indirectness.
O5wP85WFVL.key_idea: Tests public task-compatible handshake messages at intermediate indirectness where monitor punishment drops faster than prospective partner coordination.
O5wP85WFVL.evidence: Evaluated with LLM agents and monitors in a public mutual-identification game (including strategy-unspecified conditions) and a controlled message-explicitness coordination experiment.
O5wP85WFVL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that investigating covert accomplice discovery without pre-shared identities addresses an important, previously overlooked prerequisite to multi-agent LLM collusion.
O5wP85WFVL.main_concern: The paper assumes rather than formally derives an information or detection-threshold asymmetry between prospective partners and public monitors observing identical transcripts, and relies on stylized prompted-schemer setups.

MAadrlBbnT.one_liner: Uses eleven procedural Blender environments to benchmark VLMs on field-work photograph acceptability and physical-state documentation.
MAadrlBbnT.problem: Evaluating vision-language models on assisting and documenting unconstrained physical field work is impeded by proprietary real-world data and uncontrolled visual variability.
MAadrlBbnT.method: RealityBench procedurally simulates rooftop solar installation and vehicle repair scenarios across eleven Blender environments with controllable camera pose, blur, visibility, and object state. It evaluates VLMs on two tasks: judging whether an image is acceptable proof-of-work and extracting fine-grained task documentation such as measurements and part states.
MAadrlBbnT.key_idea: Simulates unconstrained physical work across eleven Blender environments with controllable camera and scene state to evaluate proof-of-work photo acceptability and visual documentation.
MAadrlBbnT.evidence: Evaluates 26 vision-language models across eleven simulated Blender environments spanning rooftop solar installation and vehicle repair, plus a small real-image transfer check on three documentation questions.
MAadrlBbnT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating proof-of-work photograph acceptability from state extraction in controllable procedural 3D scenes provides useful fine-grained diagnostics of VLM perceptual failures.
MAadrlBbnT.main_concern: Real-world transfer validation covers only three static documentation questions with model-dependent truncation exclusions and omits acceptability, while acceptability ground truth relies largely on author raters across just two work domains.

V4fFofbqKX.one_liner: Proves exponential relative Fisher-divergence contraction for continuous reverse SDEs and averaged Fisher stationarity bounds for discretized samplers.
V4fFofbqKX.problem: Diffusion sampling theory lacks a data-convexity-free first-order stationarity framework analogous to gradient-norm guarantees in nonconvex optimization across both overdamped and underdamped dynamics.
V4fFofbqKX.method: The authors prove explicit exponential contraction of relative (and twisted) Fisher divergences along continuous reverse-time SDEs of overdamped and underdamped Langevin diffusions whenever the forward stationary potential is strongly convex. They then derive averaged Fisher-divergence stationarity bounds for discretized samplers using exact scores.
V4fFofbqKX.key_idea: Uses strong convexity of the forward stationary potential to contract relative Fisher divergence along reverse Langevin SDEs and bound averaged discretized Fisher error.
V4fFofbqKX.evidence: Supported by continuous-time contraction and discrete-time stationarity theorems for overdamped and underdamped Langevin reverse diffusions, validated numerically on Gaussian-mixture and CelebA experiments.
V4fFofbqKX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear theoretical framework extending Fisher-divergence contraction and discretized stationarity guarantees to both overdamped and underdamped reverse-time SDEs.
V4fFofbqKX.main_concern: Discretized bounds reintroduce restrictive uniform score-Lipschitz and sub-Gaussian data assumptions that blow up at small noise levels, while Fisher contraction neither guarantees global mode recovery nor addresses score-estimation error.

XbsphS97LG.one_liner: Separates environmental premises from expected behaviors using a per-query strategy DSL for online long-horizon agent error recovery.
XbsphS97LG.problem: Online error recovery in long-horizon agents fails when methods refine execution without recognizing that an underlying assumption about partially observable environmental preconditions is false.
XbsphS97LG.method: ALTER decomposes task specifications into environmental premises and expected behaviors alongside a lightweight per-query domain-specific language (DSL) of alternative and combinable strategies. When an attempt stalls or fails, ALTER diagnoses whether to recalibrate actor execution or revise an environmental premise and switch strategies.
XbsphS97LG.key_idea: Pairs explicit environmental-premise specifications with a per-query strategy DSL so stalled agents can revise inaccurate environment assumptions or recalibrate actor execution.
XbsphS97LG.evidence: Evaluated on filtered subsets of three long-horizon benchmarks (BrowseCompPlus, DeepSearchQA, and CVE-Bench) across three actor models against unrecovered agents and five error-recovery baselines.
XbsphS97LG.claimed_gains: Improves task success by 5.9–47.1% across three long-horizon benchmarks and three actor models.
XbsphS97LG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating execution failures from false environmental premises provides a well-motivated and actionable framework for online agent recovery.
XbsphS97LG.main_concern: Main benchmark splits are small (17–28 filtered cases per benchmark) and lack confidence intervals or significance tests, while recovery depends on explicit yield triggers and incurs extra LLM calls.
