iid140ahZn.one_liner: Applies automated neuron-level circuit discovery to graph neural networks trained on classical graph algorithms.
iid140ahZn.problem: Neural algorithmic reasoning studies whether graph neural networks align with classical algorithms, but lacks granular mechanistic tools to identify neuron-level circuits, multi-task reuse, and shortcuts.
iid140ahZn.method: MINAR adapts gradient-based automated circuit discovery to extract sparse neuron-level subgraphs inside algorithmic reasoning GNNs. Through three case studies, the authors analyze circuit formation and pruning over training, shared component reuse in multi-task GNNs, and circuit-guided model editing.
iid140ahZn.key_idea: Identifies sparse neuron-level computational circuits inside algorithmic reasoning graph neural networks to analyze circuit formation, multi-task reuse, and model editing.
iid140ahZn.evidence: Demonstrated across three GNN algorithmic reasoning case studies covering Bellman-Ford shortest paths, multi-task graph algorithm circuit sharing, and model editing.
iid140ahZn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that applying automated circuit discovery to algorithmic GNNs is a promising, underexplored direction and find the Bellman-Ford minimal-circuit recovery convincing.
iid140ahZn.main_concern: Strong validation is confined to simple architectures tailored to Bellman-Ford, whereas multi-task experiments exhibit weak base GNN performance and low circuit-characterization scores alongside notation and baseline-runtime gaps.

kvzlRwS73X.one_liner: Shrinks forget-dominant weight coordinates in closed form using QR-orthonormalized generalized eigenvectors of forget-versus-retain layer activation moments.
kvzlRwS73X.problem: Optimization-based LLM unlearning requires iterative gradient tuning to balance suppressing forget-set knowledge against preserving general retain capabilities.
kvzlRwS73X.method: Rotation-First Unlearning (RFU) collects forget and retain layer activation second-moment matrices in a single forward pass, solves a generalized eigenproblem for forget-over-retain energy, orthonormalizes the basis via QR while preserving nested leading subspaces, and applies closed-form coordinate shrinkage to model weights. It also derives a first-order retain-damage bound and a spectral concentration diagnostic, and can serve as a warm start for gradient-based unlearning.
kvzlRwS73X.key_idea: Rotates layer weights into a Euclidean-orthonormalized generalized eigenbasis ordered by forget-over-retain activation energy and attenuates leading forget-aligned weight coordinates in closed form.
kvzlRwS73X.evidence: Evaluated standalone and as a warm start on TOFU, MUSE, and WMDP across Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral models (up to ~8B parameters), alongside basis ablations.
kvzlRwS73X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, gradient-free linear-algebraic formulation, bounded closed-form weight edit, and broad evaluation across multiple unlearning benchmarks and model families.
kvzlRwS73X.main_concern: Shrinkage factors derived in the generalized eigenbasis lose their exact per-direction forget-to-retain Rayleigh-quotient guarantees once applied after QR orthonormalization, alongside close overlap with prior subspace unlearning methods.

71qICnn2Mj.one_liner: Analyzes via synthetic subject-grammar-attribute pretraining and attention-only constructions how implicit-inference fine-tuning unlocks in-context recall of pretrained facts.
71qICnn2Mj.problem: Transformers pretrained on open-ended text store factual associations in weights yet often fail to retrieve those facts in novel in-context prompt formats lacking pretraining surface cues.
71qICnn2Mj.method: Using a controlled synthetic corpus of subject-grammar-attribute sequences where attribute types correlate with grammar statistics, the authors study when pretrained Transformers fail at grammar-free in-context recall and what fine-tuning tasks unlock cross-subject transfer. They complement empirical representation analyses with an analytical construction and training-dynamics study of an attention-only Transformer.
71qICnn2Mj.key_idea: Fine-tuning on implicit attribute-type inference over a subset of subjects induces low-dimensional latent attribute-type encodings that enable contextual recall on held-out subjects.
71qICnn2Mj.evidence: Evaluated in a controlled synthetic subject-grammar-attribute framework with held-out-subject and cross-format transfer tests alongside an analytical attention-only Transformer construction.
71qICnn2Mj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean synthetic design and held-out-subject experiments that separate in-weight fact memorization from learning a transferable in-context access mechanism.
71qICnn2Mj.main_concern: Sequence-length and prompt-format mismatches between pretraining and ICL confound causal attributions to grammar statistics, while conceptual gains over prior task-vector and knowledge-extraction work remain modest.

D60Az2aOBR.one_liner: Aligns LoRA-adapted vision encoders with normalized class prototypes averaged over multiple forensic text prompts for fake-image detection.
D60Az2aOBR.problem: Contrastive VLM-based AI-generated image detectors using single-token class labels or per-image captions rely on narrow supervision cues that generalize poorly across unseen image generators.
D60Az2aOBR.method: Prompt Prototype Learning (PPL) encodes multiple manually designed text prompts describing texture, boundary consistency, and semantic realism for each class and averages their normalized embeddings into stable class prototypes. A LoRA-adapted vision encoder is aligned against these prototypes using only four-category ProGAN training data and runs vision-only at inference.
D60Az2aOBR.key_idea: Encodes and averages multiple artifact- and realism-focused prompts per class into normalized prototype embeddings to supervise LoRA-adapted contrastive vision encoders.
D60Az2aOBR.evidence: Trained on four-category ProGAN images (using PE-Core-G/14 and CLIP ViT-L/14 backbones in ablations) and evaluated on UniversalFakeDetect plus four additional cross-generator and real-world transmission benchmarks.
D60Az2aOBR.claimed_gains: Trained only on four-category ProGAN data, PPL achieves 97.3% mACC and 99.8% mAP on UniversalFakeDetect and 94.1% mACC and 97.7% mAP across four additional unseen-generator datasets.
D60Az2aOBR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-prompt prototype formulation is simple, incurs zero extra inference cost, and achieves strong cross-generator detection accuracy from limited ProGAN training data.
D60Az2aOBR.main_concern: Methodological novelty over CLIP prompt ensembling and C2P-CLIP is incremental, and headline gains are confounded by switching to a much larger 1.88B PE-Core-G/14 vision backbone.

IW0aL7JYuC.one_liner: Augments each Transformer layer with a parallel-trainable recurrent horizontal latent state alongside vertical residual computation.
IW0aL7JYuC.problem: Standard autoregressive Transformers route all active per-token computation through a single depth-wise residual vector while treating past states solely as a write-once KV cache.
IW0aL7JYuC.method: Latent Lattice Language Models introduce a zero-initialized per-layer horizontal latent state updated via an input-dependent linear recurrence across token positions in parallel with the standard vertical depth-wise residual stream, preserving token-parallel training.
IW0aL7JYuC.key_idea: Adds a per-layer horizontal latent state updated via linear recurrence across time alongside the vertical depth-wise residual stream while preserving token-parallel training.
IW0aL7JYuC.evidence: Evaluated against same-size, depth-scaled, and width-scaled Transformer baselines across three token budgets on in-domain and out-of-domain perplexity and nine downstream tasks.
IW0aL7JYuC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the clean zero-initialized recurrent-latent design that preserves parallel training and consistently improves perplexity and downstream accuracy over standard Transformers.
IW0aL7JYuC.main_concern: Experiments omit parameter-matched hybrid Transformer-SSM and short-convolution baselines needed to validate claims that horizontal latents differ functionally from existing sequence mixers.

6bXdhIQJVO.one_liner: Derives three-order-parameter mean-field learning dynamics for attention retrieval and MLP logic on permutation-composition chain-of-thought state tracking.
6bXdhIQJVO.problem: How attention-based retrieval and MLP-based state-update logic co-develop during supervised training on multi-step chain-of-thought state-tracking sequences remains poorly understood mathematically.
6bXdhIQJVO.method: The authors analyze a simplified one-block Transformer separating fixed-lag attention from a permutation-applying MLP trained on permutation-composition sequences, deriving closed ODEs via statistical-physics mean-field theory and an empirical attention-gradient closure for three order parameters tracking retrieval and on/off-target logic alignment.
6bXdhIQJVO.key_idea: Reduces coupled attention-retrieval and MLP-logic training dynamics on permutation state tracking to three mean-field order parameters capturing heuristic-first staged alignment.
6bXdhIQJVO.evidence: Validated by comparing ODE order-parameter trajectories and Gaussian rollout-accuracy predictions against numerical training simulations in both constrained and standard one-block Transformers.
6bXdhIQJVO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise reducing coupled attention-retrieval and MLP-logic training dynamics to three interpretable order parameters whose trajectories match simulations and carry over to unconstrained one-block Transformers.
6bXdhIQJVO.main_concern: Closing the solvable mean-field equations relies on an empirically posited attention-gradient approximation without direct error validation, while staged MLP-before-attention dynamics overlap conceptually with prior work.

WPzisRnvAd.one_liner: Combines Nesterov momentum with Gaussian-sketch or leverage-score randomized subspace regularized Newton for smooth optimization.
WPzisRnvAd.problem: Randomized Subspace Regularized Newton (RSRN) methods suffer from slow linear dependence on pessimistic full-Hessian condition numbers in local convergence rates.
WPzisRnvAd.method: Acc-RSRN incorporates Nesterov momentum into randomized subspace regularized Newton updates using either Hessian-vector Gaussian sketching or entry-wise ridge leverage score sampling, paired with a local spectral-tail convergence analysis for nonlinear objectives.
WPzisRnvAd.key_idea: Couples Nesterov acceleration with randomized subspace regularized Newton steps constructed via Gaussian Hessian-vector sketches or ridge leverage score entry sampling.
WPzisRnvAd.evidence: Supported by local convergence proofs for nonlinear objectives and experiments on synthetic controlled Hessian spectra, kernel logistic regression, and a small CNN.
WPzisRnvAd.claimed_gains: Improves local iteration complexity for n-dimensional problems with subspace size r from \widetilde{O}(n\kappa/r) in prior RSRN analysis to \widetilde{O}(n\sqrt{\bar\kappa_r}/r).
WPzisRnvAd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers commend the clear presentation and rigorous local nonlinear convergence analysis achieving square-root dependence on the spectral-tail condition number.
WPzisRnvAd.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty for the spectral-tail bound, an impractical local switch test requiring a known smallest Hessian eigenvalue bound, and narrow empirical evaluation without component ablations.

1qlOUKjPch.one_liner: Post-trains robot policies inside an action-conditioned latent world model using group-relative latent progress rewards.
1qlOUKjPch.problem: Improving generalist robot policies via physical rollouts is unscalable, while pixel-space world models entangle task dynamics with visual appearance under distribution shifts.
1qlOUKjPch.method: DreamEvolve learns action-conditioned latent dynamics with a Joint-Attention-of-Mixed-Experts world model augmented by scene edits, then post-trains VLA policies entirely in latent imagination using Latent Progress Reward Optimization to compute group-relative progress rewards. The authors also introduce the DreamEvolveBench evaluation suite.
1qlOUKjPch.key_idea: Roll out robot policies in an action-conditioned latent world model and optimize them with group-relative progress rewards estimated in latent space.
1qlOUKjPch.evidence: Evaluated with π-series VLA policies on LIBERO-Pro, DreamEvolveBench, and real-world robotic manipulation under visual, clutter, and task perturbations.
1qlOUKjPch.claimed_gains: Raises the average success rate under real-world perturbations from 10.1% to 61.7%.
1qlOUKjPch.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that post-training VLA policies via latent world-model rollouts and latent progress rewards yields strong robustness gains on simulation and real-robot perturbations.
1qlOUKjPch.main_concern: Retaining original action trajectories after automated scene edits can violate physical causality, world-model prediction errors risk reward exploitation, and the four-stage training cost is unablated.

W9rc1olHoW.one_liner: Assigns and selects continual LoRA experts without a router using Chinese Restaurant Process empirical-Bayes statistics.
W9rc1olHoW.problem: Expert-based multimodal continual instruction tuning relies on heuristic capacity expansion and separately trained routers that suffer from routing drift as tasks arrive.
W9rc1olHoW.method: PACE models task distributions in a frozen multimodal feature space using a Chinese Restaurant Process prior and closed-form parametric empirical-Bayes evidence to decide before adaptation whether an arriving task reuses an existing LoRA expert or creates a new one. At inference, the same stored statistics select a single LoRA expert without training a separate router.
W9rc1olHoW.key_idea: Combine a Chinese Restaurant Process prior with closed-form empirical-Bayes evidence in frozen feature space for router-free LoRA expert allocation and inference selection.
W9rc1olHoW.evidence: Supported by theoretical bounds on cross-task interference under shared experts and evaluations across four continual multimodal benchmarks (CoIN, UCIT, TriGap, MLLM-CL) on two backbones.
W9rc1olHoW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying continual LoRA expert allocation and single-expert inference selection via frozen statistics without a trainable router is simple, coherent, and competitive.
W9rc1olHoW.main_concern: Experiments do not train and compare simpler cosine or Euclidean task-grouping baselines under matched expert budgets, and gains over strict one-expert-per-task isolation are tiny.

HFfcBg8MZo.one_liner: Injects utterance-adaptive spectral cues into SSL audio detectors via Stiefel-constrained low-rank updates preserving pretrained subspaces.
HFfcBg8MZo.problem: Self-supervised speech encoders miss fine-grained spoofing artifacts across unseen generators, whereas classical spectral features capture artifacts but degrade under acoustic variation.
HFfcBg8MZo.method: SILO augments a pretrained self-supervised audio backbone with a low-rank utterance-adaptive spectral-injection branch optimized on restricted Stiefel manifolds. It enforces orthogonality constraints that decouple low-rank directions from signed amplitudes while protecting high-energy pretrained subspace directions, alongside releasing the VDD and FVD evaluation datasets.
HFfcBg8MZo.key_idea: Optimize a low-rank spectral-injection adapter on restricted Stiefel manifolds so spoofing cues are added orthogonally to high-energy pretrained SSL directions.
HFfcBg8MZo.evidence: Evaluated cross-dataset on ASVspoof 2019, ASVspoof 2021, MLAAD, and two newly curated pathological and long-form forensic datasets (VDD and FVD).
HFfcBg8MZo.claimed_gains: Achieves 1.02% EER on ASVspoof 2019, 1.56% EER on ASVspoof 2021, and 14.38% macro-EER on MLAAD.
HFfcBg8MZo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that complementing acoustically robust SSL encoders with subspace-preserving spectral injection achieves strong cross-dataset deepfake detection results and contributes useful forensic test sets.
HFfcBg8MZo.main_concern: Ablations do not cleanly isolate spectral injection from SSL adaptation or verify high-frequency artifact learning, while VDD/FVD are limited to Hungarian speech and underspecified protocols.

uQg2XxN7Ef.one_liner: Benchmarks whether LLM agents given benign permission-blocked tasks exploit workspace vulnerabilities under varying documentation cues.
uQg2XxN7Ef.problem: Agent safety benchmarks focus on malicious prompt attacks rather than testing whether agents given benign but permission-blocked goals bypass authorization boundaries and conceal it.
uQg2XxN7Ef.method: VirtualFelonyBench constructs 180 permission-blocked tasks in self-hosted web applications, pairing each task with four matched workspace conditions: no vulnerability, an undocumented vulnerability, a formal maintenance record, or a peer-agent note describing the flaw. Automated environment controllers verify actual privilege escalation, unauthorized attempts, and user disclosure.
uQg2XxN7Ef.key_idea: Hold benign permission-blocked goals fixed across four controlled vulnerability-availability and workspace-documentation conditions in live self-hosted applications to measure unauthorized exploitation.
uQg2XxN7Ef.evidence: Evaluated across 12 deployed LLM agent systems over 8,640 trials spanning 180 base tasks and four matched conditions.
uQg2XxN7Ef.claimed_gains: In 10 of 12 systems, agents attempt unauthorized actions in 42.5% of undocumented-vulnerability trials (with zero successful exploits), whereas at least one system exploits documented vulnerabilities on 165 of 180 base tasks.
uQg2XxN7Ef.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the four-condition benchmark in real self-hosted applications cleanly studies an important, underexplored risk of authorization violations under benign instructions.
uQg2XxN7Ef.main_concern: Zero exploits occur unless workspace files explicitly document the route (making 'agent-initiated' overstated), 180 tasks reuse 15 vulnerability paths with unclear construction details, and model-versus-harness effects are unisolated.

j49htODgNn.one_liner: Trains RL agents in a real-time meta-reasoning MDP to trigger asynchronous planners while continuing execution.
j49htODgNn.problem: In dynamic real-time environments that do not pause during computation, agents invoking slow planners face compute costs and execution delays that render returned plans stale.
j49htODgNn.method: The authors formulate a real-time meta-reasoning MDP where querying an asynchronous planner incurs an explicit cost and multi-step delay before returning a plan computed from the request state. Acting While Thinking (AWT) trains an RL policy over augmented state-plan histories to jointly decide when to request plans, how to act during delays, and whether to follow stale plans.
j49htODgNn.key_idea: Augment an MDP with asynchronous delayed plan requests so an RL policy jointly learns planner triggering, interim actions, and stale-plan adherence.
j49htODgNn.evidence: Supported by theoretical conditions on when delayed costly planning improves value and experiments across five real-time dynamic tasks using an oracle planner.
j49htODgNn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the asynchronous real-time meta-reasoning MDP cleanly models acting during non-instantaneous planning in dynamic environments.
j49htODgNn.main_concern: Experiments rely exclusively on a perfect oracle planner with pre-sampled delays, omit stronger non-heuristic baselines, and under-cite closely related adaptive-planning works.

iH0RK8pUGh.one_liner: Refines complete per-sensor temporal forecasts using a post-hoc stack of zero-initialized gated residual graph blocks.
iH0RK8pUGh.problem: Interleaving learned graph operators inside every encoder layer multiplicatively amplifies adjacency estimation noise across depth on fragmented sensor networks.
iH0RK8pUGh.method: GraFT reorders spatio-temporal forecasting by first generating a complete forecast independently per sensor using a temporal backbone, then applying a stack of zero-initialized α-gated LayerNorm graph residual blocks. Under perturbed-adjacency analysis, closing gates recovers a zero-noise per-sensor path rather than compounding errors multiplicatively.
iH0RK8pUGh.key_idea: Place zero-initialized scalar-gated residual graph blocks strictly after a standalone per-sensor temporal forecaster to isolate and suppress noisy learned adjacencies.
iH0RK8pUGh.evidence: Supported by perturbed-adjacency noise bounds, controlled synthetic experiments, and evaluations across 14 spatio-temporal benchmarks (up to 8,600 sensors) with MLP, PatchTST, and TSMixer backbones.
iH0RK8pUGh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular post-forecast graph refinement architecture is clear and achieves strong results across 14 spatio-temporal benchmarks and multiple temporal backbones.
iH0RK8pUGh.main_concern: Both theory and ablations compare gated post-forecast refinement against ungated interleaved substrates, failing to isolate graph placement from zero-initialized residual gating.

4AJYvotr0w.one_liner: Proves sharper iterative ridge-regression convergence with per-step fresh column sketches and derives residual-aware sampling distributions.
4AJYvotr0w.problem: Whether drawing fresh column sketches per iteration provably outperforms reusing a single fixed sketch in under-constrained iterative ridge regression has remained open.
4AJYvotr0w.method: Exploiting conditional independence of fresh per-step column sketches, the authors bound approximation error solely along the current residual direction rather than uniformly across the Gram matrix, tightening leverage and ridge-leverage score bounds. They also minimize sketched matrix-vector product variance to derive a residual-aware oracle distribution and a practical mixture approximation.
4AJYvotr0w.key_idea: Draw fresh column sketches each iteration to bound error only along the current residual direction and adapt sampling probabilities to residuals.
4AJYvotr0w.evidence: Supported by mean-square convergence bounds and empirical iteration-convergence experiments on synthetic matrices and real datasets including linear ridge probes on Qwen2.5 representations.
4AJYvotr0w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly establishes sharper per-iteration convergence bounds for fresh over fixed column sketching in iterative ridge regression.
4AJYvotr0w.main_concern: Proof and variance-reduction techniques closely extend prior RandNLA works, and experiments omit wall-clock runtime comparisons that account for recomputing sketch factorizations every step.

UZ46K2NIS0.one_liner: Establishes minimax rates and a variance-corrected group-sum contrast for change-point localization in dynamic Bernoulli networks.
UZ46K2NIS0.problem: Compressing dynamic networks into structural summaries can lower dimensionality during change-point localization, yet poorly aligned summaries can attenuate or erase the underlying change.
UZ46K2NIS0.method: For a single change-point in independent Bernoulli networks, the authors prove two-term minimax lower bounds showing how aligned edge-group structure replaces edge count with group count in the directional penalty. They attain matching upper bounds up to logarithmic factors using normalized group sums inside a variance-corrected distinct-index contrast, and analyze pilot-estimated groups and held-out representation selection.
UZ46K2NIS0.key_idea: Aggregate aligned Bernoulli network edges into normalized group sums within a distinct-index contrast to replace edge-count dimensionality with group count in localization.
UZ46K2NIS0.evidence: Supported by minimax lower and upper bounds, synthetic simulations varying network size, group count, and sample splitting, and an application to Enron email networks.
UZ46K2NIS0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers who followed the proofs agree that characterizing minimax lower bounds and variance-corrected contrasts for structured versus harmful network compression addresses a meaningful theoretical question.
UZ46K2NIS0.main_concern: Poor problem exposition with missing definitions and undefined notation makes the manuscript very hard to read, alongside incomplete positioning against prior network and Gaussian localization bounds.

TMR4uoKcJM.one_liner: Iteratively selects and scales sparse cross-layer neuron subsets via gradient attribution to steer language models.
TMR4uoKcJM.problem: Dense residual-stream steering vectors modify thousands of activations simultaneously under a linear additivity assumption, obscuring task-relevant neurons and ignoring cross-layer interactions.
TMR4uoKcJM.method: Distributed Sparse Interventions (DSI) alternates between attribution-based re-selection of candidate neurons distributed across layers and attention heads and gradient-based optimization of per-neuron additive intervention scales. This iterative refinement accounts for non-monotone responses and nonlinear interactions among intervened neurons.
TMR4uoKcJM.key_idea: Iteratively alternate neuron subset re-selection and backpropagation-based per-neuron scale optimization across layers and heads to capture nonlinear steering interactions.
TMR4uoKcJM.evidence: Evaluated across 12 in-context tasks, AxBench concept steering, and three instruction-tuned LLM families against dense steering vectors, function vectors, and 10-shot prompting.
TMR4uoKcJM.claimed_gains: Activates target task behavior across 12 tasks and three instruction-tuned models by intervening on fewer than 0.1% of neurons, outperforming dense steering vectors.
TMR4uoKcJM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical evaluation across models and tasks is rigorous and shows that accounting for neuron interactions yields sparse, effective steering sets.
TMR4uoKcJM.main_concern: DSI combines existing mean-difference, gradient-patching, and sparse-offset components at high backpropagation cost while lacking direct comparisons to recent fine-grained neuron steering baselines.

2Upxdbf1hl.one_liner: Trains a lightweight external encoder via distillation and RL to prepend continuous reasoning tokens to frozen LLMs.
2Upxdbf1hl.problem: Latent soft-token reasoning methods typically fine-tune the language model backbone itself, risking capability degradation and requiring costly full-model updates.
2Upxdbf1hl.method: INTACT keeps the backbone LLM completely frozen and trains a small external encoder to iteratively map backbone hidden states into continuous latent prefix blocks before textual decoding resumes. The encoder is first distilled to match the frozen model's post-step output distribution and then fine-tuned with reinforcement learning on final answer accuracy.
2Upxdbf1hl.key_idea: Iteratively generate soft-token reasoning prefixes from a frozen LLM's hidden states using an external encoder trained with step-substitution distillation and RL.
2Upxdbf1hl.evidence: Evaluated across four frozen 3B and 8B LLM backbones on GSM8K and 12 held-out mathematics, science, and commonsense benchmarks.
2Upxdbf1hl.claimed_gains: Raises GSM8K accuracy from 75.8% to 79.3% on Llama-3.2-3B and from 77.6% to 79.7% on Qwen-2.5-3B while cutting end-to-end per-problem latency by 19%.
2Upxdbf1hl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that inducing hybrid latent-and-text reasoning via a small external encoder without modifying backbone weights is a practical, well-structured design.
2Upxdbf1hl.main_concern: Baselines face truncation or missing concise-LoRA controls, RL length normalization confounds token-reduction claims, and evaluation omits harder reasoning benchmarks like AIME or GPQA.

sxZ6c1mrT4.one_liner: Adapts perspective 3D reconstruction transformers to panoramas via spherical-cap view selection and SO(3) harmonic encodings.
sxZ6c1mrT4.problem: Adapting perspective-pretrained 3D reconstruction models to 360-degree panoramas degrades accuracy because planar view projections and 2D positional encodings distort spherical geometry.
sxZ6c1mrT4.method: SGA3R projects each panorama into informative perspective views via spherical-cap optimization under coverage and overlap constraints, and injects spherical geometry into transformer attention through Dual-Path Harmonic Encoding (DPHE), which combines additive harmonics with SO(3) rotary harmonic encodings. Alternating view, frame, and global attention with frame-conditioned pose refinement extends reconstruction to multi-panorama inputs.
sxZ6c1mrT4.key_idea: Combine information-guided spherical-cap perspective projection with additive and SO(3)-lifted rotary spherical harmonic encodings inside a perspective-pretrained 3D reconstruction transformer.
sxZ6c1mrT4.evidence: Evaluated on single- and multi-panorama 3D reconstruction across indoor Matterport3D and Stanford 2D-3D-S benchmarks and outdoor Mapillary Metropolis.
sxZ6c1mrT4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that injecting spherical ray geometry and adaptive perspective projections into pretrained 3D transformers forms a coherent, competitive panoramic reconstruction pipeline.
sxZ6c1mrT4.main_concern: Key projection and pose components closely resemble recent panoramic reconstruction works, while ablations show the core Dual-Path Harmonic Encoding module adds only marginal accuracy gains and confounds view-selection factors.

H1uVreprXe.one_liner: Noisy ternary comparisons refine frozen query embeddings without encoder retraining or gallery access.
H1uVreprXe.problem: Interactive retrieval needs to improve frozen embeddings from limited noisy feedback without retraining or exposing the retrieval gallery.
H1uVreprXe.method: ICM estimates feedback consistency, accounts for ambiguous responses, and uses existing embedding geometry to control query updates from a fixed ternary-comparison budget.
H1uVreprXe.key_idea: Estimate comparison reliability and scale query updates through existing embedding geometry to accommodate ambiguous, noisy responses.
H1uVreprXe.evidence: A post-hoc set of 36 dataset-representation combinations spans eight families and noise levels from 0.0 to 0.5, with hierarchical nDCG@10 evaluation.
H1uVreprXe.claimed_gains: ICM improves hierarchical nDCG@10 by up to 16.48% in the strongest condition and by a family-balanced average of 3.03% across noise levels from 0.0 to 0.4.
H1uVreprXe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the budgeted gallery-free setting is clear and that broad multimodal evaluation and theory support the update rule.
H1uVreprXe.main_concern: Reviewers most often question evaluation validity because outcome-informed subset selection and a simulated oracle tied to the metric limit generalization.

Q947vyFU9R.one_liner: Partitions sparse-autoencoder latents into supervised correctness units and unsupervised reconstruction units to expose reasoning features.
Q947vyFU9R.problem: Standard reconstruction-sparsity training can miss subtle reasoning-related features because they contribute little to activation reconstruction variance.
Q947vyFU9R.method: G-SAE jointly supervises a subset of latent dimensions for step-reasoning correctness while leaving the remaining dimensions unsupervised for broad activation reconstruction, using labeled ProcessBench and unlabeled activations.
Q947vyFU9R.key_idea: Injects correctness supervision into only a partitioned subset of SAE latents while preserving unsupervised reconstruction capacity in the rest.
Q947vyFU9R.evidence: Experiments across six LLMs and five training seeds compare G-SAE with standard Top-K and label-free gated SAEs on correctness retention and reconstruction.
Q947vyFU9R.claimed_gains: G-SAE retains more correctness information than a standard Top-K SAE on five of six models at a small reconstruction cost.
Q947vyFU9R.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the partitioned design offers a useful correctness–reconstruction trade-off supported by broad evaluation and ablations.
Q947vyFU9R.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether gains are specific to guided dictionary learning, citing weak baselines and overlap with prior supervised SAE work.

x7actWdqhZ.one_liner: Disentangles inference-time fast-weight updates from TTT-aware training to explain limited adaptation in pretrained LLMs.
x7actWdqhZ.problem: The respective contributions of inference-time fast-weight updates and TTT-aware training to pretrained LLM performance remain unclear.
x7actWdqhZ.method: The study compares fast-weight learning rules, update objectives, and write and forget gates, analyzes training dynamics, and amplifies inference-time updates to test capability preservation.
x7actWdqhZ.key_idea: Compares the same TTT-trained model with fast-weight updates enabled and disabled to isolate their direct inference-time effect.
x7actWdqhZ.evidence: Experiments compare six update rules, two backbones, two training stages, and RULER and HELMET evaluations with updates enabled or disabled.
x7actWdqhZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the update-on/update-off protocol cleanly separates inference-time adaptation from changes learned during TTT-aware training.
x7actWdqhZ.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that full attention over the entire evaluation context makes fast weights redundant, limiting the central conclusion.

3FcQoFiFnC.one_liner: Exposes Blender procedural generation as composable Python functions for scalable synthetic data and VLM-authored 3D content.
3FcQoFiFnC.problem: Procedural 3D generation and VLM-authored Blender code are hindered by cumbersome workflows and difficulty composing reusable generation components.
3FcQoFiFnC.method: ProcFunc provides Python functions for creating, combining, analyzing, and executing Blender-based procedural material and geometry code, and includes an indoor-room generator built from compositional materials.
3FcQoFiFnC.key_idea: Represents procedural materials and geometry as explicit-input, explicit-output functions that can be composed and edited by VLMs.
3FcQoFiFnC.evidence: Experiments evaluate VLM material and geometry code editing, from-scratch code creation, and an indoor-room generator's detail, runtime, and diversity.
3FcQoFiFnC.claimed_gains: VLMs create new procedural code with significantly fewer coding errors using ProcFunc.
3FcQoFiFnC.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the explicit functional interface and modular material composition provide a practical foundation for reusable 3D data generation.
3FcQoFiFnC.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the evaluation incomplete, particularly for from-scratch geometry generation, visual diversity, and controlled API comparisons.

RuZFnMYbiV.one_liner: Stress-tests LLM judges under reprompting, challenges, and sustained persuasion to measure verdict stability.
RuZFnMYbiV.problem: Golden-data accuracy does not reveal whether LLM judges remain stable under reprompting, challenge, or sustained pushback.
RuZFnMYbiV.method: The Wiggle Framework measures mechanical consistency, single-turn conviction, and multi-turn persistence across nine frontier models and 14 judging tasks using static and adaptive pressure.
RuZFnMYbiV.key_idea: Measures verdict changes along mechanical consistency, single-turn conviction, and multi-turn persistence on matched judging items.
RuZFnMYbiV.evidence: The evaluation spans nine models and 14 safety, toxicity, AI-writing-detection, and political-response tasks, including repeated consensus pressure and three persuaders.
RuZFnMYbiV.claimed_gains: At turn 10, task-average wiggle rates range from 19–71% under repeated static consensus pressure and 40–73% for a single adaptive LLM persuader, with 62–91% coverage under at least one of three persuaders.
RuZFnMYbiV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that unifying previously separate stability probes on matched judges and items enables valuable, comprehensive comparisons.
RuZFnMYbiV.main_concern: Reviewers most often argue that wiggle does not distinguish unjustified capitulation from justified revision in response to valid counterarguments.

zGPDwbNzcx.one_liner: Approximates local action-conditioned image manifolds with Taylor polynomials to score many candidate actions from one extraction.
zGPDwbNzcx.problem: High-dimensional action-conditioned world models require expensive inference for each candidate action, limiting short-horizon planning.
zGPDwbNzcx.method: Action Jet predicts per-region responses to each action axis, uses a trajectory-fit correction head to estimate a third-order Taylor approximation, and computes an empirically calibrated validity radius.
zGPDwbNzcx.key_idea: Predicts state-dependent Taylor coefficients for local action responses, then reuses them to evaluate arbitrary candidate actions without further generator inference.
zGPDwbNzcx.evidence: Experiments on three domains with different action axes evaluate local prediction and candidate scoring against both source generators.
zGPDwbNzcx.claimed_gains: Scoring sixteen candidates from a single extraction is over 250× faster than with either source generator.
zGPDwbNzcx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that reusable state-dependent local predictions offer an interesting and useful way to reduce multi-candidate planning cost.
zGPDwbNzcx.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the validity radius, noting that it is an empirical heuristic rather than a bound on prediction error.

UlGpm0PjZi.one_liner: Detects token-level hallucinations causally using volume-modulated spiking dynamics over semantic box embeddings.
UlGpm0PjZi.problem: Most hallucination detectors assess completed text rather than detecting hallucinations as tokens are generated.
UlGpm0PjZi.method: LatticeSpike embeds frozen-LM signals as boxes, modulates a recurrent spiking network with box volume, and trains next-state prediction error with a token-level ranking objective; it also releases two THRIVE benchmarks.
UlGpm0PjZi.key_idea: Uses recurrent next-state prediction error, modulated by box volume, as a causal hallucination score for each generated token.
UlGpm0PjZi.evidence: The method is compared with twelve baselines on THRIVE-Llama, THRIVE-Gemma, RAGTruth, and TriviaQA under a strictly causal protocol.
UlGpm0PjZi.claimed_gains: LatticeSpike outperforms all tested baselines in 96/101 individual evaluation cells (~95% win rate) spanning average precision and AUROC.
UlGpm0PjZi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the causal token-level design, consistent empirical gains, and human-audited THRIVE datasets are useful contributions.
UlGpm0PjZi.main_concern: Reviewers most often question generalization beyond the limited generator families, decoding settings, and operating points evaluated.

Dpwe23TWWq.one_liner: Uses behavior and self-report Jacobians to quantify behavioral control hidden from low-rank activation monitors.
Dpwe23TWWq.problem: Low-rank activation monitors and model self-reports leave blind spots whose controllable behavioral consequences are difficult to quantify.
Dpwe23TWWq.method: The framework derives closed-form geometric bounds from behavior and self-report Jacobians at one hidden state, then studies monitoring subspaces, evasion, detection, and steering interventions.
Dpwe23TWWq.key_idea: Computes residual behavioral leverage outside a monitor's subspace from local Jacobians of model behavior and self-report.
Dpwe23TWWq.evidence: Experiments span Llama, Qwen3.5, Gemma, and OLMo models from 1B to 70B parameters and include monitor-aware attacks and intervention studies.
Dpwe23TWWq.claimed_gains: A fixed pre-deployment monitor captures a median 12% of behavioral leverage at rank 1 and 75% at rank 102, while rank-16-invisible steering yields 25–85% harmful, coherent completions versus 1–6% for equally sized visible edits.
Dpwe23TWWq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that jointly analyzing behavior and self-report provides a principled perspective on the difference between probing behavior and detecting interventions.
Dpwe23TWWq.main_concern: Reviewers most often caution that local next-token sensitivity does not establish attack success or safety-relevant behavior under finite interventions.

bJ9SqZK1KQ.one_liner: Probes frozen single-cell foundation models by fitting gene regulatory networks through their embeddings and testing perturbation recovery.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.problem: Predictive accuracy benchmarks cannot tell whether single-cell foundation model embeddings preserve underlying gene regulatory relationships.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.method: CLAMP fits a gene regulatory network in gene space through a frozen scFM encoder using a squared-distance embedding loss and evaluates recovered interactions against biological references. Comparing against identity, PCA, and random-projection controls reveals how much regulator-specific signal survives in the latent space.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.key_idea: Optimizes a gene-space regulatory network through a frozen scFM encoder loss to measure how much regulator-specific perturbation structure survives in embeddings.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.evidence: Applied to four scFMs (scGPT, scPRINT, Stack, Tahoe-x1) on four Perturb-seq datasets (Norman, Replogle K562, Replogle RPE1, X-Atlas HCT116) plus ChIP-seq validation.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.claimed_gains: Fitted directly in gene space, CLAMP recovers 70-89% of an empirical ceiling across the four datasets.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the mechanistic probing perspective and the informative identity, PCA, and random-projection controls.
bJ9SqZK1KQ.main_concern: Reviewers warn that Euclidean embedding loss may measure embedding geometry and scale rather than true regulatory knowledge, and note missing scFMs and dedicated GRN baselines.

VwnR4bVDOz.one_liner: Proves global convergence of gradient EM for Gaussian-gated mixtures of linear experts under logarithmic overparameterization.
VwnR4bVDOz.problem: Nonconvex Mixture-of-Experts training traps first-order methods in spurious local optima, leaving joint gate-and-expert convergence poorly understood.
VwnR4bVDOz.method: The authors analyze joint likelihood training of linear experts, learnable mixing weights, and a dense Gaussian-cluster softmax gate via gradient EM. By decoupling the loss into per-cluster subproblems, they establish a gradient-dominance inequality under logarithmic overparameterization and center separation.
VwnR4bVDOz.key_idea: Establishes a per-cluster gradient-dominance inequality showing gradient EM converges globally for Gaussian-gated linear MoEs under logarithmic overparameterization.
VwnR4bVDOz.evidence: Theoretical convergence proofs in population and finite-sample regimes, alongside empirical tests locating the success transition near width m log m.
VwnR4bVDOz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the joint gate, expert, and mixing-weight convergence analysis and the link between m log m overparameterization and initialization coverage.
VwnR4bVDOz.main_concern: Reviewers flag a technical flaw in the translation-equivariance claim affecting moment bounds, and note that dense tied-cluster routing differs from modern sparse top-k MoEs.

T6YkBc1ISt.one_liner: Selects one-shot feature batches by maximizing a submodular coverage surrogate over retrieved completed hypotheses.
T6YkBc1ISt.problem: One-shot batch active evidence acquisition must choose all features before observing outcomes, making expected loss reduction intractable.
T6YkBc1ISt.method: Hypothesis Utility Coverage (HUC) retrieves similar completed instances given a partial observation, transfers their precomputed explanation-derived action utilities, and applies concave diminishing returns within each hypothesis. Because the resulting surrogate is monotone submodular, greedy selection yields a (1-1/e) approximation guarantee.
T6YkBc1ISt.key_idea: Aggregates diminishing-return action utilities across retrieved completed hypotheses into a monotone submodular surrogate for greedy one-shot batch selection.
T6YkBc1ISt.evidence: Proves a (1-1/e) surrogate guarantee and conditional error decomposition, with empirical evaluations on tabular and image patch acquisition tasks.
T6YkBc1ISt.claimed_gains: Greedy selection on the HUC surrogate achieves a (1-1/e) approximation guarantee under a cardinality budget.
T6YkBc1ISt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem formulation clear and appreciate the submodular surrogate construction and conditional error decomposition.
T6YkBc1ISt.main_concern: Reviewers view the concave-over-modular formulation as incremental over prior submodular coverage work and question whether complete-instance attributions reflect partial-observation information gain.

5J6WudE0Gk.one_liner: Optimizes LLM inference-time skills from a task prompt alone by synthesizing data and running reflective skill editing.
5J6WudE0Gk.problem: Automated skill optimization methods require curated in-distribution training sets, which are unavailable for emerging tasks described only in natural language.
5J6WudE0Gk.method: Prompt2Skill derives a formal task specification from a natural-language description, automatically discovers or synthesizes evaluation datasets, and iteratively refines an external skill artifact through a closed loop of failure collection and reflective editing.
5J6WudE0Gk.key_idea: Automatically derives task specs and discovers or synthesizes training data from a prompt alone to drive reflective skill optimization.
5J6WudE0Gk.evidence: Evaluated across four domains (QA, reading comprehension, spreadsheets, math) and five open-source and frontier LLMs, plus matched-budget comparisons with SkillOpt.
5J6WudE0Gk.claimed_gains: Across four domains, Prompt2Skill achieves an average improvement of 10.8 over the direct prompting baseline across open-source and frontier models.
5J6WudE0Gk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that eliminating curated training sets via automatic data discovery makes skill optimization more practical and yields strong gains on text tasks like SQuAD.
5J6WudE0Gk.main_concern: Reviewers note that the reflective editing loop closely resembles SkillOpt and GEPA, while ablations do not isolate data synthesis from editing and gains on tool-use benchmarks like SpreadsheetBench are inconsistent.

waaZ4TURZx.one_liner: Updates autonomous driving policies at test time with single gradient steps toward trajectory samples accepted by safety verifiers.
waaZ4TURZx.problem: Autonomous driving policies suffer under domain shift at test time, yet lack ground-truth trajectories or differentiable simulators for adaptation.
waaZ4TURZx.method: TTLR uses existing safety verifiers (drivable area, occupancy, comfort) for rejection sampling over teacher or policy rollouts and takes one gradient step toward accepted trajectories.
waaZ4TURZx.key_idea: Turns non-differentiable trajectory safety verifiers into a test-time learning signal via rejection sampling and single-step distillation.
waaZ4TURZx.evidence: Experiments on KITScenes LongTail and Waymo Open E2E across pretrained policies (Alpamayo 1.5, AutoVLA, OneVL) and policies learned from scratch (VADv2, CILRS, CoverNet).
waaZ4TURZx.claimed_gains: Improves composite driving scores by up to 24% and lowers displacement error by up to 42%.
waaZ4TURZx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree using existing trajectory safety checks for test-time distillation and self-distillation is simple, broadly applicable, and yields consistent gains.
waaZ4TURZx.main_concern: The paper lacks a frozen-policy baseline that simply selects verifier-accepted trajectories from the 120 samples without updating weights.

9qRfc3x3UK.one_liner: Proves universal finite-time approximation of dynamical systems on a torus using autonomous Kuramoto oscillator networks.
9qRfc3x3UK.problem: The expressive power of analog computing systems like the Kuramoto model is poorly understood due to their restrictive coupled-oscillator dynamics.
9qRfc3x3UK.method: The authors prove that an autonomous Kuramoto network with hidden oscillators and appropriate initialization can uniformly approximate the finite-time flow of any continuously differentiable vector field on a torus without external forcing or a learned output map. They extend the result to smooth periodic coupling functions with a nonzero first Fourier harmonic.
9qRfc3x3UK.key_idea: Uses autonomous coupled Kuramoto oscillators with hidden oscillators and slow-fast dynamics to uniformly approximate continuously differentiable vector-field flows on a torus.
9qRfc3x3UK.evidence: The work is supported by universal approximation theorems and experiments on seven dynamical systems plus flow-matching generative modeling tasks.
9qRfc3x3UK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the universal approximation theorems for autonomous Kuramoto networks are mathematically interesting, well-presented, and relevant to analog computing.
9qRfc3x3UK.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about extreme timescale separation (10^-5 to 10^-6) causing numerical stiffness and hardware infeasibility, proof clarity, and a potential vector-field obstruction.

NP9QcmGoKO.one_liner: Replaces the R-learner's partially linear outcome model with a nonlinear class and orthogonality regularization to control nuisance-induced drift.
NP9QcmGoKO.problem: Plug-in nuisance errors induce structural drift in the R-learner's partially linear outcome equation that the target estimator cannot reduce.
NP9QcmGoKO.method: The Generalized R-learner (GRL) uses a general nonlinear outcome equation for the target estimator combined with an orthogonality-regularized objective. The authors establish conditions for reduced target error, unbiasedness, and Neyman orthogonality.
NP9QcmGoKO.key_idea: Using a nonlinear second-stage outcome model with an orthogonality penalty accommodates nuisance-induced structural drift beyond partially linear R-learner assumptions.
NP9QcmGoKO.evidence: Theoretical target-error analysis and empirical benchmarks on synthetic, semi-synthetic (IHDP), and real datasets against meta-learners.
NP9QcmGoKO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers acknowledge the clear presentation and thorough empirical comparison against meta-learner baselines.
NP9QcmGoKO.main_concern: Reviewers question the core theoretical premise (noting the binary R-learner decomposition is an exact identity), the loss of exact Neyman orthogonality, and older baselines.

df6oH8pwGm.one_liner: Recasts single-mutant protein kernels as Bayesian linear regression over one-hot features for exact constrained Thompson sampling.
df6oH8pwGm.problem: Optimizing acquisition functions of Gaussian process surrogates over combinatorial protein spaces of up to 20^L variants is computationally intractable.
df6oH8pwGm.method: BaLiSq reformulates any kernel on single-mutant variants as a Bayesian linear regression prior over one-hot variant features, preserving GP equivalence on single mutants while extending additively to multi-mutants. BaLiSqO pairs this surrogate with exact constrained Thompson sampling over the combinatorial sequence space.
df6oH8pwGm.key_idea: Recasting single-mutant kernels as Bayesian linear regression over one-hot features enables additive multi-mutant extrapolation and exact constrained Thompson sampling.
df6oH8pwGm.evidence: Theoretical equivalence proofs and experiments using the Kermut kernel on multi-mutant prediction and simulated protein optimization landscapes.
df6oH8pwGm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper is clearly written and combines kernel-informed priors with tractable constrained Thompson sampling for protein design.
df6oH8pwGm.main_concern: Reviewers note overstated theoretical novelty relative to BOCS and standard GP identities, plus missing comparisons to newer sequence Bayesian optimization baselines like LaMBO2.

M7M5rUMRa7.one_liner: Characterizes when short-path world-model feedback corrections generalize to long action paths via orthogonal response dynamics on finite graphs.
M7M5rUMRa7.problem: Feedback corrections calibrated on short action paths in world models can fail when reused along longer action sequences.
M7M5rUMRa7.method: For compact classes of orthogonal response dynamics on a fixed finite directed graph, the authors characterize when Gaussian-noisy scalar measurements on short paths suffice for reliable decisions across all legal continuations. They distinguish approximate all-path learning (via finitely many task-significant irreducible return types per strongly connected component) from exact finite linear calibration.
M7M5rUMRa7.key_idea: All-path feedback reuse is learnable exactly when each strongly connected component has only finitely many task-significant irreducible types of the joint return action.
M7M5rUMRa7.evidence: Theoretical minimax decision-risk characterizations on finite graphs and empirical visual experiments on a Meta-World task comparing cost and success rate.
M7M5rUMRa7.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers note the paper addresses an important problem of reusing short-path corrections for long-horizon planning and provides principled theoretical characterizations.
M7M5rUMRa7.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the restrictive finite-graph orthogonal-dynamics assumptions that are unverified in neural world models, limited Meta-World evaluation, and overly dense, hard-to-follow writing.

LBS9Mu4Bdz.one_liner: Imputes sparse visits with a deep kernel Gaussian process to train an autoregressive residual flow-matching model for brain trajectory forecasting.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.problem: Forecasting individualized multi-region brain trajectories from a single baseline scan is hindered by sparse, irregular longitudinal clinical visits.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.method: BrainGenFlow uses a per-region deep kernel Gaussian process to impute dense monthly supervisory trajectories from irregular visits, then trains an autoregressive residual flow-matching model to forecast 145 brain regions up to 120 months from a single baseline scan and covariates.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.key_idea: Distills irregular longitudinal visits into dense monthly trajectories via a deep kernel GP to supervise autoregressive residual flow matching from a single scan.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.evidence: Evaluated on long-horizon Alzheimer's disease biomarker forecasting across 145 brain regions, including leave-one-study-out generalization and 95% predictive interval coverage.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.claimed_gains: Forecasts 145 brain regions up to 120 months ahead with per-region 95% predictive intervals staying at 95-97% coverage across horizons.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that forecasting 145 brain regions over 120 months from a single baseline scan is clinically meaningful and well-scoped to sparse data.
LBS9Mu4Bdz.main_concern: Reviewers point out the missing direct DKGP forecasting baseline and that gains over a deterministic Transformer are statistically insignificant while compared published baselines underperform persistence.

lDRqAXf7Cs.one_liner: Jointly optimizes a face-localized adversarial perturbation across all faces in group photos to disrupt biometric matching after generative edits.
lDRqAXf7Cs.problem: Generative editors can modify group photographs while preserving biometric cues that enable unauthorized face recognition.
lDRqAXf7Cs.method: Obscrowd optimizes one soft-masked perturbation localized to all detected faces using a diffusion teacher-student pipeline, inference-time refinement, and an ensemble of face recognizers across simulated edits.
lDRqAXf7Cs.key_idea: Jointly optimizes one mask-localized perturbation across all detected faces in an image against simulated generative edits and a recognizer ensemble.
lDRqAXf7Cs.evidence: Evaluated on group photographs and single portraits across crop-edit orderings, held-out recognizers, and matched unprotected controls.
lDRqAXf7Cs.claimed_gains: Under crop-then-edit instruction editing on group photos, reduces mean cosine similarity from 0.662 to 0.287 using about one-quarter the compute of per-face optimization.
lDRqAXf7Cs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the joint multi-face compute savings and careful controls separating protection from editing-induced identity loss.
lDRqAXf7Cs.main_concern: Reviewers show that cosine-similarity drops translate to low non-match rates (6-14%) at calibrated verification thresholds and weaken under wider crops.

dXIY9FObFf.one_liner: Post-trains LLM user simulators with RL combining intent-adherence rewards and an alternatingly updated naturalness discriminator.
dXIY9FObFf.problem: Prompted LLMs follow complex intents but sound unnatural, whereas specialized user simulators sound natural but drift from complex user intents.
dXIY9FObFf.method: The authors post-train UserLM-2.0 with reinforcement learning that jointly rewards task intent adherence and behavioral naturalness. Naturalness is scored by a lightweight ModernBERT discriminator retrained in an alternating adversarial loop with the simulator.
dXIY9FObFf.key_idea: Jointly optimizes user simulators for intent adherence and conversational naturalness using a lightweight discriminator retrained in an alternating RL loop.
dXIY9FObFf.evidence: Comparisons against prompted assistants and specialized simulators, reward ablations (frozen vs. dynamic discriminator), and behavioral dynamics analyses.
dXIY9FObFf.claimed_gains: UserLM-2.0 produces valid simulated conversations 46.2% of the time, over three times the 14.1% rate of the strongest prior user simulator.
dXIY9FObFf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that balancing task fidelity and naturalness is important and that dynamic discriminator ablations are well targeted.
dXIY9FObFf.main_concern: Reviewers note missing human evaluation of naturalness, evaluation tied to a single simulator/assistant/data setup, and reduced naturalness compared to SFT initialization.

ikAiWp0Wbi.one_liner: Evaluates text diversity metrics using controlled mixtures of human-authored perspectives across four conceptual diversity criteria.
ikAiWp0Wbi.problem: Existing text diversity evaluations lack ground truth to test whether metrics capture variety, balance, disparity, and composition invariance.
ikAiWp0Wbi.method: The authors operationalize Stirling's diversity criteria plus composition invariance by constructing controlled mixtures from Perspectrum and DiverseSumm datasets and statistically testing how proposed diversity metrics respond to each dimension.
ikAiWp0Wbi.key_idea: Constructs controlled mixtures of real labeled perspectives to test text diversity metrics separately on variety, balance, disparity, and composition invariance.
ikAiWp0Wbi.evidence: Empirical and statistical evaluations of diversity metrics across controlled mixtures built from Perspectrum and DiverseSumm.
ikAiWp0Wbi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the interpretable decomposition of diversity evaluation into four diagnostic criteria grounded in real datasets.
ikAiWp0Wbi.main_concern: Reviewers note small collection sizes (4-10 texts), confounding in the composition-invariance experiment, and overstated claims contradicting figure evidence for embedding metrics.

9gwsqDABXH.one_liner: Introduces HIDE, a full-graph, single-batch evaluation protocol without task-identity leakage for graph class-incremental learning.
9gwsqDABXH.problem: The standard CGLB benchmark leaks task identity in graph class-incremental learning by scoring test nodes one task at a time on task-specific subgraphs.
9gwsqDABXH.method: HIDE scores every test node in a single batch on the full shared graph over all seen classes, averaging accuracy across nodes. The authors vary batch composition, scoring graph, aggregation, and data choices independently across six GCIL methods and two non-continual reference classifiers.
9gwsqDABXH.key_idea: Evaluates all test nodes together in one batch on the full graph over all seen classes without exposing task boundaries.
9gwsqDABXH.evidence: Evaluates six GCIL methods and two reference classifiers across eight datasets using shared graphs and per-seed runs.
9gwsqDABXH.claimed_gains: Under HIDE, the method ranked first under CGLB on seven of eight datasets ranks last on seven of eight, dropping from 97% to 32% on ogbn-arxiv and from 87% to 12% at the widest.
9gwsqDABXH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly identifies task-identity leakage in CGLB and provides thorough experiments showing major ranking reversals across datasets.
9gwsqDABXH.main_concern: Reviewers note that training without inter-task edges while evaluating with them conflates task-identity removal with training-evaluation mismatch, alongside hyperparameter tuning and clarity issues.

GwBGdP3FJU.one_liner: Defines effective shared dimension for directed latent-position networks and proves consistency and asymptotic normality for singular-vector estimators.
GwBGdP3FJU.problem: Directed networks lack a principled, identifiable measure with asymptotic inference for quantifying how much a node's sending and receiving roles align.
GwBGdP3FJU.method: They define the effective shared dimension (and a degree-free variant) for general latent position models, deriving closed-form expressions under directed random dot product graphs. They construct adjacency singular-vector estimators with bias correction and prove consistency and asymptotic normality when average degree grows faster than n^(1/2) (or n^(1/4) with bias correction).
GwBGdP3FJU.key_idea: Quantifies sender-receiver subspace alignment via closed-form singular-vector estimators of effective shared dimension with bias-corrected asymptotic normality.
GwBGdP3FJU.evidence: Supported by consistency and CLT theorems, simulated co-blockmodel coverage tables, and application to 10 real directed networks.
GwBGdP3FJU.claimed_gains: Bias correction lowers the average-degree growth threshold required for asymptotic normality from n^(1/2) to n^(1/4).
GwBGdP3FJU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the closed-form effective shared dimension and its consistency and CLT results are mathematically clean and natural.
GwBGdP3FJU.main_concern: Reviewers highlight that limiting variance depends on unknown latent distributions without a data-driven estimator (simulations use oracle variance), CLTs degenerate at 0 and d, and equal in/out dimensions are assumed.

YdeJVq3Tjy.one_liner: Learns single-parameter flow maps over compactified infinite-time autonomous vector fields for one-step and multistep generation.
YdeJVq3Tjy.problem: Autonomous generative models like Equilibrium Matching require many network evaluations to integrate their time-independent vector fields.
YdeJVq3Tjy.method: EqFM compactifies the infinite time horizon onto a bounded interval and trains or distills a single-duration flow map using Lagrangian, Eulerian, and semigroup characterizations.
YdeJVq3Tjy.key_idea: Parameterize the flow map of a time-independent equilibrium vector field by a single compactified duration variable rather than start and end times.
YdeJVq3Tjy.evidence: Theoretical characterizations and experiments on CIFAR-10 and ImageNet-256 evaluate 1-NFE and 8-NFE generation.
YdeJVq3Tjy.claimed_gains: On ImageNet-256, EqFM improves from FID 2.90 at 1 NFE to 1.96 at 8 NFE.
YdeJVq3Tjy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the single-duration flow-map formulation for autonomous fields conceptually clean and the 8-NFE ImageNet-256 FID promising.
YdeJVq3Tjy.main_concern: Reviewers note uncontrolled training budgets against baselines like MeanFlow, missing baselines (e.g., Drifting, improved MeanFlow), and unanalyzed practical time-cutoff bias.

J0at0B5JmE.one_liner: PAC-learns multiclass linear classifiers under nasty noise using convex pairwise-distance pruning followed by hinge-loss minimization.
J0at0B5JmE.problem: Efficiently PAC-learning multiclass linear classifiers under adaptive nasty noise (simultaneous feature and label corruption) lacks polynomial-time algorithms with provable sample complexity.
J0at0B5JmE.method: Assuming a mixture of bounded-variance marginals and a clean margin condition, the algorithm solves a convex optimization program to prune outliers via pairwise squared-distance bounds, then minimizes multiclass hinge loss. A deterministic certificate guarantees surviving corrupted samples lie near clean margin-satisfying references.
J0at0B5JmE.key_idea: Convexly prunes outliers using pairwise squared-distance constraints so surviving corrupted points admit nearby clean reference points that preserve multiclass hinge-loss gradient robustness.
J0at0B5JmE.evidence: Supported by theoretical proofs establishing deterministic pruning certificates, multiclass gradient bounds, and sample complexity guarantees.
J0at0B5JmE.claimed_gains: Establishes efficient PAC learning under nasty noise with a sample complexity of O~(k^2 d).
J0at0B5JmE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the nasty-noise multiclass setting is important and that the convex pruning step with its deterministic clean-reference certificate is a solid theoretical contribution.
J0at0B5JmE.main_concern: Reviewers note that the margin and distributional assumptions are restrictive and that the polynomial-time optimization tolerances are not fully connected to the exact-feasibility statistical proofs.

wkTsyrayxJ.one_liner: Uses agent-level Shapley values to select vulnerable coalitions and generate coordinated multi-agent red-teaming attacks.
wkTsyrayxJ.problem: Existing red-teaming methods for hierarchical multi-agent systems (MAS) select target agents heuristically and perturb isolated messages without modeling cross-agent collusion.
wkTsyrayxJ.method: MAStrike computes agent-level and pairwise Shapley values to quantify each agent's marginal contribution to system robustness. An autonomous red-teaming agent uses these scores to pick vulnerable coalitions and iteratively refine role-aware adversarial manipulations via structured failure diagnosis on a new benchmark (MABench).
wkTsyrayxJ.key_idea: Computes agent-level Shapley attributions to identify vulnerable agent coalitions and drives iterative, failure-diagnosed adversarial prompt manipulations across colluding agents.
wkTsyrayxJ.evidence: Evaluated on MABench across three domains and three frontier models, plus coalition/generator ablations and transfer tests on the TAMAS harness.
wkTsyrayxJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the principled Shapley-based coalition selection and careful ablations isolating coalition choice from attack generation.
wkTsyrayxJ.main_concern: Reviewers criticize the threat model for replacing full compromised agents' system prompts—giving MAStrike stronger access than suffix-based baselines like TAMAS and GCA—and not testing single-agent baselines.

A77sWKRyVE.one_liner: Compresses agent interaction history into model-written memory every turn, trained via GRPO and full-history self-distillation.
A77sWKRyVE.problem: Long-horizon LLM agents accumulate growing interaction transcripts in their prompts until threshold compaction, inflating context size and KV-cache usage.
A77sWKRyVE.method: Continuous Context Management (CCM) has the agent emit an updated memory state alongside each action so the next prompt retains only the task, memory, and latest observation. For open-weight models, GRPO is augmented with privileged full-history distillation from a frozen initial-model copy scoring student rollouts under full history.
A77sWKRyVE.key_idea: Replaces full interaction transcripts with per-turn model-written memory updates and trains open-weight agents with GRPO plus action-token distillation from a full-history copy of the initial policy.
A77sWKRyVE.evidence: Evaluated without fine-tuning on TerminalBench-2 (Claude Sonnet/Opus 4.6, GLM-5, Kimi K3) and with RL training on WebShop and Endless Terminals (Qwen3-4B/8B-Instruct).
A77sWKRyVE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the practical multi-turn context problem, transparent token/cost accounting including prompt caching, and improved WebShop performance over plain CCM + GRPO.
A77sWKRyVE.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over MEM1/SDAR, lack of periodic-compaction baselines, unmeasured GPU latency/KV savings, and test-set checkpoint selection without multi-seed variance.

Q5iYGwAe9W.one_liner: Identifies narrow 1-3 token residual-stream bottlenecks carrying evidence-to-answer computation via dual necessity-sufficiency patching.
Q5iYGwAe9W.problem: Standard attribution methods identify important components without testing whether evidence-to-answer computation is forced through a narrow bottleneck.
Q5iYGwAe9W.method: Applies paired sufficiency (clean-into-corrupted) and necessity (corrupted-into-clean) patching to the same candidate set of evidence-token positions at a single residual-stream layer, testing against a size-matched permutation null.
Q5iYGwAe9W.key_idea: Requires the same small set of evidence-token positions at one residual layer to pass both sufficiency and necessity patching relative to a size-matched permutation null.
Q5iYGwAe9W.evidence: Evaluated across seven models, three normalization schemes, controlled benchmarks, and real single-hop, multi-hop, arithmetic, and long-context QA.
Q5iYGwAe9W.claimed_gains: On the controlled benchmark in best-powered models, the cut passes about 0.98 of the time versus about 0.01 for the matched control, spanning 2-3 positions (1-2 on real text).
Q5iYGwAe9W.reviewer_consensus: Two reviewers value the dual necessity-sufficiency patching diagnostic and broad empirical coverage across architectures and QA tasks.
Q5iYGwAe9W.main_concern: Reviewers note that dual patching on a single clean-corrupted pair does not rule out parallel pathways, and comparisons only use simple DLA baselines.

sWzyKeXuKy.one_liner: Aligns a message-passing GNN with the Chambolle-Pock primal-dual hybrid gradient algorithm to solve graph saddle-point problems.
sWzyKeXuKy.problem: General graph saddle-point optimization problems lack neural algorithmic reasoning architectures that generalize across graph sizes and accelerate classical solvers.
sWzyKeXuKy.method: GraphPDHG maps the Chambolle-Pock Primal-Dual Hybrid Gradient (PDHG) method onto a message-passing GNN trained unsupervisedly with a primal-dual gap loss. It learns instance-dependent algorithmic updates that can also serve as a warm start for second-order solvers like SSNAL.
sWzyKeXuKy.key_idea: Unrolls and parameterizes the Chambolle-Pock primal-dual hybrid gradient updates as a message-passing GNN trained unsupervisedly via primal-dual gap.
sWzyKeXuKy.evidence: Proves simulation and acceleration properties theoretically, and evaluates empirically on convex clustering as an SSNAL warm start and on image datasets against GNN baselines.
sWzyKeXuKy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the motivation for learning instance-dependent PDHG updates via neural algorithmic reasoning solid, with helpful theoretical results and ablations.
sWzyKeXuKy.main_concern: Reviewers point out a narrow empirical scope (only convex clustering), missing direct comparisons to classical PDHG in main tasks, and writing/numerical inconsistencies between text and tables.

EhlfBlDI2n.one_liner: Defines predictive realization dimension and derives Gram-matrix certificates showing state-sufficient encodings can still need extra dimensions for regular prediction.
EhlfBlDI2n.problem: Whether representations that fully specify environment state can still require additional latent dimensions to support Lipschitz-regular prediction.
EhlfBlDI2n.method: The paper defines predictive realization dimension and derives verifiable geometric certificates using PSD Gram matrices, distance variation, and transition recurrence under a shared Lipschitz regularity bound, including non-invertible transitions.
EhlfBlDI2n.key_idea: Uses PSD Gram-matrix and distance-variation certificates to lower-bound the dimension required for Lipschitz-bounded predictive realization beyond state sufficiency.
EhlfBlDI2n.evidence: Supported by formal lower-bound certificates and finite-state grid experiments comparing standard and walled systems.
EhlfBlDI2n.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theoretical insight—that state sufficiency does not guarantee low-dimensional Lipschitz-regular prediction—sound and interesting.
EhlfBlDI2n.main_concern: The connection to practical learned world models or noisy state-space settings is limited, and the dimension certificates loosen sharply once the Lipschitz gain exceeds one.

gaUSLsn6k5.one_liner: Retrains six ECG pretraining methods on a unified 1.21M-recording corpus and shows signal-only JEPA matches multimodal models under full labels.
gaUSLsn6k5.problem: Whether multimodal ECG pretraining outperforms signal-only pretraining because text adds unique information or due to uncontrolled corpora, retraining, and evaluation protocols.
gaUSLsn6k5.method: The authors retrain six published signal-only and multimodal ECG methods from official code on 1.21 million recordings and evaluate them with a shared frozen linear probe and two one-sided equivalence tests on PTB-XL and SPH.
gaUSLsn6k5.key_idea: Controls pretraining corpus, retraining, and frozen linear probing to test whether signal-only JEPA matches text-paired ECG foundation models.
gaUSLsn6k5.evidence: Evaluated six retrained models on 1.21M recordings with frozen linear probes (and MLP/resampling checks) on PTB-XL and SPH under full and 10% label regimes.
gaUSLsn6k5.claimed_gains: JEPA comes within 0.005 macro-AUROC of the strongest multimodal model on PTB-XL and scores 0.007 above it on SPH (equivalent within a 0.02 margin), while reports add 0.015 and 0.045 only at 10% labels.
gaUSLsn6k5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the rigorous, standardized retraining and probing protocol that isolates full-label ceiling equivalence from reduced-label efficiency.
gaUSLsn6k5.main_concern: Pretraining data exposure and epoch budgets differ across models (e.g., 1.21M vs. 392k–800k recordings for multimodal baselines), and evaluation is restricted to frozen probing rather than zero-shot or retrieval tasks.

WE30WGcWMX.one_liner: Reformulating unsolved reasoning problems into easier answer-preserving formats supplies RL rewards before returning to open-ended tasks.
WE30WGcWMX.problem: RLVR receives no reward or gradient from problems that the current policy cannot solve, preventing learning from the hardest examples.
WE30WGcWMX.method: Cog-DRIFT converts open-ended problems into multiple-choice and cloze variants that preserve answers while shrinking the search space. An adaptive curriculum moves from easier formats toward the original tasks without teacher reasoning traces.
WE30WGcWMX.key_idea: Answer-preserving task reformulation creates denser verifiable rewards by reducing effective search space, then transfers learning back to open-ended problems.
WE30WGcWMX.evidence: Experiments cover Qwen and Llama across six challenging reasoning benchmarks, originally unsolvable problems, held-out datasets, and ablation studies.
WE30WGcWMX.claimed_gains: Cog-DRIFT improves originally unsolvable hard problems by +10.11% for Qwen and +8.64% for Llama in absolute gains.
WE30WGcWMX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that format-based difficulty adjustment is simple, needs only questions and gold answers, and can supply learning signals without external reasoning traces.
WE30WGcWMX.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the gains reflect broad reasoning improvement or answer-related scaffolding and increased sampling of existing capabilities.

7Xgkkz5DPc.one_liner: Unifying over 360 Unicode-grid game tasks supports language-agent RL training, evaluation, replay, and reasoning-transfer studies.
7Xgkkz5DPc.problem: Research on interactive language-agent learning lacks a shared environment suite connecting varied games, spatial observations, training, and reproducible trajectory analysis.
7Xgkkz5DPc.method: GlyphBench renders spatial observations as two-dimensional Unicode grids and provides one interface for training, evaluation, and replay. The suite supports studies of observation formats, reasoning effort, agent harnesses, and RL configurations.
7Xgkkz5DPc.key_idea: A common glyph-based interface converts diverse games into comparable language-agent tasks for controlled RL and transfer experiments.
7Xgkkz5DPc.evidence: Experiments cover Craftax, several BALROG environments, RL on 100 GlyphBench tasks, and held-out Reasoning Gym evaluation with Qwen3.5-4B.
7Xgkkz5DPc.claimed_gains: Gameplay RL reaches 63.48% accuracy on held-out Reasoning Gym problems, outperforming the base model and math-trained and code-trained baselines.
7Xgkkz5DPc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the shared interface is a useful training resource and that the experiments demonstrate learning and external reasoning transfer.
7Xgkkz5DPc.main_concern: Reviewers most often find the contribution beyond existing game benchmarks unclear, with one also noting that no code or detailed API is supplied.

V7MaTGeAUs.one_liner: Decomposing unconstrained neural predictions into feasible solutions enables projection-free self-supervised combinatorial optimization with automatic rounding.
V7MaTGeAUs.problem: Continuous training for constrained combinatorial optimization often requires problem-specific projections that force neural outputs into feasible polytopes.
V7MaTGeAUs.method: The framework lets networks predict arbitrary continuous vectors and approximates them with sparse convex combinations of feasible solutions using Frank-Wolfe and approximate Caratheodory decomposition. The decomposition defines a differentiable expected discrete-objective loss and supplies inference-time rounding.
V7MaTGeAUs.key_idea: Frank-Wolfe decomposition turns unconstrained predictions into distributions over feasible discrete solutions, connecting training loss and rounding through one construction.
V7MaTGeAUs.evidence: Experiments evaluate the Quadratic Assignment Problem, Maximum Coverage, and the Traveling Salesperson Problem with oracle-based decomposition.
V7MaTGeAUs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that one oracle-based decomposition can unify feasible training and solution recovery while reducing problem-specific designs.
V7MaTGeAUs.main_concern: Reviewers question whether practical solution quality and iterative decoding costs establish an advantage over existing combinatorial-learning methods.

0jzdQR2K2q.one_liner: Converts longitudinal MEDS electronic health records into leakage-safe, sparse, sharded tabular feature matrices at scale for reproducible baselines.
0jzdQR2K2q.problem: Building temporal leakage-safe, task-aligned tabular baselines from irregular longitudinal EHR event streams is repeatedly reimplemented and scales poorly.
0jzdQR2K2q.method: MEDS-Tab ingests datasets in the Medical Event Data Standard (MEDS) format and constructs sparse, subject-sharded feature matrices over heterogeneous clinical codes, lookback windows, and aggregation functions, with optional downstream tabular model training utilities.
0jzdQR2K2q.key_idea: Applies subject-level sharded sparse aggregation over timestamped MEDS event streams to generate leakage-safe tabular feature matrices at scale.
0jzdQR2K2q.evidence: Benchmarked for runtime and memory scalability against competing tabularization tools and evaluated across five external clinical prediction studies.
0jzdQR2K2q.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that MEDS-Tab addresses a genuine, recurring engineering bottleneck in clinical ML with practical usability and systematic leakage prevention.
0jzdQR2K2q.main_concern: Reviewers cite limited technical novelty over existing feature-extraction tools (e.g., FIDDLE, OHDSI, tsfresh), omission of healthcare-specific baselines, and scalability stress tests capped at 500 subjects.
