enhK7uVSgi.one_liner: Adapts health LLM benchmarks to deployment distributions using prompt-rubric semantic reweighting and efficient influence-function estimators under evaluator shift.
enhK7uVSgi.problem: Fixed LLM benchmarks differ from clinical deployment in both task distribution and scoring evaluator, while scoring large target sets is expensive.
enhK7uVSgi.method: Without target labels, the authors transport benchmark scores via importance reweighting on prompt and rubric embeddings. With small target samples—under either the same evaluator or a shifted human/LLM evaluator—they derive efficient influence functions to fuse benchmark and paired target scores for mean estimation and ranking recovery.
enhK7uVSgi.key_idea: Combines prompt-and-rubric embedding reweighting with semiparametric efficient influence-function data fusion across both task-distribution shift and paired evaluator shift.
enhK7uVSgi.evidence: Derives semiparametric efficient influence functions and evaluates ranking recovery and mean estimation on HealthBench and MentalHealthBench.
enhK7uVSgi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the practical three-regime framing separating task shift from evaluator shift and the clean semiparametric method design.
enhK7uVSgi.main_concern: Reviewers note that deployment shifts are synthetically resampled from HealthBench rather than real clinical shifts, and that experiments rely on only two models (GPT-4.1, Gemini Flash Lite) and one embedding model (BGE-M3).

klXcnEEMjl.one_liner: Constructs activation-aware low-bit LLM weights online from the current prompt during prefill and reuses them throughout decoding.
klXcnEEMjl.problem: Offline post-training activation-aware quantization suffers accuracy drops when deployment prompts diverge from the calibration dataset.
klXcnEEMjl.method: Test-Time Quantization (TTQ) estimates activation statistics from the incoming prompt during prefill to quantize weights on the fly without a calibration dataset, then reuses those low-bit weights to reduce weight traffic during autoregressive decoding.
klXcnEEMjl.key_idea: Computes prompt-specific activation-aware low-bit weight quantizations online during prefill and reuses them across decoding steps without offline calibration data.
klXcnEEMjl.evidence: Evaluated across language, vision-language, and vision-language-action models (including Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B) with matched ablations and GPU throughput measurements.
klXcnEEMjl.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find prompt-specific online quantization a natural, calibration-free response to calibration mismatch supported by multi-modal task evaluations and controlled ablations.
klXcnEEMjl.main_concern: Reviewers flag physically implausible full-model throughput numbers on RTX 5090, higher memory usage than FP16 (keeping full-precision weights resident), slower prefill/decode than AWQ, and potential future-token leakage in perplexity evaluation.

svMbuocaEB.one_liner: Optimizes set-level generation objectives over frozen models by pairing lightweight behavior controls with collection-structure-aware credit assignment.
svMbuocaEB.problem: Many generation objectives (distribution matching, demographic fairness, Pareto coverage) depend on sets of outputs rather than individual responses.
svMbuocaEB.method: The authors decompose set-level control into learning a repertoire of lightweight behavior controls over frozen generators/solvers and organizing their participation in an output set. From one set-level objective, they derive shared, objective-sensitivity, and marginal-contribution credit estimators tailored to sampled modes, semantic roles, and complementary subsets.
svMbuocaEB.key_idea: Derives shared, objective-sensitivity, and marginal-contribution credit estimators from a single set-level gradient objective to coordinate lightweight controls over fixed generators.
svMbuocaEB.evidence: Instantiated and evaluated on fiction distribution matching, demographic regard equalization, and Pareto-frontier coverage.
svMbuocaEB.claimed_gains: Learned allocation reduces fiction set KL by 32.9-46.4% across three evaluators, and sensitivity credit reduces regard disparity by 73.3% relative to shared credit.
svMbuocaEB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean conceptual decomposition of repertoire versus organization and unifying three credit signals under one set-level objective across diverse tasks.
svMbuocaEB.main_concern: Reviewers criticize circular evaluation using the same classifier for both training reward and evaluation metric (without human or independent checks) and thin technical novelty over prefix tuning and SetPO.

QSWzl6DF6M.one_liner: Constructs 157 model organisms across seven training regimes to show white-box interpretability fails much more often under realistic integrated training.
QSWzl6DF6M.problem: Interpretability evaluations rely on post-hoc SFT model organisms, which may make hidden behaviors unrealistically easy to detect compared to naturally trained models.
QSWzl6DF6M.method: The authors train 61 OLMo2-1B and gemma-3-1b-it model organisms across seven regimes (including post-hoc SFT, post-hoc DPO, and integrated DPO) plus 96 distilled variants, and benchmark four white-box tools: activation oracles, activation steering, logit lens, and Jacobian lens.
QSWzl6DF6M.key_idea: Systematically varies model-organism construction across seven post-hoc, integrated, and distilled training methods to test whether white-box interpretability tool performance is an artifact of post-hoc SFT.
QSWzl6DF6M.evidence: Benchmarks four white-box interpretability methods on 61 base model organisms and 96 distilled variants across OLMo2-1B and gemma-3-1b-it spanning three behavioral quirks.
QSWzl6DF6M.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the timely, extensive empirical audit questioning the validity of post-hoc model organisms as interpretability benchmarks across seven training methodologies.
QSWzl6DF6M.main_concern: Reviewers note that the three target quirks are contrived compared to real safety-relevant behaviors, all models are small (1B scale), and the paper lacks mechanistic explanation for why integrated/distilled models resist auditing.

itpNQUiQUU.one_liner: Derives a trace law for mean-field posterior distortion in Bayesian LoRA and shows covariance errors can hide behind unchanged proper scores.
itpNQUiQUU.problem: In Bayesian low-rank adaptation, posterior covariance factorization distorts predictive uncertainty in ways that standard proper scoring rules fail to detect.
itpNQUiQUU.method: The authors derive a trace law showing how mean-field factorization inflates uncertainty along informed predictive directions while collapsing it in uninformed complements, and prove response identities showing covariance perturbations can leave integrated predictive probabilities and proper scores nearly invariant while reversing information-gain rankings. They compare Fisher-coordinate fits against Hamiltonian Monte Carlo references.
itpNQUiQUU.key_idea: Proves a trace law for mean-field directional distortion and response identities showing posterior covariance errors can reverse active-acquisition rankings while leaving proper scores nearly unchanged.
itpNQUiQUU.evidence: Combines theoretical trace and response-identity analysis with restricted 64-dimensional Bayesian LoRA experiments on Qwen3-4B and Phi-4-mini using HMC references and ARC-Challenge.
itpNQUiQUU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the theoretical insight into how mean-field variational inference distorts Bayesian LoRA uncertainty and why standard proper scores miss covariance errors.
itpNQUiQUU.main_concern: Reviewers point out limited experimental scope (one multiclass dataset, 64-dimensional restricted adapters) and minimal downstream gains in NLL, Brier score, or ECE from Fisher coordinates.

1ymrzbtiNR.one_liner: Shows that fixed-fraction versus fixed-count elite conventions flip the effect of drawing more planner samples in CEM/MPPI world-model planning.
1ymrzbtiNR.problem: Practitioners studying whether more planner samples help in CEM/MPPI obtain contradictory results because libraries silently differ in how elite sets scale with population size.
1ymrzbtiNR.method: The authors run pre-registered controlled sweeps comparing fixed-fraction elites (MBRL-Lib default) against fixed-count elites (TD-MPC2 and original PETS/PlaNet) on identical models, seeds, and episodes, and instrument proposal dispersion to show how elite scaling widens or tightens the refit distribution.
1ymrzbtiNR.key_idea: Isolates the unreported elite-set convention (fixed fraction vs. fixed count) in sampling-based planners and shows it controls whether larger populations widen or tighten proposal dispersion.
1ymrzbtiNR.evidence: Pre-registered experiments across 35 tasks using publicly released TD-MPC2 checkpoints and author-trained PETS and PlaNet models.
1ymrzbtiNR.claimed_gains: Increasing population 40x on identical PlaNet models changes return by -63 under one elite convention and +246 under the other (both p=0.002), while shifting PETS dispersion from 0.127 to 0.219 (fixed fraction) versus 0.167 to 0.149 (fixed count).
1ymrzbtiNR.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the pre-registered experimental discipline and agree that the elite-convention confound is a consequential practical warning for cross-codebase planner comparisons.
1ymrzbtiNR.main_concern: Reviewers note that the core elite-convention finding rests on only six cells from two model families, lacks formal theoretical proof for the dispersion mechanism, and has a low pre-registration hit rate.

YXhbQ46hdE.one_liner: Distills frozen DINO features through a training-only head into a compact action-conditioned latent world model and discards DINO at inference.
YXhbQ46hdE.problem: Latent world models trained only on dynamics prediction risk representation collapse, whereas planning directly in frozen pretrained patch-feature spaces is slow.
YXhbQ46hdE.method: Anchor-WM trains a compact latent state with action-conditioned dynamics while distilling dense DINO representations via a training-only distillation head to preserve visual information and prevent collapse. At inference, both the DINO encoder and distillation head are discarded so planning runs entirely in the compact latent space.
YXhbQ46hdE.key_idea: Uses frozen DINO features solely as a training-time distillation target for a compact action-conditioned latent world model, discarding the vision encoder at planning time.
YXhbQ46hdE.evidence: Evaluated across four visual planning environments (including PushT, Cube, and TwoRoom) against LeWM and DINO-WM with ablations on loss type and patch-versus-global targets.
YXhbQ46hdE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the simple, cheap single-loss modification that speeds up planning over DINO-WM and the clear patch-versus-global distillation ablation.
YXhbQ46hdE.main_concern: Reviewers question baseline numbers falling below published LeWM results, missing baselines that compress DINO before dynamics learning, and probes not showing better physical information capture.

8aNSV8hJyB.one_liner: Peppy synthesizes tight analytic Lyapunov convergence proofs for first-order optimization algorithms using domain-specific proof structure and SymPy verification.
8aNSV8hJyB.problem: Generic LLM approaches to mathematical research lack domain structure and often rely on heavy formalization systems like Lean 4.
8aNSV8hJyB.method: Peppy is an AI-assisted workflow that restricts convergence proofs to domain-specific analytic Lyapunov forms and verifies the resulting rational identities and sign conditions with SymPy. It synthesizes tight convergence proofs for first-order optimization methods.
8aNSV8hJyB.key_idea: Constrains LLM proof synthesis to domain-specific weighted-residual minus sum-of-squares Lyapunov templates verifiable via SymPy.
8aNSV8hJyB.evidence: Demonstrated through examples of first-order optimization algorithms, closing open tight convergence conjectures for Nesterov's FGM as well as OGM, rational FGM, and rational FISTA.
8aNSV8hJyB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the resolved mathematical convergence results, including tight analytic bounds for Nesterov's FGM, are substantive and verifiable.
8aNSV8hJyB.main_concern: The evaluation lacks ablations separating the contribution of the Peppy workflow and utilities from the underlying LLM and PEP tools.

gw0cJ1vLJH.one_liner: Characterizes three power-law scaling laws for LLM ensemble disagreement, capacity error, and shared-training diversity loss.
gw0cJ1vLJH.problem: Fixed-family Bayesian and ensemble approximations miss epistemic uncertainty caused by bounded model capacity, leaving unclear how ensemble uncertainty behaves as LLMs scale.
gw0cJ1vLJH.method: The authors decompose reducible LLM loss into ensemble-visible disagreement and capacity-limited invisible error, measuring three scaling laws: loss versus model size, ensemble disagreement versus model size, and diversity loss versus shared pretraining fraction. They compare public multi-seed/model suites and newly trained controlled families.
gw0cJ1vLJH.key_idea: Decompose reducible loss into capacity error and ensemble disagreement to derive power-law scaling of ensemble uncertainty with model size and shared-training branching fraction.
gw0cJ1vLJH.evidence: Supported by multi-seed checkpoints (up to ~1B parameters), newly trained controlled families, and cross-model pairs (e.g., Qwen2.5/Qwen3).
gw0cJ1vLJH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that connecting reducible loss to epistemic uncertainty via testable scaling laws across an extensive empirical suite is valuable and interesting.
gw0cJ1vLJH.main_concern: The headline claim that ensembles capture a growing share of epistemic uncertainty depends sensitively on an unknown irreducible loss constant, and large-scale pairs mix different model families rather than true seeds.

QzkrCScPfs.one_liner: Reconstructs native Power Foam 3D scenes from sparse views using a feed-forward initializer and geometry-first appearance refinement.
QzkrCScPfs.problem: Per-scene optimization of native Power Foam radiance fields is slow, and updating appearance on stale cell geometry misaligns visibility and pixel-to-texture gradients.
QzkrCScPfs.method: SceneFoam jointly trains an image-conditioned frontend and native initializer, applies four source-conditioned color-fitting steps, and runs a geometry-first refiner. The refiner updates cell surfaces first, recomputes image residuals and gradients on the updated foam, and then predicts refined appearance.
QzkrCScPfs.key_idea: Pair a feed-forward Power Foam initializer with a geometry-first refiner that recomputes image residuals and source gradients on updated surfaces before predicting appearance.
QzkrCScPfs.evidence: Evaluated on eight-view and two-view DL3DV140 and four native-PF scenes against ReSplat and 30,000-update optimization baselines, with sequential-refinement ablations.
QzkrCScPfs.claimed_gains: On eight-view DL3DV140, achieves 27.97 dB PSNR, 0.873 SSIM, and 0.153 LPIPS (beating ReSplat on all three), and outperforms 30,000-update baselines on four native-PF scenes in 8.94-9.44s.
QzkrCScPfs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that geometry-first refinement with refreshed residuals is well-motivated and consistently outperforms ReSplat while slashing Power Foam reconstruction time.
QzkrCScPfs.main_concern: The necessity of Power Foam over combining ReSplat with ray-traceable Gaussians (3DGUT/3DGRT) is unestablished, secondary-ray direction approximations lack validation under reflection/refraction, and exposition assumes deep prior familiarity.

wPds5enu7z.one_liner: Analyzes how joint versus componentwise DP-SGD gradient clipping rotates batch updates and adjusts gradient magnitudes to improve adversarial robustness.
wPds5enu7z.problem: When combining differential privacy with adversarial robustness penalties, different per-example gradient clipping rules yield different robustness even under identical loss functions and privacy guarantees.
wPds5enu7z.method: The authors compare two gradient-bounding rules (joint versus componentwise clipping) under fixed composite objectives and privacy calibration via geometric analysis and controlled fine-tuning. They show unequal example-dependent scaling rotates the aggregate batch update and adjust gradient magnitudes without changing directions to improve robustness.
wPds5enu7z.key_idea: Shows that per-example clipping rules alter aggregate batch update directions via unequal example-dependent rescaling and modifies gradient magnitudes while preserving directions under fixed privacy calibration.
wPds5enu7z.evidence: Geometric analysis and controlled image-classification fine-tuning experiments across multiple architectures and clipping functions evaluated with AutoAttack.
wPds5enu7z.claimed_gains: The choice of clipping rule changes mean test accuracy under AutoAttack by more than 3 percentage points while changing clean accuracy by less than 1 percentage point.
wPds5enu7z.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper cleanly isolates an overlooked DP-SGD implementation choice under fixed privacy calibration with clear geometric analysis and thorough experiments.
wPds5enu7z.main_concern: Reviewers question novelty beyond prior DP-SGD gradient-misalignment analyses, note missing comparisons to simpler fixed-length normalization, and question practical motivation for DP-SGD plus TRADES.

dz0yb4MlKd.one_liner: Certifies when an LLM receiver agent can skip a helper's text or KV-cache message using a confidence probe and finite-sample risk test.
dz0yb4MlKd.problem: Waiting for helper-agent text or latent KV-cache messages adds latency, yet skipping messages risks changing the receiver's final answers.
dz0yb4MlKd.method: The authors read the receiver agent's confidence before receiving the helper message and run a finite-sample statistical test on unlabeled calibration data to certify a threshold where at most 5% of skipped answers change with high probability. They also evaluate net latency savings and compare oracle headroom against answer-agnostic control messages.
dz0yb4MlKd.key_idea: Applies a finite-sample statistical test to receiver pre-message confidence scores to certify a dynamic message-skipping threshold bounding answer-change rate at <=5%.
dz0yb4MlKd.evidence: Evaluations on OpenBookQA, ARC-Challenge, MMLU-Pro, SQuAD, and GSM8K across three Qwen model pairs and cross-family receiver-helper pairs for text and KV-cache communication.
dz0yb4MlKd.claimed_gains: Control inputs without answer-specific content reproduce a median 76% of oracle headroom over the receiver agent alone, while certified thresholds bound skipped-answer changes to at most 5%.
dz0yb4MlKd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem formulation separating answer preservation from net speedup is clear and the oracle-headroom control analysis is a useful empirical caution.
dz0yb4MlKd.main_concern: Reviewers note that bounding answer changes does not guarantee accuracy preservation (all certified KV-cache paths are less accurate than receiver-only), novelty is limited to applying Learn-Then-Test, and coverage is mostly short-answer two-agent setups.

rtQHUAvbQh.one_liner: Defines witness-integrated set effects (WISE) and a gradient-based circuit discovery algorithm (JuntaLearner) to capture component interactions and backup effects.
rtQHUAvbQh.problem: Single-component attribution in mechanistic interpretability misses context-dependent interactions such as primary components inhibiting backup components.
rtQHUAvbQh.method: The authors define Witness-Integrated Set Effect (WISE), a causal estimand averaging witness-conditioned effects over sets of causes and witnesses to avoid combinatorial enumeration. They introduce JuntaLearner, a gradient-based method ranking components across varying set and witness sizes, along with necessity, specificity, and Circuit Recognition Score (CRS) metrics.
rtQHUAvbQh.key_idea: Estimates witness-conditioned causal interactions over component sets (WISE) using a gradient-based ranking learner (JuntaLearner) across varying set and witness sizes.
rtQHUAvbQh.evidence: Circuit discovery evaluations across tasks and language models of increasing size comparing JuntaLearner against attribution baselines using faithfulness, necessity, specificity, and CRS.
rtQHUAvbQh.claimed_gains: JuntaLearner achieves higher mean CRS than attribution baselines across all evaluated metrics.
rtQHUAvbQh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree capturing joint component interactions and backup effects via causal witnesses is an important problem and a worthwhile conceptual direction.
rtQHUAvbQh.main_concern: Reviewers flag problematic evaluation where headline results tune configurations on the reported CRS metrics, unclear faithfulness of JuntaLearner to WISE, and inconsistent evidence for the descending set-size schedule.

gRJNQkOBhk.one_liner: Optimizes meaning-preserving rephrasings of source messages using AI-text detector feedback so subsequent AI-generated replies become easier to detect.
gRJNQkOBhk.problem: AI-text detection focuses passively on improving detectors after text is written, rather than letting authors shape source wording to make undisclosed AI replies more detectable.
gRJNQkOBhk.method: REAIR formulates source rephrasing as constrained optimization maximizing the expected detector score of subsequent AI replies subject to semantic similarity and length checks. It instantiates search with Best-of-N, Hill-climb, Hill-climb-ICL, and a source-specific adaptation of GEPA using feedback from the Binoculars detector.
gRJNQkOBhk.key_idea: Searches over meaning- and length-preserving rephrasings of a source text using feedback from an AI-text detector evaluated on elicited AI replies.
gRJNQkOBhk.evidence: Evaluations on an online discussion task (ChangeMyView) and a research-proposal review task (AI-Researcher) with Gemma 4 31B and Binoculars, plus cross-detector and sampling transfer tests.
gRJNQkOBhk.claimed_gains: For greedy Gemma 4 31B replies, iterative REAIR variants raise Binoculars true-positive rates from 29.39% to 77.23%-78.39% on online discussion and from 12.93% to 56.46%-63.27% on proposal review.
gRJNQkOBhk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree shifting AI-reply detection from passive post-hoc analysis to active pre-generation source phrasing is a creative framing with thorough documentation and transfer checks.
gRJNQkOBhk.main_concern: Reviewers note human replies were only collected on unmodified sources (leaving human-vs-AI separation on rephrased sources untested), question practical motivation, and view Binoculars as an outdated primary detector.

bfvmxkTKEe.one_liner: Shows AI detectors distinguish LLM-generated number sequences from human and random baselines via non-human statistical biases amplified by post-training.
bfvmxkTKEe.problem: It is unclear whether trained AI-text detectors rely only on lexical and stylistic text heuristics or can also exploit deeper statistical biases when linguistic cues are absent.
bfvmxkTKEe.method: The authors test the Pangram AI detector on identically formatted LLM-generated, human-written, and true-random number sequences under sequence transformations (reversal, recoding, shuffling, bijective substitution). They analyze statistical structure across eight open models, fit an interpretable digit-generation simulation model, and sweep checkpoints, decoding, and chat templates.
bfvmxkTKEe.key_idea: Probes an AI-text detector on linguistic-free number sequences under structural transformations and fits an interpretable simulation model to isolate non-human digit-sequence biases.
bfvmxkTKEe.evidence: Detection, transformation, and checkpoint/decoding sweeps using Pangram across eight open-weight LLMs plus human and true-random number-sequence baselines.
bfvmxkTKEe.claimed_gains: Pangram distinguishes LLM-generated number sequences from human and true-random baselines with 0.995 AUROC, and the fitted interpretable simulation captures 84% of the measured statistical structure.
bfvmxkTKEe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree testing AI detection on number sequences is an unusual, well-controlled setting with surprising empirical results and informative transformation experiments.
bfvmxkTKEe.main_concern: Reviewers note the study is mostly descriptive without explaining why these biases arise or how they help practical detection, and that the detailed statistical model covers only single-digit sequences whereas strongest detection occurs on three-digit numbers.

kA7YZJziRc.one_liner: Post-trains text-to-CAD LLMs with GRPO using deterministic geometric Design-for-Manufacturability rewards across FDM, CNC, and injection molding.
kA7YZJziRc.problem: Text-to-CAD models optimize geometric similarity while ignoring whether generated 3D parts are physically manufacturable under real fabrication processes.
kA7YZJziRc.method: The authors formalize deterministic, LLM-free geometric checks encoding Design for Manufacturability (DFM) rules for FDM printing, CNC machining, and injection molding as verifiable rewards. They build a FeatureScript-to-CadQuery translator to expand training data and post-train LLMs with SFT followed by faithfulness-gated Curriculum GRPO.
kA7YZJziRc.key_idea: Encodes process-specific geometric Design-for-Manufacturability checks (FDM, CNC, injection molding) as deterministic, faithfulness-gated verifiable rewards for GRPO post-training of CAD code generators.
kA7YZJziRc.evidence: Post-training evaluations on the CADFS test set across three manufacturing processes comparing SFT and Curriculum GRPO on manufacturability and design-intent preservation.
kA7YZJziRc.claimed_gains: Improves overall manufacturability across all three manufacturing processes and paired manufacturability scores on three of four evaluated process settings.
kA7YZJziRc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree manufacturability is a practically relevant gap in text-to-CAD and appreciate the faithfulness-gated deterministic geometric reward design.
kA7YZJziRc.main_concern: Reviewers note the paper never validates physical manufacturability beyond its own heuristic DFM score, omits an LLM/VLM-judge baseline despite claiming superiority over judges, and lacks ablations isolating reward and curriculum choices.

5smcyBazE0.one_liner: Trains a normalizing flow (isobank) to map curved manifolds into approximately isometric Euclidean coordinates for fast gravitational-wave template placement.
5smcyBazE0.problem: Constructing sphere coverings (template banks) on curved high-dimensional parameter manifolds is computationally expensive because distances require repeated position-dependent metric evaluations.
5smcyBazE0.method: isobank trains a normalizing flow with a multi-scale loss so Euclidean distances in latent space approximate proper metric distances in physical parameter space. Template placement then runs stochastic rejection sampling using fast Euclidean distance checks in latent space before inverting templates back to physical parameters.
5smcyBazE0.key_idea: Learns an approximately isometric normalizing-flow coordinate map so curved-manifold sphere covering can use Euclidean distance checks in latent space.
5smcyBazE0.evidence: Gravitational-wave template bank experiments in 3D and 5D eccentric aligned-spin binary parameter spaces audited with exact waveform match on independent injections against mbank.
5smcyBazE0.claimed_gains: On a 5D eccentric binary space, isobank reaches 96.6% coverage at maximum mismatch mu = 0.03 with 23% fewer templates than mbank (94.2% coverage), taking ~2.5 h to train and under 1 h to place on 32 CPU cores.
5smcyBazE0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree learning an invertible approximately isometric map for template bank construction is intuitive, well motivated, and audited rigorously using exact waveform matches.
5smcyBazE0.main_concern: Reviewers note missing ablations for the four-term multi-scale loss, no comparisons to metric-preserving autoencoders, and an unmatched operating-radius comparison against default mbank settings.

IXnpSW8g3v.one_liner: Trains an RL Feedback-Agent to rewrite executable training harnesses using post-update transfer rewards on fixed reference harnesses.
IXnpSW8g3v.problem: Execution harnesses that boost immediate agent success during post-training can yield weaker models once deployed under different or minimal harnesses, a failure called harness rank reversal.
IXnpSW8g3v.method: TAME trains a Feedback-Agent language model with token-level PPO to write persistent, executable revisions to the training harness before each fixed-budget Task-Specific Agent training stage. Revisions are rewarded by post-update performance changes measured on independently fixed reference harnesses.
IXnpSW8g3v.key_idea: Apply token-level PPO over complete revision-and-training trajectories to optimize persistent training-harness code using downstream performance on held-out reference harnesses.
IXnpSW8g3v.evidence: Evaluated with crossed training- and deployment-harness protocols across three task models and four domains (including ALFWorld and Telecom as noted in reviews).
IXnpSW8g3v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that isolating learned model capability from runtime harness assistance via crossed-harness evaluation is a valuable, carefully controlled formulation.
IXnpSW8g3v.main_concern: Reviewers note heterogeneous gains (underperforming fixed baselines on Telecom), high computational overhead, and underspecified held-out harness and task-partition details.

QHZe9UAJVp.one_liner: Learns per-layer task-vector merging coefficients for frozen text-to-image specialists via multi-objective DPO and SFT.
QHZe9UAJVp.problem: Existing text-to-image model merging relies on static, global heuristics that ignore layer-specific roles and fail to balance multiple generative objectives.
QHZe9UAJVp.method: LEMMA keeps base and specialist diffusion checkpoints frozen and optimizes a small matrix of layer-tailored merging coefficients over specialist task vectors directly on target multi-objective DPO or SFT losses, then folds them into one checkpoint.
QHZe9UAJVp.key_idea: Optimize per-layer, per-specialist task-vector weights with frozen backbones directly under multi-objective DPO or SFT losses with zero added inference cost.
QHZe9UAJVp.evidence: Evaluated on SDXL and SD3 across multi-objective reward merging (DPO) and style merging (SFT), including unobserved evaluation metrics and a human rater study.
QHZe9UAJVp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, parameter-efficient, practical to deploy as a single checkpoint with no inference overhead, and applicable to both DPO and SFT.
QHZe9UAJVp.main_concern: Reviewers criticize limited novelty over AdaMerging and ZipLoRA, missing learnable-merging and multi-objective specialist baselines, and unfair comparisons against training-free heuristics.

CgLTapI6Mr.one_liner: Constructs 1,000 verifiable desktop tasks across 33 real apps using native state verifiers and execution-grounded verifier refinement.
CgLTapI6Mr.problem: Computer-use agent evaluation lacks scalable, machine-checkable tasks over real desktop applications whose fine-grained state is poorly judged by screenshots or LLM judges.
CgLTapI6Mr.method: OpenComputer combines app-specific state verifiers over native inspection endpoints, a self-evolving verification layer refined via execution feedback, an automated task-generation pipeline, and an evaluation harness that records trajectories and partial-credit rewards.
CgLTapI6Mr.key_idea: Ground automated desktop task synthesis and partial-credit verification directly in native application-state inspection endpoints refined with execution feedback.
CgLTapI6Mr.evidence: Covers 33 real desktop applications (including Blender, darktable, MuseScore, Zotero) and 1,000 tasks, with a 120-task human audit and comparisons against LLM-as-judge and OSWorld-Verified.
CgLTapI6Mr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that building state-grounded verifiers and automated task generation across 33 real desktop applications provides practical infrastructure value.
CgLTapI6Mr.main_concern: Reviewers flag underspecified agent evaluation protocols, thin benchmark validation (only 120 audited tasks with unclear annotator details), and limited analysis of task distribution and incremental coverage.

8FnPDWugkh.one_liner: Benchmarks autonomous agents building executable low-order stochastic ENSO climate models from real observations under hidden evaluation.
8FnPDWugkh.problem: Open-ended scientific agent benchmarks typically grade against known answers, rubrics, or LLM reviewers rather than testing whether a newly constructed scientific model is valid.
8FnPDWugkh.method: SciExam for ENSO gives agents a six-hour budget to process real climate observations, write frozen self-diagnostics, and build low-order stochastic ENSO models that hidden graders test on statistics, unobserved variable recovery, and held-out forecasting.
8FnPDWugkh.key_idea: Evaluate autonomous scientific modeling by grading agent-built executable dynamical models on hidden long-run statistics, conditional reconstruction, and held-out forecasts.
8FnPDWugkh.evidence: Evaluated twelve agent systems (up to three runs each) and automated empirical baselines on real ENSO observations.
8FnPDWugkh.claimed_gains: Nine of twelve agent systems outperform the published model in at least one run and two do so in every run; these two score 0.53 to 0.74 on statistics versus at most 0.49 for automated baselines reaching ENSO asymmetry.
8FnPDWugkh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that evaluating executable dynamical models on simulation, reconstruction, and held-out forecasting with hidden graders makes open-ended scientific modeling directly testable.
8FnPDWugkh.main_concern: Reviewers note that relying on a single well-studied five-variable ENSO task with limited independent replications restricts generalization and confounds modeling skill with literature familiarity.

1LriTZcewx.one_liner: Introduces WITNESS, a 2D ASCII puzzle suite and RL gym testing interactive discovery of held-out rules and compositions.
1LriTZcewx.problem: It is unclear what limits language models in inferring hidden environment rules through interaction and whether RL transfers to rules held out from training.
1LriTZcewx.method: WITNESS uses an agentic pipeline to generate verifiable 2D grid puzzles with ground-truth ASCII observations for WitnessGym (RL training) and WitnessBench (public validation split by new compositions vs. unseen primitives, plus private test), alongside ground-truth rule-card diagnostics.
1LriTZcewx.key_idea: Separate state perception from interactive rule discovery using generated 2D ASCII puzzles split into held-out rule compositions, unseen primitives, and rule-card controls.
1LriTZcewx.evidence: Evaluated 18 frontier proprietary and open-weight models on WitnessBench and ran RL training on WitnessGym with Qwen3.8-27B and Qwen3.5-9B.
1LriTZcewx.claimed_gains: The best of 18 models solves 24% of private test level slots; ground-truth rules raise Opus-5 validation RHAE-L5 from 59.9 to 97.8 (versus +2.1 for a 27B model), and RL raises the 27B model's private test RHAE-L5 from 2.1 to 5.4.
1LriTZcewx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree WITNESS provides a clean, controlled diagnostic environment separating state interpretation from rule acquisition and testing both compositional and unseen-primitive generalization.
1LriTZcewx.main_concern: Reviewers note that RL gains are untested with thinking enabled, model size is confounded with model version (9B vs. 27B), and the rule-level train/test split is hard to audit.

d1iLX4RRsv.one_liner: Automatically turns multi-turn human-LLM dialogues into self-contained instructions and verifiable checklists using only open-weight models.
d1iLX4RRsv.problem: Traditional LLM benchmarks require costly expert curation, while prior automated pipelines focus on single-turn prompts and depend on proprietary model APIs.
d1iLX4RRsv.method: Conv-to-Bench runs a multi-stage open-weight pipeline that distills multi-turn human-LLM conversations and user refinements into standalone instructions paired with fine-grained requirement checklists scored by open-weight LLM judges.
d1iLX4RRsv.key_idea: Distill multi-turn user refinements from dialogue logs into standalone prompts and verifiable requirement checklists constructed and judged solely with open-weight models.
d1iLX4RRsv.evidence: Validated across an aligned 19-model roster against Arena AI human preferences and compared against Arena-Hard-Auto and pairwise judging baselines.
d1iLX4RRsv.claimed_gains: Achieves Spearman correlation 0.926-0.946 vs. 0.916 and Brier score 0.053-0.069 vs. 0.092 relative to Arena-Hard-Auto, building a 500-instruction benchmark for USD 19.05 and evaluating models for USD 1.62 each.
d1iLX4RRsv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the open-weight, low-cost pipeline addresses a practical benchmarking need and includes well-motivated ablations comparing checklist and pairwise judging.
d1iLX4RRsv.main_concern: Reviewers emphasize that validation relies on an outdated mid-2024 19-model roster excluding modern reasoning models and does not test robustness across different open-weight generator families.

w5C2BdduKt.one_liner: Predicts signed surface-normal displacements from multi-view projected image evidence and fits parametric 3D face model coefficients.
w5C2BdduKt.problem: Refining 3D face reconstructions along camera rays is viewpoint-dependent and ill-conditioned at oblique angles, while direct coefficient regression is tied to a specific face model.
w5C2BdduKt.method: The method projects reconstructed 3D face surface points into calibrated multi-view images, fuses visible appearance and viewing geometry to predict signed local normal displacements, and applies a robust parametric fit to convert displacements into face-model coefficients.
w5C2BdduKt.key_idea: Represent multi-view 3D face corrections as signed local surface-normal displacements decoupled from camera rays and parametric model coefficients before robust fitting.
w5C2BdduKt.evidence: Evaluated on held-out FaceScape identities across single-view, five-view, and oblique-angle settings, comparing against ray-space targets and direct coefficient regression.
w5C2BdduKt.claimed_gains: Achieves residual correlation of 0.52 (one view) and 0.74 (five views) versus 0.39 for ray projection and 0.48 for ray intersection, reducing five-view symmetric Chamfer error by 4.5% from a strong start and 8.5% from an image-predicted start.
w5C2BdduKt.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that expressing corrections along surface normals is geometrically well-justified and validated by clean matched-target comparisons.
w5C2BdduKt.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior surface-aligned multi-view refinement methods, lack of evaluation under uncalibrated cameras or poor initial meshes, and unclear advantage over single-stage alternatives.

xtBEFnwHGc.one_liner: Extends HouseDiffusion with multi-constraint conditioning and redundant-corner polygon augmentation for vector floorplan generation.
xtBEFnwHGc.problem: Existing vector floorplan diffusion models handle few architectural constraints and assume room corner counts are known at inference time.
xtBEFnwHGc.method: HouseDiffusion++ adds conditioning modules to HouseDiffusion for joint control over room adjacency graphs, outer boundaries, room sizes, windows, and entrance doors, and introduces a polygon augmentation strategy with redundant points to bridge the training-inference corner-count mismatch.
xtBEFnwHGc.key_idea: Augment vector room polygons with redundant collinear points during training while adding modular multi-constraint conditioning to vector floorplan diffusion.
xtBEFnwHGc.evidence: Evaluated quantitatively and qualitatively on the RPLAN floorplan dataset.
xtBEFnwHGc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the multi-constrained editable vector floorplan generation setting practical and the modular plug-and-play presentation clear.
xtBEFnwHGc.main_concern: Reviewers flag unfair comparisons giving HouseDiffusion++ extra conditioning inputs over baselines, reliance on a single non-diverse dataset (RPLAN), and a heuristic corner-augmentation fix.

5ePXVciBEM.one_liner: Commits to per-step action transactions with masked untrusted GUI regions and isolated query models to secure computer-use agents.
5ePXVciBEM.problem: Untrusted GUI content can inject instructions or misleading visual cues that hijack a computer-use agent's decisions or redirect its clicks to unintended targets.
5ePXVciBEM.method: Secure-CUA formalizes generation and grounding integrity and executes each step as an explicit action transaction committed before viewing untrusted content. It masks untrusted screen regions, answers bounded queries via an isolated query model, and grounds GUI commands on the masked interface.
5ePXVciBEM.key_idea: Commit to a per-step action transaction before reading untrusted GUI regions, isolating untrusted queries in a separate model and grounding clicks on masked screenshots.
5ePXVciBEM.evidence: Formalized via an ideal execution model and evaluated empirically against Vanilla and CaMeL-CUA baselines on benign tasks.
5ePXVciBEM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating security into action-generation integrity and visual-grounding integrity is a useful and practical system insight.
5ePXVciBEM.main_concern: Reviewers criticize that all experiments are benign without adversarial evaluation of the 'secure by design' claim, and question how the new integrity terms add to classical CFI/DFI guarantees.

AwPclR0QPz.one_liner: Benchmarks multilingual LLM confidence estimation across 17 models and introduces translation-based multilingual consistency (Rosetta).
AwPclR0QPz.problem: Consistency-based confidence estimation has mostly been evaluated on English prompts with small models, obscuring non-English degradation and frontier-model behavior.
AwPclR0QPz.method: The authors evaluate self-consistency and verbalized confidence across nine languages and 17 open-source and frontier models, and propose Rosetta, which translates questions into multiple languages and measures agreement between multilingual samples and the original answer without labeled calibration data.
AwPclR0QPz.key_idea: Use cross-lingual translation as a perturbation operator and compute agreement between translated-prompt samples and the original answer to estimate black-box confidence.
AwPclR0QPz.evidence: Evaluated across nine languages and 17 small-to-frontier models using AUROC, Brier Score, and ECE on benchmarks including PolyMath and MMLU-ProX.
AwPclR0QPz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad 17-model, nine-language evaluation, the finding that frontier verbalized confidence can beat self-consistency, and Rosetta's simple multilingual calibration gains.
AwPclR0QPz.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty in translation-based perturbation, lack of explanation for why it helps or when its extra call cost is worthwhile over verbalized confidence, and omission of CoT settings.
